customBoxes.content:
[[No Ability]]
Placed when: After the Truelove invites the Storyteller.
Placed where: Beside the Truelove's character token once they have invited the Storyteller, whether or not the Truelove was drunk or poisoned or the ability resolved normally.
Removed when: When the Truelove dies or leaves play.

characters.name: Ronin
characters.ability: Once per game, at night*, choose a player: if the Demon attacks them tonight, an evil player is attacked instead. You regain your ability.
characters.lede: The Ronin turns the Demon's attack back upon the evil team.
characters.quote: Child, do not be afraid. Close your eyes. Feel the flow of killing intent with your heart.
summaryBullets: Attack: when a player with a Demon ability, or the Storyteller, selects a player with the Demon's killing ability. Attacks usually kill an alive player; sometimes they don't, such as attacking a player who cannot die or a dead player.
The Ronin's ability changes the Demon's attack target; it is not death immunity. The protected player is not attacked by the Demon tonight and never enters the "about to die" state.

If the Ronin's ability triggers, you should choose a living evil player to be attacked instead. Try not to choose a dead evil player (the ability text doesn't say the substitute must be alive, but the Ronin's trigger is hard to land—don't deliberately deny them their earned reward). If every evil player except the Demon is dead, you should have the Demon be attacked.
If the Ronin is drunk or poisoned, you may wake them on nights when you shouldn't, or not wake them on nights when you should, to deceive them about whether their ability triggered.

Players who cannot die (such as the Fool or players protected by the Tea Lady) can be protected by the Ronin normally. If the Ronin chooses such a player and the Demon attacks them, the Ronin's ability triggers normally.

The Ronin only changes the Demon's attack target, so the dead player still counts as killed by the Demon. This doesn't interfere with abilities that trigger on the Demon's kills, such as the Doll, Cerberus, or King Arthur.

If the Ronin chose an evil player and the Demon attacks that same evil player tonight, that evil player cannot substitute for themself. If that evil player is the only living evil player besides the Demon, it is recommended to have the Demon be attacked instead, even if this ends the game immediately.
The Ronin cannot choose Traveller players, and Travellers never substitute as attack targets (Traveller Exclusion Principle).
howToRun: Each night except the first, wake the Ronin. The Ronin either shakes their head no or points at a player. If the Ronin chooses a player, place the Ronin's "Riposte" reminder by the chosen player's character token, then place the "No Ability" reminder by the Ronin's character token. If the Demon attacks that player tonight—or, for Demons whose target is chosen by the Storyteller, the Storyteller decides to attack that player—choose an evil player to be attacked by the Demon instead: place the Demon's "Dead" reminder by that evil player, remove the Ronin's "No Ability" reminder, and declare that evil player dead at dawn.
At dawn, remove the "Riposte" reminder.
examples: On the second night, the Ronin is woken and chooses the Noble; the Demon also chooses the Noble. At dawn, the Storyteller declares that the Widow died (the Widow was attacked instead). The next night, the Ronin is woken again (their ability is regained).

On the fourth night, the only living evil player is the Demon. At night, the Ronin is woken and chooses the Fool, who still has their ability; the Demon also chooses the Fool. At dawn, the Storyteller declares that the Demon is dead and the game ends—good wins. (The Demon attacked themself.)

On the second night, the Ronin is woken and chooses the Noble; the Demon chooses the Seamstress. At dawn, the Storyteller declares that the Seamstress died. The Ronin is not woken again for the rest of the game.
tips: If you are the Ronin, work hard to read the Demon's mind—who will they choose? You only get one shot; use it on the night you think most likely to succeed.
If you are the Ronin, one successful trigger means one fewer evil player—a heavy blow to evil. Two successes leave evil with almost no chance. Three, and you will have cut down the Demon yourself.
If you are the Ronin and you've used your ability, yet you're woken again the next night, your ability succeeded last night—and whoever died last night was definitely evil.
If you are the Ronin and you used your ability last night but weren't woken tonight, your ability didn't trigger—the Demon didn't attack your protected player yesterday.
If you are the Ronin, don't rush. Once a key Townsfolk reveals their character, protect them—your odds of triggering rise sharply.
If you are the Ronin, bluffing as an important Townsfolk and then protecting yourself is also a fine strategy.
If you are the Ronin and the player you protected at night still died that night, you may be the Drunk, or drunk or poisoned—think it over.
If you are the Demon, be careful about attacking a key Townsfolk on the night they reveal—the Ronin often chooses to protect them right then.

If you are the Demon and yesterday's dead player wasn't your chosen target but your own Minion, the Ronin is likely responsible. They'll probably use their ability again tonight—avoid their protected target. Two successful Ronin triggers usually break the evil team.
bluffing: You can claim you protected an important player; this makes you look credible.
If you claim you were woken the night after using your ability, you're accusing last night's dead player of being evil. They may fight back and mark you as a bluffing evil player.
You can also claim the player you protected last night still died, pretending to be the Drunk or drunk/poisoned.
After a Minion claims to be the Goblin, have the Demon kill them at night, then claim you protected an important player—the Minion's death will look like your handiwork, winning you the town's trust.
characters.creator: Taiyi
characters.otherNightReminder: Let them choose a player and place the 'Riposte' reminder by that player.

customBoxes.title: Reminder Tokens
customBoxes.content:
[[Riposte]]
Placed when: After the Ronin acts at night and chooses a player.
Placed where: Beside the character token of the player the Ronin is protecting. Do not place it if the Ronin was drunk or poisoned at the time.
Removed when: At dawn.

[[No Ability]]
Placed when: After the Ronin chooses to use their ability at night and chooses a player.
Placed where: Beside the Ronin's character token as long as they chose a player, whether or not the Ronin was drunk or poisoned.
Removed when: When the Ronin dies or leaves play, or when the Ronin successfully makes an evil player die instead.

characters.name: Lunar Knight
characters.ability: Each night*, if nobody died by execution today, you are woken to choose a player: if they are a Minion, they die.
characters.quote: On still nights free of the smell of blood, a deer leaps across the creek, moonlight slips through the gauze window, and the tip of my spear slips through the chest of sin.
summaryBullets: "Nobody died by execution" covers three cases: (1) no execution occurred at all; (2) a dead player was executed (nobody died by execution, since death means going from alive to dead); (3) an alive player was executed but did not die (due to the Fool, Tea Lady, Psychopath, White Knight, etc.).
The Lunar Knight cannot choose Traveller players (Traveller Exclusion Principle).
howToRun: Each night except the first, if nobody died by execution today, wake the Lunar Knight and let them choose a player, then put them to sleep. If the chosen player is a Minion, mark that Minion with the "Dead" reminder.
examples: On the first day, the Psychopath is executed but does not die. That night, the Lunar Knight is woken and chooses the Psychopath; the Psychopath dies.
On the first day, the Baron dies by execution. That night, the Lunar Knight is not woken.
tips: If you are the Lunar Knight, persuade the town to execute the Tea Lady's neighbors! Executing the Fool, or executing nobody, also lets you wake. Get your ability firing as often as possible and hunt down suspected Minions!
If you are the Lunar Knight, you act very early in the night order—even before the Demon! Apart from the Narcotizer, you have little to fear!
If you are the Lunar Knight and your chosen player died, reveal yourself as the Lunar Knight promptly and claim your glory—the town will favor you as the hero who slew a Minion.

If you are the Lunar Knight and your chosen player didn't die, don't be discouraged—they aren't a Minion! Tell everyone; it's a valuable clue. If the town is sure they're evil, then since they aren't a Minion, they're very likely the Demon.

If you are the Demon, the Lunar Knight maximally threatens your Minions. Ensuring someone dies by execution every day is the best way to shut the Lunar Knight down. If several Townsfolk in play can survive execution, deciding whether to kill them or the Lunar Knight first is your problem to solve.
If you are a Minion and can't stop the Lunar Knight from acting, try not to look like a Minion! Otherwise you'll likely die miserably on the Lunar Knight's spear.
bluffing: If several players die at night, stepping forward as the Lunar Knight and claiming you killed one of them is fairly credible. But the player you accuse will almost certainly fight back, since they aren't a Minion! Be ready for that fight.

If the Demon is Cerberus, the Lunar Knight is an excellent bluff, because Cerberus itself can kill Minions and produce multiple night deaths. Claiming a dead Minion as your kill is easier to believe—they really were a Minion! And since they're your teammate, they won't react strongly and can even play along with your bluff.
If you're bluffing as the Lunar Knight, do the things a Lunar Knight would do: push to execute the Tea Lady's neighbors or the Fool, or propose executing nobody.
characters.creator: Taiyi
characters.otherNightReminder: If nobody died by execution today, let them choose a player; if they chose a Minion, mark that Minion 'Dead'.

customBoxes.title: Reminder Tokens
customBoxes.content:
[[Dead]]
Placed when: After the Lunar Knight acts at night and chooses a player.
Placed where: If the chosen player is a Minion, currently alive, can be killed by the Lunar Knight, and the Lunar Knight is sober and healthy, place it by that player's character token, reminding the Storyteller to announce the night's dead at dawn.
Removed when: After announcing the dead at dawn, at the Storyteller's convenience.

characters.name: Lady of the Lake
characters.ability: Each night*, if someone was executed today, learn if they are a Townsfolk. If alive, instead learn if both their neighbors are Townsfolk.
characters.lede: The Lady of the Lake learns whether executed players are Townsfolk.
characters.quote: The lake water is my mirror, reflecting hearts; the moonlight is my eye, beholding truth. I come from the shimmering waves to guide wandering souls. If your heart is honest, I shall grant you clear revelation; if you hide in shadow, the lake will show the ripples you cannot conceal.
summaryBullets: As long as an execution occurred during the day, the Lady of the Lake is woken that night. If no execution occurred, she is not woken.
If several players were executed today, the Lady of the Lake's ability only examines the first executed player.
If the executed player is still alive, the Lady of the Lake instead examines the two players nearest to that player on either side—she no longer examines the executed player.

If the executed player is still alive, the Lady of the Lake learns about the two players nearest to that player on either side, dead or alive—this does not skip past dead players to living ones (an ability that skips the dead would read "their living neighbors" or "the two alive players neighboring you"—note the difference).
The Lady of the Lake's ability ignores Travellers (Traveller Exclusion Principle).
Information format: "yes" or "no."
False information format: "yes" or "no," opposite to the truth.
howToRun: Each day, when the first player is executed, place the "Executed" reminder by that player.

Each night, if the "Executed" reminder is in play, wake the Lady of the Lake. If the player marked "Executed" is dead, tell the Lady of the Lake whether they are a Townsfolk. If the player marked "Executed" is alive, tell the Lady of the Lake whether the two players neighboring that player are both Townsfolk.
At dawn, remove the "Executed" reminder.
examples: On the first day, the Mutant is executed and dies. That night, the Lady of the Lake learns "no."
On the second day, the dead Mutant is executed. That night, the Lady of the Lake learns "no."
Both players neighboring the Devil's Advocate are Townsfolk. Today, the Devil's Advocate is executed but does not die. That night, the Lady of the Lake learns "yes."
No execution occurred today. That night, the Lady of the Lake is not woken.
tips: If you are the Lady of the Lake, your information is vital to the good team—survive to the mid-to-late game!
If you are the Lady of the Lake, you gain no information without executions, so push the town to execute as often as possible!

If you are the Lady of the Lake and the executed player survives, your information directly identifies whether the players beside them are Townsfolk—extremely powerful. So executing the Fool or the Tea Lady's neighbors pays off handsomely for you.
If you are the Demon, finding and killing the Lady of the Lake quickly is a priority.
If you are the Demon and can't kill her, arranging for a teammate to poison her is an excellent alternative.
bluffing: The Lady of the Lake rarely survives to the end, so if you bluff as her, you may need to explain late in the game why you haven't died.

Her information is crucial, so if you bluff as her, plan in advance what information to report and what consequences it will have. If your information accuses other players of not being Townsfolk, several players will likely stand up and attack you.
characters.creator: Taiyi
characters.otherNightReminder: If a player was executed today, wake her.

customBoxes.title: Reminder Tokens
customBoxes.content:
[[Executed]]
Placed when: Each day, when the first player is executed.
Placed where: Beside the first executed player each day.
Removed when: At dawn, or when the Lady of the Lake dies or leaves play.

characters.name: White Knight
characters.ability: Once per game, a player who is mad about wanting to survive might not die when executed.
characters.lede: The White Knight may save an executed player.
characters.quote: I sank into the muddy, barren soil, where salty tears and pained moans stretch on without end, slowly suffocating under fragile pride and tenderness. But if you are willing to call my name — even if it tears my rotting skin apart completely, even with the last breath of strength left in me — I will come and save you.
summaryBullets: The White Knight is an Outsider; in most cases his ability should be triggered to evil's benefit, though in a few cases it may favor good instead. The Storyteller must judge this carefully — how to create an interesting game is the ultimate consideration.
Try not to trigger the White Knight's ability on the game's final execution to decide the outcome directly.

If the Devil's Advocate protected a player who is also mad about wanting to survive, you should — and must — trigger the Devil's Advocate's ability first to spare that player from execution death. The White Knight's trigger condition is "about to die by execution," and since the Devil's Advocate protects the executed player from death, the Devil's Advocate's ability always takes priority in this situation.
Travellers cannot trigger the White Knight's ability (Traveller Exclusion Principle).

Jinx (White Knight & Devil's Advocate): if a player does not die by execution because of the Devil's Advocate's or the White Knight's ability, then the next day neither the White Knight's nor the Devil's Advocate's ability can affect them.
howToRun: If a player is "mad" about wanting to survive, when they are about to die by execution that day, decide whether to trigger the White Knight's ability. If you decide to trigger it, the executed player does not die. Place the "No Ability" reminder by the White Knight.
examples: While speaking on his nomination, the Mastermind is "mad" about wanting to survive; the Storyteller decides to trigger the White Knight's ability, and today the Mastermind is executed but does not die.
Today the Tea Lady is "mad" about wanting to survive, but the Storyteller decides not to trigger the White Knight's ability; today the Tea Lady is executed and dies.
tips: If you're the White Knight, persuade players about to be executed to meet death generously — if they'll listen. This avoids triggering your ability and causing chaos.
If you're the White Knight, dead means no ability. If you want to make sure your ability never matters, dying early is a good plan.

If you're the White Knight, whoever survived by your ability isn't necessarily evil — they may be a good player you all mistook for evil. The Storyteller will use this to make you even more convinced that player is evil, wasting execution after execution.
If you're an evil player, make good use of the White Knight's ability: show an overwhelming will to live at the critical moment, and let the Storyteller carry you safely through the execution.
If you're an evil player, don't pin your hopes on the White Knight on the final day — the Storyteller usually won't let his ability matter then.
bluffing: If your team has a Devil's Advocate, the White Knight may be a fine bluff — he offers another explanation for why a player protected by the Devil's Advocate didn't die.

When a player survives because of the Devil's Advocate's or the Tea Lady's ability — especially if they didn't want to be executed in the first place — you can step forward as the White Knight, making it look like they survived the execution thanks to your ability.
characters.creator: Taiyi
characters.tags: Death Modification, Madness, Once Per Game

customBoxes.title: Reminder Tokens
customBoxes.content:
[[No Ability]]
Placed when: When you decide to trigger the White Knight's ability.
Condition: When a player does not die by execution because of the White Knight's ability, place this reminder by the White Knight.
Removed when: The White Knight dies or leaves play.

jinxes.name: Devil's Advocate
jinxes.text: if a player does not die by execution because of the Devil's Advocate's or the White Knight's ability, then the next day neither the White Knight's nor the Devil's Advocate's ability can affect them.

characters.name: Dark Knight
characters.ability: Each night*, learn the Outsider who died today & guess their character: if correct, a player dies. [+1 Outsider]
characters.quote: Life is nothing but a fraud, you dead soul. I will speak your name, strip away your attachments, and take you with me to savor the exquisite taste of a living being's extinction.
summaryBullets: Whether to wake the Dark Knight is judged by whether an Outsider died during the whole of today (day + night before the Dark Knight acts). If the Dark Knight kills an Outsider, do not wake the Dark Knight again.

If multiple Outsiders died today, point to all dead Outsiders for the Dark Knight in turn. If the Dark Knight needs to guess multiple players' Outsider characters, he only needs to point to an equal number of Outsider characters — he doesn't need to match which player is which Outsider one-to-one. If the Dark Knight correctly guesses at least one Outsider character who died today, the guess succeeds. If the Dark Knight guesses more than one Outsider character correctly, still only one player dies.
After the Dark Knight guesses correctly, the Storyteller decides which player dies.
The Dark Knight does not know whether he guessed correctly.
howToRun: During initial setup, before putting character tokens into the bag, replace one Townsfolk character token with one Outsider character token.
When an Outsider dies, place the "Guess Tonight" reminder by the dead Outsider's character token.

At night, if a "Guess Tonight" reminder is on the Grimoire, wake the Dark Knight and point to each player with a "Guess Tonight" reminder in turn. Have the Dark Knight guess what Outsider characters they are; when he finishes guessing, put the Dark Knight back to sleep. If the Dark Knight correctly guessed at least one dead Outsider's character, place the "Dead" reminder by one player's character and announce that player dead after dawn. If the Dark Knight guessed all of them wrong, no further action is needed. After the Dark Knight finishes acting, remove all "Guess Tonight" reminders from the Grimoire.
examples: On the first day, the Butler dies. That night, the Dark Knight is woken and learns the Butler player (the Storyteller points to the Butler player). The Dark Knight guesses the Butler — the Fortune Teller is killed by the Dark Knight.

On the second night, the Imp attacks the Butler; the Butler dies. That night, the Dark Knight is woken and learns the Butler player (the Storyteller points to the Butler player). The Dark Knight guesses the Butler — the Saint is killed by the Dark Knight.

On the first day, the Butler dies. That night, the Imp attacks the Saint; the Saint dies. That night, the Dark Knight is woken and learns the Butler and Saint players (the Storyteller points to the Butler and Saint players). The Dark Knight guesses Butler, Saint — the Fortune Teller is killed by the Dark Knight.
tips: If you're the Dark Knight, keep a constant eye on the Outsider situation — only then can you guess correctly when an Outsider dies.
If you're the Dark Knight and you're woken and shown a player, they must be an Outsider. You can deliberately guess wrong to mislead the good team into misjudging which Minions are in play.
If you're the Dark Knight and your team needs multiple players dead, you can have the Demon attack Outsiders at night — this lets you dispose of multiple players in a single night.
If you're a good player, the Dark Knight increases the Outsider count — if there are more Outsiders than expected, the Dark Knight may be in play.
If you're an Outsider, hide your character well! Don't reveal it carelessly, or the Dark Knight will use your death to attack other players.
characters.creator: Taiyi
characters.otherNightReminder: Wake him and point to the Outsider player who died today; have him guess their Outsider character.

customBoxes.title: Reminder Tokens
customBoxes.content:
[[Guess Tonight]]
Placed when: If an Outsider died, whatever the cause of death, place it by the dead Outsider's character token.
Condition: Place it by the dead Outsider's character token regardless of whether the Dark Knight is in play, drunk, or poisoned.
Removed when: At dawn.

[[Dead]]
Placed when: After the Dark Knight acts at night and guesses a player correctly.
Condition: If the Dark Knight guessed at least one character correctly and the Dark Knight is sober and healthy, place it by any player's character token to remind the Storyteller to announce that night's dead player at dawn.
Removed when: After announcing the dead player at dawn; the Storyteller may remove it at their convenience.

characters.name: Narcotizer
characters.ability: Each night, choose a player: they are poisoned until you choose again. When they become healthy, they learn the Narcotizer is in play.
characters.quote: Darling, do you prefer lidocaine or ether? Oh... I didn't bring either — how about we make do with this hammer today? I promise it won't hurt.
summaryBullets: If a player poisoned by the Narcotizer recovers because the Narcotizer died, became drunk or poisoned, lost his ability, or left play, they do not learn that the Narcotizer is in play — because the Narcotizer's ability has already stopped working and naturally can't make a player learn it. In other words, only the Narcotizer choosing a new player makes the previously poisoned player learn the Narcotizer is in play.
If the Narcotizer chooses himself, then even if his previously chosen player is still alive, they do not learn the Narcotizer is in play — because the Narcotizer is poisoned (has no ability).
A Narcotizer who poisoned himself immediately recovers when choosing a new player, and poisons the player he chose.
The Narcotizer cannot choose Traveller players (the Traveller Exclusion Principle).
howToRun: Each night, wake the Narcotizer. He points to a player. The chosen player is poisoned — place the "Poisoned" reminder by the chosen player's character token, remove the previous "Poisoned" reminder, then put the Narcotizer back to sleep. If you removed an alive player's "Poisoned" reminder, wake that player and tell them that the Narcotizer is in play.
examples: On the first night, the Narcotizer chooses the Noble; the poisoned Noble learns false information. On the second night, the Narcotizer chooses the Fortune Teller; the Noble is still alive at this point, so the Noble learns that the Narcotizer is in play.

On the first night, the Narcotizer chooses the Noble; the poisoned Noble learns false information. On the first day, the Noble dies by execution. On the second night, the Narcotizer chooses the Fortune Teller; the poisoned Fortune Teller learns false information.

On the first night, the Narcotizer chooses the Noble; the poisoned Noble learns false information. On the second night, the Narcotizer chooses himself (here, because the Narcotizer is poisoned, the Noble does not learn the Narcotizer is in play even though he's alive). On the third night, the Narcotizer chooses the Fortune Teller (skipping the step where the Narcotizer would learn the Narcotizer is in play); the poisoned Fortune Teller gets false information.
tips: If you're the Narcotizer, choosing a new player while a player poisoned by you is still alive exposes you! That's a huge disadvantage. If you don't want to reveal the Narcotizer is in play, wait until that player dies before choosing a new one.

If you're the Narcotizer and you want to move the poison without exposing yourself, you can choose yourself, then choose a new target the next night. The downside is that on the night you choose yourself, definitely no other player is poisoned by you.

If you're a good player, don't fear the Narcotizer excessively. If nobody has learned the Narcotizer is in play, the Narcotizer's poison can only spread in a very limited way. If you believe you're poisoned by the Narcotizer, then before you die, nobody else can become poisoned by the Narcotizer — unless you learn the Narcotizer is in play, or the Narcotizer wastes a night moving the poison.

If you're a good player and you learn the Narcotizer is in play, tell everyone at dawn immediately! This is extremely important — it not only means the Narcotizer is in play, it also means you were poisoned by the Narcotizer before, and that starting last night a new player is being poisoned by the Narcotizer!
characters.creator: Taiyi
characters.firstNightReminder: Have him choose a player.
characters.otherNightReminder: Have him choose a player.

customBoxes.title: Reminder Tokens
customBoxes.content:
[[Poisoned]]
Placed when: After the Narcotizer acts at night and chooses a player.
Condition: Place it by the character token of the player the Narcotizer chose. If the Narcotizer is drunk or poisoned at this time, do not place this reminder.
Removed when: The Narcotizer's next choice, or when the Narcotizer dies or leaves play.

[[Learn]]
Placed when: When a player poisoned by the Narcotizer recovers.
Condition: A player poisoned by the Narcotizer recovers, the Narcotizer has his ability at this time, and that player is alive.
Removed when: After that player gets the information; the Storyteller may remove it at their convenience.

characters.name: Siren
characters.ability: Each night*, choose a player: they die. You may lose this ability. Townsfolk abilities yield false info.
characters.quote: Hush... listen — this gentle tide is my whisper. When my song sounds, the truths you chase are nothing but phantom lights in my stage set. If I take my bow and exit, will you wake with a start — or fall into an even deeper illusion?
summaryBullets: False information: objectively wrong, untrue information. Whether information is false is not affected by any ability.
Whenever players whose character is a Townsfolk gain information through an ability, they get false information — even if they're drunk or poisoned, the information is guaranteed false.
If the Siren is poisoned or drunk, she loses her ability — so Townsfolk aren't affected by the Siren's ability while she's poisoned or drunk.
Once the Siren takes her bow, she permanently loses her last ability.
The Siren's ability cannot choose Traveller players (the Traveller Exclusion Principle).
howToRun: Each night except the first, wake the Siren. Have her point to a player and mark that player "Dead", then have the Siren choose whether to take her bow. If the Siren nods, mark her with "Curtain Call", then put the Siren back to sleep.
Whenever a Townsfolk's ability requires you to give them information, you must give false information — until the "Curtain Call" reminder is placed in the Grimoire.
Once the Siren has taken her bow, there's no need to ask the Siren whether to take her bow on later nights.
examples: On the first night, the Noble learns three good players (false information).

On the first night, the Noble learns three good players (false information). On the second night, the Siren chooses to take her bow — from this point on, Townsfolk players' abilities no longer produce false information because of the Siren.
The Siren never takes her bow the whole game — all Townsfolk produce false information for the entire game.
tips: If you're the Siren, taking your bow at the right moment is the key to victory!
If you're the Siren, you can also never take your bow all game — the good team may mistakenly believe you've already taken your bow, leading them to misjudge some information.

If you're a good player, don't fear the Siren — the single most critical point in identifying the Siren is the first night's information! With the Siren in play, first-night information is guaranteed false!

If you're a good player, once the Siren takes her bow she permanently loses the ability to make Townsfolk produce false information. If you believe the Siren has taken her bow, treat all information as true!
characters.creator: Taiyi
characters.otherNightReminder: Have her choose a player, then she chooses whether to take her bow.

customBoxes.title: Reminder Tokens
customBoxes.content:
[[Curtain Call]]
Placed when: When the Siren chooses to "take her bow".
Condition: If the Siren chooses "Curtain Call" after being woken at night, place it by her character token.
Removed when: The Siren dies or leaves play.

[[Dead]]
Placed when: After the Siren acts at night and chooses a player.
Condition: The player the Siren chose is currently alive, can be killed by the Siren, and the Siren is not drunk or poisoned — place it by that player's character token to remind the Storyteller to announce that night's dead player at dawn.
Removed when: After announcing the dead player at dawn; the Storyteller may remove it at their convenience.

characters.name: Arthur
characters.ability: Each night*, choose a player: they die. The 1st time you would kill a Minion, 2 players die instead & you swap characters with that Minion.
characters.quote: When the Lady of the Lake handed me the sword, she hid another sentence — 'You will drown in your own glory.' Now I rise to the surface, spitting out resentment and regret, only to find I've long grown scales and claws. Fallen? This is my rebirth. Everyone who betrayed me will be hung to dry on the ruins of Camelot. I have returned, with a rusted holy sword and a heart of stone.
summaryBullets: "The first time Arthur is about to kill a Minion": the first time this game that a player whose character is Arthur or who has Arthur's ability is about to kill a Minion. It can happen at most once per game — a new Arthur who has already Castled cannot swap characters with a Minion again.

When a player who has Arthur's ability but whose character isn't Arthur swaps characters with a Minion, they swap their current character, not the Arthur character. "Arthur" in Arthur's ability means a player whose character is Arthur or who has Arthur's ability.

Any player can die in the about-to-die Minion's stead (including the original Arthur) — the Storyteller decides based on the situation, but it's not recommended to kill players who can't die (dead players, the Fool, or protected players), because good players need the multiple deaths to notice the Demon's position has changed.

When Arthur becomes a Minion, that Minion is treated as newly entering play, so they don't inherit the original Minion's choices. For example: the Devil's Advocate chose a player, then Arthur swaps characters with the Devil's Advocate — the former Devil's Advocate's ability disappears, and the new Devil's Advocate isn't woken because their action window has passed. This means no Devil's Advocate ability is in effect the next day.
If Arthur swaps characters with the Dark Knight, and an Outsider died that day before the Dark Knight is woken, still wake the new Dark Knight and have him guess.

If the Devil's Advocate is in play and Arthur swaps characters with another Minion, the Devil's Advocate may end up protecting the Demon two days in a row (the Devil's Advocate chooses the original Arthur on day one, then chooses the new post-swap Arthur on day two). If you find the evil team exploiting this strategy for consecutive protection and good has no chance of winning, you can use Arthur's ability to kill the Devil's Advocate, breaking the 2-day execution protection and giving the good team one last chance to win.
Arthur's ability cannot choose Traveller players (the Traveller Exclusion Principle).
howToRun: Each night except the first, wake Arthur. Have him point to a player. Put Arthur back to sleep. Place the "Dead" reminder by that player.

If the chosen player is a Minion, can be killed by Arthur, and this is the first time this game that Arthur is about to kill a Minion (the "Castling" reminder is not in the Grimoire), instead place "Dead" reminders by two other players — they die in that Minion's stead. Then swap that Minion's and Arthur's characters. Wake that Minion and Arthur separately and tell them what their characters changed to. Put them to sleep. Place the "Castling" reminder in the Grimoire.
examples: Arthur attacks the Baron; the Baron doesn't die — the Butler and the Poisoner die instead. The former Baron becomes the new Arthur; the former Arthur becomes the new Baron.
Arthur attacks the Poisoner; the Poisoner doesn't die — Arthur and the Butler die. The former Poisoner becomes the new Arthur; the former Arthur (now dead) becomes the new Poisoner.
The previous night, the Baron swapped characters with Arthur and became the new Arthur. Tonight, Arthur attacks the Poisoner — the Poisoner dies.
tips: If you're Arthur, swapping characters with a Minion is cool! The Demon's position changes — but the sudden multi-death night may also expose that the in-play Demon is Arthur and has relocated! So disguise the Castling as much as possible with other characters' multi-death logic!

If you're Arthur, your extra ability isn't just for swapping! It's also a great way to get extra kills and speed up the game! If only 4 players remain alive, using Castling kills 2 players and ends the game early.
If you're a good player, pay special attention when sudden extra deaths occur — Arthur has very likely Castled and slipped away!

If you're a good player, fighting Arthur may require locating every Minion, since you don't know which Minion Arthur will Castle with. But if nights never produce extra deaths, don't worry about Demon relocation — Arthur definitely hasn't Castled yet.

customBoxes.content:
[[Dead" ×2]]
Placed when: After Arthur chooses a player.
Condition: If the player Arthur chose is currently alive, can be killed by Arthur, Arthur is not drunk or poisoned, and the Castling condition isn't met — place it by that player's character token. If Castling conditions are met, instead place them by any two players' character tokens.
Removed when: After announcing the dead players at dawn; the Storyteller may remove them at their convenience.

[[Castling]]
Placed when: After Arthur swaps characters with a Minion.
Condition: After Arthur successfully swaps characters with a Minion, place this reminder in the center of the Grimoire.
Removed when: This reminder is never removed for any reason.

characters.name: Corruptus
characters.ability: Each night*, choose a player: they die, even if they cannot. Dead Outsiders share your win condition, even if you are dead. [+0–1 Outsider]
characters.quote: Embrace the darkness, outlander. I will forge your death and your wails into armor, forge the ostracism and malice you've suffered into a blade — and then you shall follow me, and take your revenge upon them.
summaryBullets: They die, even if they cannot die: the death-causing ability ignores death-preventing abilities (the Fool, the Tea Master, etc.) to cause death.

When Corruptus attacks a player protected by the Ronin, an evil player is attacked in their stead. The protected player doesn't die, and the player attacked in their stead dies — even if protected by effects like the Fool's ability. The Ronin's ability changes the Demon's attack target; it isn't death immunity, so Corruptus cannot kill the Ronin's protected target.

Attention!! Whether Corruptus adds an Outsider is decided by the Storyteller. In 9-, 12-, and 15-player games, try not to let in-play Outsiders exceed two; in games of other sizes, try not to let Outsiders exceed one. Otherwise evil vote-binding can easily occur, making it hard for the good team to win. Storytellers, treat this issue seriously — you may appropriately use other characters' Outsider-adding/removing abilities to adjust the Outsider count in play.

In games where the Demon isn't Corruptus, the evil team may try to deceive Outsiders into believing the Demon is Corruptus — you can help them in reasonable ways, such as giving the Occultist (who gets false information) the information "Corruptus is in play".
Corruptus's ability cannot choose Traveller players (the Traveller Exclusion Principle).
howToRun: During game setup, you may remove one Townsfolk character token and add one Outsider character token.

Each night except the first, wake Corruptus. Have Corruptus point to any player — that player dies: place the "Dead" reminder by that player's character token. This death ignores death-immunity effects.
As long as Corruptus is in play, even if Corruptus is dead, dead Outsiders win when Corruptus wins and lose when Corruptus loses.
examples: Corruptus wins — all dead Outsiders also win.
Corruptus loses — all dead Outsiders also lose.
Corruptus attacks the Fool — the Fool dies. Corruptus attacks the Fortune Teller protected by the Tea Master — the Fortune Teller dies.
Corruptus attacks the Fortune Teller protected by the Ronin — the Psychopath dies.
tips: If you're Corruptus, you can unscrupulously kill any player you want. But revealing Corruptus is in play early-to-mid game may not be a great choice — the good team will rule out other Demons and narrow down many possibilities.

If you're Corruptus, attack Outsiders as much as possible before the game ends! You need to inform the Outsiders somehow that the in-play Demon is Corruptus — whether by killing the Fool outright or having Minions loudly proclaim Corruptus is in play. This helps the evil team on the final day's vote.

If you're another evil character and Corruptus isn't in play, you can still deceive the Outsiders — especially already-dead ones — into believing the Demon is Corruptus. This makes them side with the evil team on the final day.

If you're an Outsider, carefully identify the in-play Demon! Whether it's Corruptus matters enormously to you. If you're still alive before the game ends, Corruptus's ability definitely can't affect you — vote for whoever you believe is the Demon with confidence! But if you're dead, be careful — if the Demon is Corruptus, you must help the evil team to achieve final victory.

customBoxes.content:
[[Dead]]
Placed when: After Corruptus chooses a player.
Condition: If the player Corruptus chose is currently alive and Corruptus is not drunk or poisoned, place it by that player's character token.

characters.name: Paperboy
characters.ability: Each day, you may visit the Storyteller for news. If you read it aloud publicly, learn tonight if it is true.
characters.lede: The Paperboy brings the town its daily news.
characters.quote: Extra! Extra! Today's headlines! Today's headlines!
summaryBullets: A "news" item is appropriately embellished information. It may be true or false, and it should have three qualities: 1) a precise subject (name characters by character name, players by player name or seat number); 2) a clear meaning (players should grasp what you're saying at a glance); 3) entertaining embellishment.
Fact: objectively correct. Anything not objectively correct is not fact.
If a new evil player bluffing as the Paperboy comes to you for a private chat, give them some help or suggestions so they can craft their own "news" convincingly.

Whether a "news" item is true is decided at the moment the Storyteller gives it. For example, if the Paperboy gets "No dead player is evil" during the day and the Storyteller marks it as true, then even if an evil player dies that night, the Storyteller still tells the Paperboy "yes" (meaning what he received during the day was fact).

Note: a lone piece of news is not "information" (the ability deliberately says "get" rather than "learn"), so news is not forced false by the Vortox or Vortox-like abilities. The Paperboy's complete information is "day + night"; Vortox-like abilities can affect what the Paperboy learns at night.

Example "news" items: "The biggest Demon in history, the Imp, graces our town" (the Imp is in play); "The Demon received a new Doll last night" (the Demon created a new Doll last night); "Shocking! Best friends Duckie and Lemon are secretly on different teams!" (Duckie and Lemon are on different teams); "The Scarlet Woman and the Baron were spotted in town at the same time" (both are in play); "Horrifying! The town Drunk was found dead at home" (the Drunk is dead); "What a refined scoundrel! The Demon wears glasses!" (the Demon player wears glasses); "The Cannibal has joined the Devil's party" (the Cannibal has turned evil).
Information format: a lone "news" item is not information. The night information format is "yes" or "no."
False information format: "news" has no false format. The night information's false format is the opposite result — "yes" becomes "no," and "no" becomes "yes."
howToRun: Once per day, if the Paperboy asks for a private chat with you, leave the circle of players together so your conversation cannot be overheard. Then give the Paperboy one piece of "news" — by whispering, writing it down, or typing it on a screen.

If the Paperboy publicly read aloud the "news" you gave him today, place the "True News" reminder by his character token if the news was objectively true, or the "False News" reminder if it was not. Each night, if the "True News" reminder is by the Paperboy's character token, wake him and tell him "yes"; if the "False News" reminder is there, wake him and tell him "no". If no reminder is by his token, do not wake him.
At dawn, remove all "True News" and "False News" reminders.
examples: On the first day, the Paperboy visits the Storyteller and gets the news *"Shocking! Best friends Duckie and Lemon are secretly on different teams!"* He reads it aloud publicly. That night, he is woken and learns "yes."

On the first day, the Paperboy visits the Storyteller and gets the news *"The Scarlet Woman and the Baron were spotted in town at the same time."* He does not read it aloud that day. That night, he is not woken.
tips: If you are the Paperboy, you can publicly read several news items each day (both the one you really received and ones you fabricate), so the Demon can't tell what information you're about to confirm — this muddies their decision about whether to kill you.

If you aren't the Paperboy — say you're the Sage or the Ronin — you can also read news aloud during the day to cover for the real Paperboy. If the Demon mistakes you for the Paperboy and kills you, your own character ability comes into play.

If you are the Demon, generally a player who read no news today definitely isn't the Paperboy, but a player who did read news isn't necessarily the Paperboy either. Decide whether to attack the Paperboy based on how important the "news" is.
bluffing: From day one, diligently read news aloud in public, playing the hardworking Paperboy. Keep your news low-stakes so it looks unimportant — that explains why you never die at night.
Follow the example news items as closely as you can; avoid fabricating anything too outlandish, or other players will spot your lie instantly.
If your Paperboy bluff fails, you can pivot to claiming the Sage, the Ronin, the Silversmith, or the Aerialist, explaining that your bluff was meant to help the good team confuse the Demon.

characters.name: Tuner
characters.ability: On your 1st night, you learn an Outsider character and a Minion character. Exactly one of them is in play.
characters.lede: The Tuner learns information about Outsider and Minion characters.
characters.quote: In the dissonant chord there is a whiff of Minion... and that sudden microtone is plainly the panicked heartbeat of an Outsider.
summaryBullets: Information format: "one Outsider character + one Minion character" (e.g., the Baron and the Drunk).
False information format: "one Outsider character + one Minion character," but the two characters must satisfy the condition that both are in play or neither is in play.
howToRun: While preparing for the first night, decide which Outsider character and which Minion character to give the Tuner; these two characters must satisfy the condition that one is in play and the other is not.
On the first night, wake the Tuner. Show them the prepared Outsider character token and Minion character token.
examples: On the first night, the Tuner learns the Drunk and the Baron. This game, the Drunk is in play and the Baron is not.
On the first night, the Tuner learns the Cannibal and the Scarlet Woman. This game, the Cannibal is not in play and the Scarlet Woman is.
On the first night, the Tuner learns the Cannibal and the Goblin. The Vortox is in play. This game, neither the Cannibal nor the Goblin is in play (false information).
On the first night, the Tuner learns the Drunk and the Baron. The Vortox is in play. This game, both the Drunk and the Baron are in play (false information).
tips: You can reveal your character and information as soon as possible, giving everyone a basic understanding of the game's situation.

You can also hide your character and reveal it later, once the game has developed. First, this may make the Demon think you're a more important Townsfolk and kill you at night, when in fact you already have the information you needed — letting more important Townsfolk survive more days. Second, the evil team won't know what you learned and may misread the situation (for example, your information may clearly imply the Baron is not in play while evil is bluffing multiple Outsiders).
The Vortox corrupts your information. If you can confirm the Demon in play is the Vortox, then of the two characters in your information, either both are in play or neither is.
bluffing: Reveal your character and information early so everyone believes you as much as possible.
Keep the Tuner as a backup bluff: when your first bluff is exposed, you can say you're actually the Tuner and only pretended to be a more important Townsfolk to confuse the Demon.

If the Baron is not in play, you can report a Minion other than the Baron plus an Outsider who is obviously in play (such as the Snitch — Minions will know whether a Snitch is in play). This helps evil fake a Baron game.
Or, if you want to fake the presence of some other Minion, report information containing that Minion plus an Outsider who is obviously not in play.

Whatever information you report, remember the Tuner's information is corrupted by the Vortox. If everyone confirms the Demon in play is the Vortox and your information can't be explained, you may well be executed.
characters.creator: Taiyi
characters.firstNightReminder: Tell him one Minion character and one Outsider character.

characters.name: Perfumer
characters.ability: Once per game, at night, you may choose a player or an evil character: they learn the Perfumer is in play.
characters.lede: The Perfumer proves herself or attacks other players through different means.
characters.quote: Tonight I've prepared two perfumes: one frank as a love letter, the other... (suddenly leaning close) like a rose on a bear trap. Darling, guess which one you're smelling?
summaryBullets: If the Perfumer chooses a character not in play, nobody learns the Perfumer is in play, and the Perfumer still loses her ability.
If the Perfumer chooses the Doll and the Doll is in play, let the Doll player learn the Perfumer is in play, but do not reveal in any way that they are the Doll.
A good Doll is still an evil character; if the Perfumer chooses the Doll, the Storyteller may choose to let a good Doll learn the Perfumer is in play.
If several players are the character the Perfumer chose, the Storyteller chooses one of them to learn the Perfumer is in play.
The Perfumer cannot choose Traveller players (Traveller Exclusion Principle).
Information format: "The Perfumer is in play," or show the woken player the Perfumer character token.

False information format: this character has no false information format (per the official "general simplification principle"). The Vortox and similar characters do not affect the Perfumer's ability, whether she chooses a player or a character.
howToRun: Each night, wake the Perfumer. If she shakes her head to decline her ability, put her back to sleep. If she points at a player or an evil character, put her back to sleep, then wake the chosen player, or the player of the chosen character, and show them the "This character's ability affected you" reminder token and the Perfumer's character token, then put that player back to sleep. Place the "No Ability" reminder by the Perfumer's character token. Do not wake the Perfumer on later nights.

If the Perfumer was drunk or poisoned when choosing, after putting her back to sleep, do not wake her chosen player — but still mark the Perfumer with "No Ability," because she used her once-per-game ability.
examples: On the first night, the Perfumer chooses player #1; player #1 learns that the Perfumer is in play.
On the first night, the Perfumer chooses the Goblin; the Goblin is player #1, so player #1 learns that the Perfumer is in play.
On the first night, the Perfumer chooses the Goblin; the Goblin is not in play, so nobody learns that the Perfumer is in play.
tips: Don't seek out the player you chose; wait for them to announce that the Perfumer is in play. When an evil player learns the Perfumer is in play, they can't tell whether you chose a player or an evil character — so they generally don't dare announce it themselves (a guilty conscience). If you go to them first, they can be almost certain you chose a player, and can then claim to have learned the Perfumer is in play with no risk.
Use your ability on a player you trust. After they announce the Perfumer is in play, they can corroborate that you truly are the Perfumer.
Use your ability on a player you don't trust. If they keep quiet about the Perfumer being in play for a long time, they're very likely an evil player with a guilty conscience.
Choose an evil character and wait for the fish to bite. If a player claims they learned the Perfumer is in play, you can be almost certain they are the evil character you chose.
bluffing: If you're a Minion who doesn't much fear death, like the Baron or the Goblin, you can claim you chose a player who then denied learning the Perfumer is in play — painting them as a guilty evil player and steering the town to execute them.
You can double-act with an evil teammate: one of you claims to be the Perfumer, the other claims to have learned the Perfumer is in play, mutually confirming you're both good.

If you have a Goblin teammate, have them first claim to have learned the Perfumer is in play; then you say you're the Perfumer and you chose a Demon or the Scarlet Woman, staging a "successful fishing trip." This steers the town into executing the Goblin — and even if the Goblin publicly claims to be the Goblin, everyone will think they're just a non-Goblin making a last-ditch struggle.
characters.creator: Taiyi
characters.firstNightReminder: Let her choose a player or a character.
characters.otherNightReminder: Let her choose a player or a character.

customBoxes.title: Reminder Tokens
customBoxes.content:
[[No Ability]]
Placed when: After the Perfumer chooses to use her ability at night and chooses a player or a character.
Condition: As long as the Perfumer chose a player or an evil character, this token is placed by her character token whether or not she was drunk or poisoned.
Removed when: The Perfumer dies or leaves play.

characters.name: Doll
characters.ability: You think you are good, but you are not. If the Demon kills you, they choose a player: they become the Doll. [The Doll neighbors the Demon]
characters.quote: They say I'm a good kid... but I keep hearing the stitches split. That string of numbers on the tag on my back... is it counting down? My lord, you need a new friend, don't you? This time I'll lie down in the coffin obediently...
summaryBullets: The original Doll is on the evil team. But the Doll registers to herself as the good team and a good character. Therefore, no matter how the Doll player asks you, you must not reveal her true character or true team (the evil Doll). You must reasonably deceive her into believing she is the good character she learned.

The Demon does not learn who the Doll is. Through the Demon info (the first-night evil team introduction), the Demon learns which players are Minions — this includes the Doll, but the Demon can't tell whether one of them is the Doll (the Doll always neighbors the Demon; when the Demon learns a Minion neighbors him, he can anticipate that this Minion is the Doll).

Other Minions learn normally through the Minion info (the first-night evil team introduction) who the Demon is and who the Minions are (including the Doll), but do not learn the specific characters of the Demon and Minions.
The Doll thinks she's a good character, so she is not shown the Minion info on the first night (the first-night evil team introduction) — she does not learn who the Minions or the Demon are.

The Doll may think she's a Townsfolk, or may think she's an Outsider (except the Drunk — misregistration does not nest). If the Doll thinks she's an Outsider, the actual number of Outsiders in play is one fewer than there should be. For example, in a 12-player 7-2-2-1 setup (7 Townsfolk, 2 Outsiders, 2 Minions, 1 Demon), there should be 2 Outsiders, but one of them is marked as the Doll by the Storyteller at game start — so only one Outsider actually exists in play.
The Demon chooses a new Doll at night, immediately after killing the Doll. If some Demon kills the Doll during the day, have the Demon choose at the earliest opportunity after nightfall.
When creating a new Doll, the Demon doesn't need to follow the requirement that "the Doll sits next to the Demon" — because the [ ] ability applies to the setup phase before the game begins.

A player turned into the Doll generally doesn't learn their character changed — they still think they're their original character, but they've actually lost their original ability. From the moment they become the Doll, they may get false information (or correct information) and no longer have their original ability.
If a good player is turned into the Doll, they become a good Doll (only the character changes, not the team) — they still belong to the good team and do not become an evil player because of it.

The Doll is a Minion, not a Townsfolk — so if a Doll thinks she's a Townsfolk character and a character like the Vortox that only affects Townsfolk is in play, the information she gets may be correct or incorrect — not necessarily false (because such abilities only affect Townsfolk). Note: neither the original Doll nor a Townsfolk turned into the Doll is affected by the abilities of characters like the Vortox.
The original Doll is treated as the evil team and a Minion character by other characters' abilities (she already is evil and a Minion).

When the Imp kills itself, the Storyteller may choose the Doll to become the new Imp, but this doesn't change the Doll's original team. An evil Doll becomes an evil Imp; a good Doll becomes a good Imp. It's not recommended to turn a good Doll into the Imp while other evil Minions are still alive.
Each night, the Demon can only create one new Doll.
The Demon cannot use the Doll's ability to choose Traveller players (the Traveller Exclusion Principle).

Jinx (Doll & Snitch): The Doll does not learn three not-in-play characters; instead, the Demon additionally learns three not-in-play characters (these may be the same as the Demon's bluffs). Non-original Dolls do not interact with the Snitch's ability.
howToRun: During game setup, before putting character tokens into the bag, remove the Doll's character token and add one Townsfolk character token. After all players have learned their characters, choose a non-Minion player neighboring the Demon (in games of 12 or more players, if the players on both sides of the Demon happen to be Minions, the simplest fix is recommended: find an excuse to redeal the characters) and place the "Original Doll" reminder by their character token.

Run the Doll as if she were the character she thinks she is. She is woken at the times of the good character she thinks she is, may get false information, is not woken during the first-night Minion info, and so on.

If the Demon kills the Doll at night, show him the Doll's character token and "This character's ability applies to you", then have the Demon choose a player. Place a "New Doll" reminder by that player — they have now become the Doll. (Generally, they still think they're their original character, so there's no need to wake them to announce the character change. See Rule Details.) If some Demon kills the Doll during the day, do this at the earliest opportunity after nightfall.
examples: The Doll thinks she's the Slayer and publicly chooses the Demon during the day. Nothing happens, because the Doll is not really the Slayer.

The Demon kills the Doll at night and chooses the Fortune Teller; the Fortune Teller becomes the new Doll (good). But the Fortune Teller doesn't notice and still thinks she's the Fortune Teller, because the Doll thinks she's a good character.
The Demon deceives the Fortune Teller sitting next to him, saying she is the Doll, an evil Minion; the Fortune Teller believes it and helps the Demon win. But the Fortune Teller is not the Doll.

On the second night, the Demon kills the original Doll (evil) and chooses the Fortune Teller; the Fortune Teller becomes the Doll (good) without knowing it. On the third night, the Demon kills the former Fortune Teller (now the good Doll) and chooses the Oracle; the Oracle becomes the Doll (good) without knowing it. On the fourth night, the Demon kills the former Oracle (now the good Doll) and chooses the Noble; the Noble becomes the Doll (good) without knowing it.
tips: If you're the original Doll, that means the Demon must be right next to you.

If you can be sure neither player beside you is the Demon, you can almost conclude that the player telling you you're the Doll is deceiving you — expose them; or you may have already been chosen by the Demon as the new Doll — judge carefully!

As the original Doll, you are essentially an evil Drunk — not only do you lack the ability you think you have, you're not even the team you think you are! The good news is that many tricks you'd use to detect being the Drunk also work for detecting the Doll. If your information doesn't add up, or your ability fails when it should have worked, you may be the Doll rather than a good player!

If a player next to you claims you're the Doll and then you die at night, the Demon is likely using your ability to make a new Doll. This isn't certain, of course — stay vigilant and use information to judge whether you're really the original Doll.
The number of Minions is fixed — a 12-player game has only 2 Minions. If you find both the Baron and the Goblin in play, you can hardly be the Doll.

If you're sure you're not the Doll but someone tells you you are, tell the group. The group will likely execute one of your neighbors — meaning either a Demon dies, a Minion dies, a good player who bluffed pointlessly dies, or at worst a mischievous good player dies.

You're good, but a neighbor doesn't quite trust you. Deceive them into thinking they're the Doll! For a while at least, most players will cooperate with you and try to figure out their own character. Just make sure they understand before the game ends that they must work with you to win.

Should I deceive other players into thinking they're the Doll? Any player can deceive others into thinking they're the Doll. If you're a Minion hoping to trick more good players into serving evil, you can tell a neighboring player that you're the Demon and they're the Doll.

If you're the Demon, nothing stops you from telling your neighboring good players they're the Doll. In fact, you can tell both of them, making each believe she's the "real" Doll and the other one is just deceived!

What does finding the Doll bring the good team? If you find an original Doll, the Demon must be among her neighbors! If you find a suspected new Doll created by the Demon, then a Doll must have been killed by the Demon on some earlier night. If only one player has died at night so far, that player was the original Doll — and the Demon must be beside them!

The Demon can only create one new Doll per night, and creating a new Doll requires killing all old Dolls — remember this. If you suspect multiple Dolls exist, the Doll chain can be traced — try to unravel the chain and find the Demon behind it.
If you think a player may have been turned into the Doll, they no longer have their ability — their ability and information are no longer trustworthy.

characters.name: Martyra
characters.ability: If a Minion dies by execution, you die that night, and all evil characters are drunk until dusk tomorrow.
characters.lede: The Martyra dies on the night a Minion is executed.
characters.quote: The olive branch at my throat is Apollo's shackle, and a faint light in the sea mist. When my dagger opens my throat, lies will scatter with the bloody haze. Remember: my death is not the end, but the dawn in which you stare into the truth.
summaryBullets: The Martyra's ability to make all evil characters drunk works only if the Martyra dies from her own ability. If she should die from her own ability but doesn't for some reason, or dies from another cause, she does not make evil characters drunk.
If the Bard publicly chooses the Martyra, the Martyra immediately becomes drunk. So even if a Minion dies by execution that day, the Martyra will not die from her own ability that night.
howToRun: If a Minion player dies by execution, place the "Martyrdom" reminder by the Martyra. When the Martyra acts at night, if the "Martyrdom" reminder is in play, place the "Dead" reminder by the Martyra's character token, and from this moment all evil characters are drunk until the next dusk. If the "Martyrdom" reminder is in play but the Martyra does not die for some reason, remove the "Martyrdom" reminder.
At dusk the next day, all players made drunk by the Martyra sober up — remove the "Martyrdom" reminder.
examples: The Mastermind dies by execution; the Martyra dies at night from her own ability. That night the Vortox chooses the Seamstress, but the Seamstress does not die and gets correct information, because the Demon is drunk. At dawn, the Storyteller announces the Martyra died.
The Vortox is in play. A Townsfolk dies by execution; that night the Martyra is killed by the Vortox, and the Seamstress gets false information.

A Minion dies by execution; that night the Innkeeper protects the Martyra, and she does not die. Because the Martyra did not successfully die, the Demon's and Minions' abilities all function normally that night.
tips: If you didn't die at night, the player executed that day was not a Minion.

If you died at night — especially if you were the only one to die — analyze carefully whether you died from your own ability or another cause. If you died from your own ability, the Townsfolk's information that night is highly credible, since Minion and Demon interference is ruled out.
If you're still alive in the mid-to-late game, be wary: either all Minions are still alive, or you were poisoned or drunk at some point.
bluffing: The Martyra is a fairly hard character to bluff. If you don't die at night, it's very hard to explain why.
characters.creator: Taiyi
characters.otherNightReminder: If the 'Martyrdom' token is in play, she dies.

customBoxes.title: Reminder Tokens
customBoxes.content:
[[Dead]]
Placed when: When the Martyra acts at night.
Condition: The "Martyrdom" reminder is by the Martyra's character token, and the Martyra is not poisoned or drunk, and the Martyra can die.
Removed when: The Martyra leaves play.

[[Martyrdom]]
Placed when: When a Minion dies by execution.
Condition: When a Minion dies by execution and the Martyra is not drunk or poisoned at that time; place it by the Martyra's character token.
Removed when: At dusk the day after this token was placed, or when the Martyra leaves play.

characters.name: Yeti
characters.ability: Once per game, the Demon may publicly guess you are the Yeti: if right, you replace their execution. If no-one is executed, your team loses.
characters.lede: If the Demon finds the Yeti, the Yeti is executed in the Demon's place.
characters.quote: The wind will sweep away my tracks; every flake of new snow is a seal.
summaryBullets: If several Yetis (or players with the Yeti ability) are in play, the Demon still gets only one guess, and the Demon's guess consumes the guess for all Yetis.
If several Yetis (or players with the Yeti ability) are in play, guessing any one Yeti correctly counts as correct, and if the Demon is executed that day, the Yeti they guessed is executed instead.
The Yeti loses his ability upon death — all of his abilities stop working.
However many Demons there are, they share a single guess. If a Demon has guessed and was wrong, no later guess has any effect.
howToRun: Each dusk, if no player was executed today, the game ends and the Yeti's team loses.

At any time during the game, if a Demon publicly guesses who the Yeti is and guesses wrong, mark all Yetis with "Guessed" — no later guesses have any effect. At any time during the game, if a Demon publicly guesses who the Yeti is and guesses correctly (and the "Guessed" reminder hasn't been placed), mark the guessed Yeti with "Guessed Right"; that day, if the guessing Demon is executed, the Yeti marked "Guessed Right" is executed instead of them.
examples: On the first day nobody is executed; the good team loses.
Today the Demon is about to be executed; the Demon guesses the Yeti player is the Yeti; when the Demon is executed, the Yeti player is executed instead and dies.

Yesterday the Demon died by execution, and with the Mastermind in play the game entered Mastermind Day. Today the Demon is about to be executed; the Demon guesses the Yeti player is the Yeti; the Yeti is executed instead, and evil wins.

Today the Demon is about to be executed; the Demon guesses the Yeti player is the Yeti; another player then makes a new nomination, and today a dead player is executed. The next day, the Demon is executed and dies. Good wins.
tips: If you're the Yeti and you're not confident the Demon won't recognize you, it's best to get yourself killed earlier in the game — avoiding a catastrophic negative effect on the final day.

If you're the Yeti, swap claimed characters with a player you trust to waste the Demon's only guess. Of course, this only works if your swap partner is good — if they're evil, you've practically exposed yourself to the Demon.
If you're the Demon, finding the Yeti buys you one more day of life.
If you're the Demon and you think the Yeti is already dead, when you're about to be executed, just guess randomly — maybe you'll actually hit it.
bluffing: The Yeti isn't a great Demon bluff, since generally only evil wants the Yeti alive at the end.

If you're a Minion, stepping forward as the Yeti in the mid-to-late game can be a good choice. If the Yeti is really in play, you can force them out; if not, you can steer everyone into executing you to help the Demon survive to the end.

[[Guessed]]

Removed when: The Yeti dies or leaves play.

[[Guessed Right]]
