Removed when: The Yeti dies or leaves play.

customBoxes.title: Design Notes
customBoxes.content: An Outsider custom-made for One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest Ⅱ, forming the core Mastermind–Yeti component.

characters.name: Wolfboy
characters.ability: When all other Wolfboys are dead, you become an evil Minion that is not in play. [There may be multiple Outsiders who are Wolfboys]
characters.lede: Surviving Wolfboys turn into evil Minions.
characters.quote: You call us 'Wolfboys,' as if we were a pack. We never were. The only thing we share is this: we were all cast out by the town. You hate us, and we hate you. The wolf pack has no name, and neither do I. But one day the Demon will grant one of us a new name — a real name. And on that day, he will use that name to knock on every one of your doors.
summaryBullets: The Wolfboy's setup adjustment does not increase or decrease the number of Outsiders, but it may result in several Outsiders all being Wolfboys.
The Wolfboy's ability can only trigger when other Wolfboys die. So if only one Wolfboy is in play, his ability can never trigger.

The Wolfboy's character change happens immediately when all other Wolfboys are dead. The Wolfboy's night-order slot only reminds the Storyteller not to forget to wake a Wolfboy who changed during the day and tell him his character and team changes.
If the Wolfboy's character changes at night, wake him immediately and tell him how his character and team changed.

If some condition restricts the Wolfboy's character change or team change, the Wolfboy only changes whichever part can change. For example, if all Minion characters are already in play, the Wolfboy only turns evil without changing character. If the Wolfboy cannot turn evil (e.g., restricted by the Spirit of Sanctity), he only becomes a Minion character not in play.
howToRun: During setup, before putting character tokens into the bag, you may replace other Outsider character tokens with Wolfboy character tokens.

When a Wolfboy dies, if only one Wolfboy remains alive, replace that surviving Wolfboy's character token with a Minion character not in play and turn them evil. If it is daytime, tell that Wolfboy player at the first opportunity after nightfall. If it is nighttime, wake that Wolfboy player and tell them how their character and team have changed.
examples: 12-player game; both Outsiders are Wolfboys. On the first day, one Wolfboy dies by execution; the other Wolfboy immediately becomes the evil Poisoner.
12-player game; only one Wolfboy is in play. The Wolfboy cannot become an evil Minion.
12-player game; the Baron is in play and all 4 Outsiders are Wolfboys. After 3 of the Wolfboys die, the last surviving Wolfboy becomes the evil Scarlet Woman.
tips: If you're the Wolfboy, there may be several Wolfboys in play, or only you. If all other Outsiders are dead but your character hasn't changed, you're the only Wolfboy — and you can go public with this.
If you're the Wolfboy and you die, announce your character immediately — because another Wolfboy has very likely become an evil Minion.
If you're the Wolfboy and you've become an evil Minion, all other Wolfboys are dead. From now on, wreak as much havoc as you can for the evil team.
If you're the Demon, attack the other Wolfboys and spare one! He'll become your capable teammate.
If you're a Minion, quickly work out who the Wolfboys are and how many there are. If necessary, you can bluff as a Wolfboy to fish for other players' information.
bluffing: Wolfboys tend not to reveal their character early.
Wolfboys tend to reveal their character after death.
The Wolfboy works well as a backup bluff.
If you die, you can claim you were a Wolfboy and attack the other Outsider players.
characters.creator: Taiyi
characters.otherNightReminder: If a Wolfboy changed character today, wake him and tell him his new character and team.

customBoxes.title: Design Notes
customBoxes.content:
A rework of the Demon's Bastard. The Demon's Bastard swings the game too hard — Outsiders shouldn't have that kind of ability.

Among several Wolfboys, at most one will ever actually inflict the negative effect, but the Wolfboys fall into mutual suspicion, hiding, and attacks — even with only one Wolfboy in play.

The Wolfboy suits scripts built around Outsiders as the central theme.

characters.name: Cowboy
characters.ability: On the 1st night, a Minion learns you are in play. Their nominations wake you that night. The 1st of you to nominate the other is executed.
characters.lede: The Cowboy duels his nemesis.
characters.quote: When the countdown ends, the speed of my draw is the length of the rest of your life.
summaryBullets: The Cowboy's nemesis is determined at the start of the game and never changes, whatever character or team the nemesis becomes.
In rare cases, if there is no Minion in play at the start of the game, the Cowboy has no nemesis.
A Cowboy created mid-game has no nemesis, and no Minion learns he is in play — effectively, he has no usable ability.
If the Cowboy's nemesis is already dead but they have never nominated each other, the Cowboy nominating the dead nemesis still triggers an immediate execution.

It's best to announce clearly when nominations begin. If the Cowboy and the nemesis nominate each other simultaneously, you decide who nominated first. If you truly can't tell, you may re-open nominations or use a quick mini-game to decide (such as the bell slap from "German Heart Attack," or placing a card on the table and seeing who grabs it after a countdown; online, the Storyteller can post "Go" in the chat and players reply "I nominate X," with message order deciding).

If the Cowboy or the nemesis nominate each other while the Cowboy is poisoned or drunk, the first-nomination chance is wasted (the "Settled" token is still placed in the Grimoire); once the Cowboy is sober and healthy again, their mutual nominations no longer trigger executions.
If the Cowboy is poisoned or drunk, you may wake him on nights you shouldn't, or not wake him on nights you should, to deceive him appropriately.
False information format: waking the Cowboy is not information; there is no false information format, and the Vortox does not affect whether the Cowboy is woken.
howToRun: While preparing for the first night, place the Cowboy's "Nemesis" reminder by a Minion's character token. On the first night, wake that Minion, tell them the Cowboy is in play, then put them back to sleep.
Each day, if the "Nemesis" nominates, place the "Nominated" reminder by the "Nemesis" character token.
Each night except the first, if the "Nemesis" is marked "Nominated," wake the Cowboy, then put him back to sleep. At dawn, remove the "Nominated" reminder.

When the Cowboy nominates the "Nemesis," or the "Nemesis" nominates the Cowboy, and the "Settled" reminder is not in play, immediately declare the nominated player executed. Then place the "Settled" reminder in play.
examples: On the first night, the Poisoner learns the Cowboy is in play. On the first day, the Cowboy nominates the Poisoner; the Poisoner is immediately executed and dies. The Storyteller declares night falls.

On the first night, the Poisoner learns the Cowboy is in play. On the first day, when nominations open, the Cowboy and the Poisoner nominate each other simultaneously; the Storyteller hears the Poisoner's nomination first, so the Cowboy is immediately executed and dies. The Storyteller declares night falls.
On the first night, the Poisoner learns the Cowboy is in play. On the first day, the Poisoner nominates a player. That night, the Cowboy is woken.

On the first night, the Poisoner learns the Cowboy is in play. On the first day, the Poisoner does not nominate. On the second night, the Cowboy is not woken. On the second day, the Cowboy nominates the Imp, then the Poisoner nominates the Cowboy; the Cowboy is immediately executed and dies. The Storyteller declares night falls.

On the first night, the Poisoner learns the Cowboy is in play. On the first day, the Poisoner is nominated by another player and dies by execution; that night the Cowboy is not woken. On the second day, the Cowboy nominates the dead Poisoner; the Poisoner is immediately executed. The Storyteller declares night falls.

On the first night, the Poisoner learns the Cowboy is in play. On the first day, the Cowboy is poisoned; the Cowboy nominates the Poisoner, and the nomination proceeds normally. The next day, the Cowboy is healthy again; the Poisoner nominates the Cowboy, and the nomination proceeds normally (the Cowboy's ability was wasted while poisoned).
tips: Revealing yourself as the Cowboy early is very dangerous — your nemesis may nominate you first. That's not necessarily bad: it at least proves there's a Cowboy and a Minion among you, though it's better if the one lying on the ground is the Minion.
Ignore players you've already nominated or who have nominated you — they can't be your nemesis (assuming you weren't poisoned or drunk).
You can make some casual nominations every day; maybe fortune favors you and your very first shot chooses your nemesis.
You can also hold off nominating early — though your nemesis may spot that you're the Cowboy — then strike precisely after gathering a few nights of information, one shot, one kill.
If you're the Minion who learned the Cowboy is in play (the nemesis), find the Cowboy quickly and watch whether the Cowboy suspects you before acting.

If you're the nemesis, the best way to handle the Cowboy may be asking your Demon boss to kill him at night, or nominating him (or letting him nominate you) while he's poisoned. Even if you execute him by nomination, it definitively proves there's a Cowboy and a Minion among you — and unless you publicly claim to be the Cowboy, everyone else will know you're the Minion.

If you're the nemesis and the Cowboy has publicly claimed to be the Cowboy, you can also publicly claim to be the Cowboy. But then you're locked in a life-or-death duel that day. If you're lucky enough, you might not only beat him but convince everyone you're the real Cowboy.
bluffing: The Cowboy is a hard character to bluff. If you go the whole game without your ability executing a player or getting you executed, it's hard to convince others you're a Cowboy.

If you want to bluff as the Cowboy and survive to the late game, plan in advance how to explain why your ability never fired. Claiming your "nemesis" is already dead is a reasonable explanation — but other players may still demand you nominate the dead player to trigger the execution and prove you're the Cowboy.
characters.creator: Taiyi, 提线政客
characters.tags: Execution, Nominations, Public, You Start Knowing
characters.firstNightReminder: Wake a Minion and tell them the Cowboy is in play.
characters.otherNightReminder: If the Minion who learned the Cowboy is in play nominated today, wake the Cowboy.

customBoxes.title: Reminder Tokens
customBoxes.content:
[[Nemesis]]
Placed when: While preparing for the first night.
Condition: Place the "Nemesis" reminder by a Minion's character token.
Removed when: The Cowboy dies or leaves play.

[[Nominated]]
Placed when: When the "Nemesis" nominates.
Condition: Place the "Nominated" reminder by the "Nemesis" character token.
Removed when: At dawn.

[[Settled]]
Placed when: When the Cowboy nominates the "Nemesis," or the "Nemesis" nominates the Cowboy.
Condition: Place it by the Cowboy's character token. Place it whether or not the Cowboy is drunk or poisoned.
Removed when: The Cowboy dies or leaves play.

characters.name: The Cat Adventurers
characters.ability: Each day, a player who has not explored may publicly choose to explore. If they live that night, you learn an opposing player.
characters.lede: The Cat Adventurers send an explorer out each day to find players of the opposing team.
characters.quote: Good afternoon, meow, everyone. The Cat Adventurers have come at the riddle's call, and we're honored to lighten your town's burdens, meow. We need a brave soul familiar with the local terrain to clear our path, meow. Before that, I'm obliged to inform you all that venturing into danger carries enormous risk, meow. Now then — which brave soul will join the glorious Cat Adventurers, meow?
summaryBullets: Any player who has not "explored" may publicly "explore" (including the Cat Adventurers themselves and dead players), once per day, first come first served. If the publicly "exploring" player qualifies, clearly reply "Received" or "On behalf of the Cat Adventurers, I thank you for your bravery." If a player who has already "explored" declares again, or a new player declares after an "Explorer" has been set that day, clearly refuse them. Refused players are not treated as having "explored."
If the Cat Adventurers are not in play, or are poisoned or drunk, still play along with publicly "exploring" players exactly as if the Cat Adventurers were in play.

If the Cat Adventurers are poisoned or drunk, you may give them false information. But do not wake them on nights nobody publicly "explored," or skip waking them on nights somebody did — the Cat Adventurers would then know for certain they were poisoned or drunk.

Whether a player has "explored" does not change with whether the Cat Adventurers are in play. If a player has "explored," they cannot explore again even if the Cat Adventurers are not in play — not even if the Cat Adventurers join mid-game or the Cat Adventurers player changes.
Travellers may not "explore" (Traveller Exclusion Principle).
Information format: one player, e.g., "May" or "player #1."
False information format: one player, e.g., "May" or "player #1," but on the same team as that day's explorer.
howToRun: Each day, if a player publicly declares they want to "explore" — or makes any other statement expressing they want to trigger the Cat Adventurers' ability (you can encourage fun declarations) — if they have not "explored" before, clearly respond "Received" or "On behalf of the Cat Adventurers, I thank you for your bravery," or similar atmospheric replies. Then place the "Explorer" reminder by that player's character token. If any other living player also publicly declares they want to "explore" that day, tell them someone beat them to it and clearly refuse them. If a player who has already "explored" publicly declares again, clearly refuse them.

Each night except the first, if the player marked "Explorer" is alive, wake the Cat Adventurers and tell them a player on a different team to the player marked "Explorer". If the "Explorer" reminder was not placed, or the player marked "Explorer" is dead, do not wake the Cat Adventurers.
Each dawn, replace all "Explorer" reminders in play with "Explored" reminders.
examples: On the first day, the Noble publicly declares "I'm going exploring!" The Demon does not kill the Noble that night, and the Cat Adventurers learn the Poisoner player. On the second day, the Noble publicly declares "I'm going exploring!" — since the Noble has already "explored," the Storyteller refuses them.
On the first day, the Noble publicly declares "I want to join the glorious Cat Adventurers!" The Demon kills the Noble that night, and the Cat Adventurers are not woken.
On the first day, the Noble publicly declares "I am the Cat Adventurers' vanguard guide!" CodeX kills the Cat Adventurers that night, and the Cat Adventurers are not woken.

On the first day, the Poisoner publicly declares "I will defend the Cat Adventurers' glory with my life!" The Demon does not kill the Poisoner that night, and the Cat Adventurers learn the Noble player.

On the first day, the Noble publicly declares "I'll be the Cat Adventurers' guide!", and the Poisoner then publicly declares "I'll clear the path for the Cat Adventurers!" — but since the Noble beat them to it, the Storyteller refuses the Poisoner.

On the first day, the Cat Adventurers are not in play; the Noble publicly declares "I am the Cat Adventurers' vanguard guide!", and the Storyteller answers "Received" just as if the Cat Adventurers were in play.
tips: Encourage everyone to "explore"! Otherwise you do nothing at all. If all else fails, go yourself!

The "exploring" player and the player you learn that night are on different teams, but the explorer isn't necessarily good, and the player you learn isn't necessarily evil. Evil players volunteering to "explore" is quite common.
If you think the "exploring" player and the player you learned are on the same team, consider the Vortox, or that you were poisoned or drunk.

If you're a good character who doesn't fear death, fight for the chance to "explore"! If you survive, the Cat Adventurers learn a player on a different team from you. Even if you die, you've taken a knife for a more important Townsfolk! If you're a character like the Aerialist who wants to fall at night, you should fight even harder for the "explore" slot.

If you're a good character who fears death, exploring carries enormous risk — but you can still "explore." Bluff yourself as a death-defying character, or even as one like the Aerialist who wants to die at night; if you fool the Demon, you pass the night safely.

If you're an evil player, you can fight to "explore" too! To most players, volunteering to "explore" looks like active, pro-town play. And your "exploring" guarantees the Cat Adventurers won't learn the Demon or your other key teammates that day.

If you're the Demon and you think the Cat Adventurers might be in play, weigh your next moves carefully. Kill that day's "explorer" to guarantee the Cat Adventurers learn nothing? Gamble on killing the suspected Cat Adventurers player directly? Or leave it alone? Killing the day's explorer guarantees no information that night, but it may only be treating the symptoms — a new explorer will step up tomorrow.
bluffing: When bluffing as the Cat Adventurers, beware! If the "explorer" died that day, or there was no "explorer," you are not woken at night.
Each day, offer opinions about who should "explore" — this helps everyone believe you're the Cat Adventurers.

Think carefully about how to report your information. Your information sets two players against each other; if they're both inclined to trust each other as good, they may unite to attack you. In most cases, naming a player the day's "explorer" already distrusts helps you win the town's trust.
characters.creator: Taiyi
characters.otherNightReminder: If today's explorer is alive, wake them and tell them a player on the opposing team to the explorer.

customBoxes.title: Reminder Tokens
customBoxes.content:
[[Explorer" ×1]]
Placed when: When a player publicly "explores."
Condition: When a player publicly "explores," if they have never been marked "Explored" and no "Explorer" token has been placed that day, place the "Explorer" reminder by that player's character token to remind the Storyteller whether to wake the Cat Adventurers at their point in the night order. Place it whenever these conditions are met, whether or not the Cat Adventurers are drunk or poisoned.
Removed when: At dawn.

[[Explored" ×4]]
Placed when: At dawn.
Condition: At dawn, replace the "Explorer" reminder with an "Explored" reminder.
Removed when: Never.

characters.name: Ranger
characters.ability: If 1 of your alive neighbors dies, you are woken that night to choose a player: if they are a Minion, they die.
characters.lede: The Ranger hunts Minions on the night a neighboring player dies.
characters.quote: No grave for hounds and hawks — the forest crows are their burial.
summaryBullets: If the player wasn't the Ranger when the alive player neighboring them died, they are not woken that night even if they become the Ranger.

As long as an alive player neighboring the Ranger dies (refer to the Tea Lady or the Empath for "neighboring"), the Ranger is woken that night. Over a game, the Ranger may be woken many times or not at all — but at most once per night.
Determining who neighbors the Ranger ignores Travellers, and the Ranger cannot choose Traveller players (Traveller Exclusion Principle).
howToRun: When an alive player neighboring the Ranger dies, place the "Vengeance" reminder by the Ranger. At night, if the "Vengeance" reminder has been placed, wake the Ranger and let them choose a player. If they chose a Minion, mark that Minion "Dead." Remove the "Vengeance" reminder after the Ranger acts.
examples: The Paperboy is the alive player nearest to the Ranger. By day the Paperboy dies by execution; that night the Ranger is woken and chooses the Widow, and the Widow dies.
The Paperboy is the alive player nearest to the Ranger. At night the Paperboy is killed by the Demon; that night the Ranger is woken and chooses the Widow, and the Widow dies.
The Ranger sits next to the Paperboy. By day the Paperboy dies by execution; that night the Ranger is woken and chooses the Vortox, and nothing happens.
The Ranger sits next to the Paperboy. By day the already-dead Paperboy is executed again; that night the Ranger is not woken.
tips: Find ways to get the alive players nearest to you killed. Only when they die are you woken to use your ability.
If your neighbors are important Townsfolk, they'll easily die at night — don't rush, just wait for their deaths.
If the player you chose didn't die, they're definitely not a Minion. If you're sure they're evil, they're very likely the Demon.
bluffing: Actively pushing to execute your neighbors makes you look more like a Ranger.
If your neighbor died that day, remember that as the Ranger you'd be woken and act — decide your claimed choice in advance.
characters.creator: Taiyi
characters.otherNightReminder: If an alive player neighboring the Ranger died today, let them choose a player.

customBoxes.title: Reminder Tokens
customBoxes.content:
[[Dead]]
Placed when: After the Ranger acts at night and chooses a player.
Condition: The Ranger's chosen player is currently alive and a Minion, can be killed by the Ranger, and the Ranger is not drunk or poisoned — place it by that player's character token to remind the Storyteller to announce the night's dead at dawn.
Removed when: After announcing the dead at dawn, at the Storyteller's convenience.

[[Vengeance]]
Placed when: Each day before the Ranger acts, if an alive player neighboring the Ranger dies — whatever the cause — place it by the Ranger's character token.
Condition: When an alive player neighboring the Ranger dies, place it by the Ranger's character token whether or not the Ranger is drunk or poisoned. If several alive players neighboring the Ranger die in one day, only one "Vengeance" token is placed. This token reminds the Storyteller whether to wake the Ranger at night.
Removed when: After the Ranger acts at night, at the Storyteller's convenience.

characters.name: Valkyrie
characters.ability: Each night*, deaths are delayed until you learn who died. You may choose to be the only death instead.
characters.lede: The Valkyrie can sacrifice herself to protect other players.
characters.quote: Standing on the border of life and death, I feel the weight of life more than anyone. I have seen too much sacrifice, too many pointless deaths. But among you, I still long to see a different final chapter — one that shines with the light of wisdom and resounds with the echo of courage.
summaryBullets: Learning who died: the Valkyrie is told which players' deaths were delayed tonight when she acts. This is part of the Valkyrie's life-and-death decision ability, not information-gathering in the usual sense, so the Valkyrie's ability has no false information format and the Vortox cannot affect it.

Delayed death: when a player is about to die but temporarily does not, with the death postponed until the delay effect ends or disappears. Delayed deaths include deaths from execution and from character abilities.

If the Valkyrie is poisoned or drunk, under the "reasonable deception" principle you may give her false deaths. This is generally not recommended, because whether or not she uses her ability that night, she'll discover from the ability's abnormality that she was poisoned or drunk (if she lets the deaths happen, she'll find the dead aren't the players she was told; if she dies instead, she'll find the dead player isn't herself). One exception: when the Valkyrie is poisoned or drunk and dies that night, you may tell her false deaths — if she chooses to die instead, she'll be deceived into thinking she saved the other players.
The Valkyrie's ability delays all players' deaths, including her own. So when the Valkyrie learns her own death was delayed, she can choose to be the only death that night.
Only when the Valkyrie dies from her own ability do other players escape death. If the Valkyrie chooses to die instead but doesn't die for some reason, the players with delayed deaths still die.

After the Valkyrie lets the deaths happen, those deaths resolve in their original order, and they cannot be "cancelled" for any reason. For example, if Puck chose to kill CodeX and CodeX chose to kill the Noble, once the Valkyrie lets the deaths happen that night, both CodeX and the Noble die — the kill on the Noble is not "cancelled" just because CodeX is already dead.

If the Lich King chooses a player whose death was delayed that night (e.g., by CodeX's or Puck's ability, which act before the Demon), then whether or not the Valkyrie let the deaths happen that night, the Lich King only "kills" that player without treating them as a dead player to trigger his special ability — because that player was still alive when the Lich King chose them.

If the Valkyrie is poisoned or drunk at night and the source of the poisoning/drunkenness then disappears or dies, the Valkyrie's poisoned/drunk state persists until dawn. This rule avoids complex interactions from the Valkyrie regaining her ability mid-process when the source dies — e.g., the Bard's ability makes the Valkyrie drunk, the Bard is killed that night, the Valkyrie regains her ability because of the Bard's death, and the restored Valkyrie can no longer protect the Bard.

"About to die" resolves before "delayed death." For example, if the Demon kills the Lady, you first decide whether another player dies in the Lady's place, then delay the death of whoever is about to die.

Special interaction: if one Ettin is killed at night, treat the other living Ettin as having a delayed death; if the Valkyrie lets this death happen, both Ettins die. Because of the Ettin's special mechanics, without this treatment they might die after the Valkyrie acts without their death being delayed, which defeats the design intent.
The Valkyrie never learns of Traveller deaths, and even when the Valkyrie uses her ability she cannot make a Traveller death-proof (Traveller Exclusion Principle).
howToRun: On nights except the first, if players die at night, wait until the Valkyrie acts before resolving those deaths. At the Valkyrie's point in the night order, wake the Valkyrie and point at each player who died tonight in turn. The Valkyrie then either nods to let these deaths happen (the deaths resolve) or shakes her head to die instead (mark the Valkyrie dead; no other player dies tonight).
examples: On the second night, the Noble is killed by CodeX and the Truelove is killed by the Demon, but their deaths are delayed by the Valkyrie's ability, so the Truelove's ability does not trigger yet. The Valkyrie is woken; the Storyteller points at the Noble player and the Truelove player; the Valkyrie nods in approval. The Noble and the Truelove die, and a player starts being drunk.

On the second night, the Truelove is killed by CodeX and the Valkyrie is killed by the Demon, but their deaths are delayed by the Valkyrie's ability, so the Truelove's ability does not trigger yet. The Valkyrie is woken; the Storyteller points at the Valkyrie player and the Truelove player; the Valkyrie shakes her head in disapproval. The Valkyrie dies and the Truelove does not.

On the second night, the Demon kills themself, but the death is delayed by the Valkyrie's ability. The Valkyrie is woken; the Storyteller points at the Demon player; the Valkyrie shakes her head in disapproval. The Valkyrie dies and the Demon does not.

On the second night, the Demon kills themself, but the death is delayed by the Valkyrie's ability. The Valkyrie is woken; the Storyteller points at the Demon player; the Valkyrie nods in approval. The only living Demon dies, and the game ends.
tips: Your ability is enormously powerful: if you don't want certain players to die at night, they won't! Secretly protect the players you think are important, and don't use your ability lightly before their deaths are delayed.
If you learn your own death was delayed, you'd best use your ability. Either way, you're unlikely to survive the night — and you might save the other players dying alongside you.
If two, three, or even more players' deaths were delayed, think hard about using your ability. Trading your life for more players' lives is usually a bargain.
After using your ability, tell everyone whom you protected. Players who die at night are usually good players.
Beware of cunning evil players baiting you into using your ability! Minions — even the Demon — may kill themselves to trick you into spending your ability protecting them!
If you're an evil player, distribute your team's death-causing abilities carefully! Causing too many deaths with abilities at once can easily be wiped out by the Valkyrie's ability!

If you're the Demon, consider a wicked plan — kill other evil players, even yourself, to bait the Valkyrie into protecting you! It's a very high-risk plan, of course — but the greater the risk, the greater the reward. If the Valkyrie protects you, you must be a good player in her eyes.
bluffing: The Valkyrie is a hard character for the Demon to bluff. After important Townsfolk die, everyone will demand to know why you didn't step in to protect them. Without a good answer, you may be executed.
A good plan: a Minion bluffs as the Valkyrie and is killed by the Demon at night. The dead Minion can claim they protected the Demon or another evil player, making them look like good players.

characters.otherNightReminder: Tell her which players are about to die tonight, and let her choose whether to die instead.

customBoxes.title: Reminder Tokens
customBoxes.content:
[[Dead]]
Placed when: When the Valkyrie acts at night.
Condition: The Valkyrie is not drunk or poisoned, and she chose to die instead tonight. Place it by the Valkyrie to remind the Storyteller that the Valkyrie died from her own ability and no other player will die tonight.
Removed when: At the Storyteller's convenience.

characters.name: Hell's Outcast
characters.ability: Each day before nominations, a Minion may publicly name you: you turn evil & swap characters with the Demon, who becomes drunk.
characters.lede: If the Minions decide to enthrone a new king, Hell's Outcast becomes the new Demon.
characters.quote: They clipped my wings and cast me into the wasteland. Every inch of rotting earth is counting down, until hell enthrones its new king.
summaryBullets: Publicly enthrone Hell's Outcast: a Minion publicly declaring "I enthrone Hell's Outcast!" This declaration does not need to name a player (no need to specify which Hell's Outcast is enthroned).
Whether the Minion is dead or alive does not affect their ability to publicly enthrone Hell's Outcast.
A player who started as a Minion and became another character type can no longer trigger Hell's Outcast's ability by publicly enthroning.

When a Minion publicly declares "I enthrone Hell's Outcast!", the character swap and team changes of the Demon and Hell's Outcast happen immediately, but you wait until the first opportunity after nightfall to wake them and tell them the changes.
If Hell's Outcast asks during the day after someone has publicly enthroned to confirm his current character and team, do not answer.
If several Demons are in play, the Storyteller chooses one Demon to swap with Hell's Outcast — generally preferring a living evil Demon.

Jinx (Hell's Outcast & Ettin): if the total number of evil players already exceeds the initial setup by one (not counting evil Travellers), then in Hell's Outcast's ability, "you immediately turn evil and swap characters with the Demon" becomes "you immediately swap teams and characters with the Demon."
howToRun: When a Minion publicly declares "I enthrone Hell's Outcast!" before nominations begin during the day, and a sober and healthy Hell's Outcast is in play, immediately swap the Demon's character token with the Hell's Outcast token, place "Dethroned (Drunk)" by the new Hell's Outcast, and mark the new Demon evil. After nightfall, at the first opportunity, wake them and tell them their character and team changes.
examples: On the first day before nominations begin, the Widow publicly declares "I enthrone Hell's Outcast!" Hell's Outcast (good) immediately becomes the Vortox (evil); the Vortox (evil) immediately becomes Hell's Outcast (evil) and is drunk.
During the first day's nomination phase, the Widow publicly declares "I enthrone Hell's Outcast!" Nothing happens.
On the first day before nominations begin, the Vortox publicly declares "I enthrone Hell's Outcast!" Nothing happens.

With only 4 players left, before nominations begin, the Widow publicly declares "I enthrone Hell's Outcast!" Hell's Outcast (good) immediately becomes the Vortox (evil); the Vortox (evil) immediately becomes Hell's Outcast (evil) and is drunk.

On the second night, Puck turns the Fortune Teller (good) into Hell's Outcast (good). After dawn, Puck immediately declares "I enthrone Hell's Outcast!" Hell's Outcast (good) immediately becomes the Vortox (evil); the Vortox (evil) immediately becomes Hell's Outcast (evil) and is drunk.

12-player game. On the first day before nominations begin, there are 4 evil players in play: the Widow (evil), 2 Ettins (evil), and the Vortox (evil). The Widow (evil) publicly declares "I enthrone Hell's Outcast!" Hell's Outcast (good) immediately becomes the Vortox (evil); the Vortox (evil) immediately becomes Hell's Outcast (good) and is drunk. (See the jinx with the Ettin in Rule Details.)
tips: If you don't want to join evil and become their new leader, you can reveal your character early. With your position exposed, evil will carefully consider whether to enthrone you. Of course, if evil is cornered, they may still risk enthroning you — most likely dragging you down to defeat with them. So the safest plan is getting yourself killed, ending any possibility of joining evil.
If you do want to join evil and become their new king, don't reveal your character early — find a good bluff and quietly wait for the Minions to crown you.

If you watch evil about to win and the Minions show no sign of enthroning you, nominate the player you believe is the Demon during the final day's nomination phase. You've missed the last train to evil; the Minions have abandoned you; all you can do now is serve good. Reveal your true character and start attacking the real Demon.

If you're the Demon, there's no Ettin among the Minions, and a Minion has now publicly enthroned Hell's Outcast: if Hell's Outcast is truly still alive, you're now an evil Outsider and the Minions have a new boss — drop the Demon's burdens and do the last things you can for evil. If you're unsure whether Hell's Outcast is in play, wait for the definite information at night before acting.

If you're the Demon, there IS an Ettin among the Minions, and a Minion has now publicly enthroned Hell's Outcast: be extremely careful, because if Hell's Outcast is truly still alive, you've just become a GOOD and DRUNK Outsider Hell's Outcast!!! (With an Ettin in play, enthronement swaps the Demon's and Hell's Outcast's characters AND teams.) If this really happened, you've been utterly abandoned by evil — you're not only no longer the Demon, you're not even evil. If you can confirm this has happened, announce it immediately and let the Minions who betrayed you and their new king face your vengeful wrath.

If you're a Minion, quickly figuring out whether Hell's Outcast is in play — and who — is very important. A living Hell's Outcast is evil's spare tire and escape route; if possible, keep him for the end of the game.

If you're a Minion, choosing the right moment to enthrone Hell's Outcast matters. If the wind turns against you that day and the Demon will likely die by execution, enthrone publicly before nominations begin.
If you're a Minion, have a dead Minion do the public enthroning whenever possible, preserving evil's living strength.

If you're a Minion, you can publicly enthrone Hell's Outcast even when he's not in play, confusing good's read on the Demon's position. Or, with Hell's Outcast in play, have the Demon do the public enthroning — this doesn't trigger Hell's Outcast's ability, and good can't tell whether the Demon actually moved.
bluffing: Revealing yourself as Hell's Outcast early is risky — people may execute you immediately to keep you from joining evil.

Revealing yourself as Hell's Outcast late may be a fine choice, explaining your odd behavior earlier in the game. As long as nobody publicly enthroned Hell's Outcast this game and the Outsider count isn't abnormal, you can probably survive to the end.

Placed when: When the Demon's character is swapped away by enthronement.

characters.name: Don Quixote
characters.ability: A player — the Windmill — registers as a Demon to Townsfolk abilities, even after you die. You learn who they are. They then change.
characters.lede: Don Quixote spends his life chasing the wrong target — but he never gives up.
characters.quote: Look! That towering giant, waving its long arms, awaits my challenge! What? You say it's a windmill? No, no — you are mistaken. They move, they breathe, they mock my hesitation. My lance is ready, my steed is neighing. Don't hold me back — glory calls!
summaryBullets: In A Midsummer Night's Dream, the Townsfolk Don Quixote can affect: the Perfumer, the Dreamer, the Priest, the Bard, the Wish Fairy (if her wished ability relates to the Demon), the Aerialist (you may substitute the Don Quixote-affected player for the real Demon in the Aerialist's information).

In A Midsummer Night's Dream, the Townsfolk definitely NOT affected by Don Quixote: the Paperboy (fact/fiction checks ignore interaction interference), the Truelove, the Noble, the Seamstress, the Cat Adventurers, the Cowboy.

Don Quixote's ability only affects Townsfolk characters' abilities — not other characters' (Outsider, Minion, Demon) abilities or game rules. So after all Demons are dead, you cannot treat Don Quixote's Windmill as a living Demon to keep the game going, because his ability can't affect game rules. Nor, after the Cyclops chooses the Windmill, can you treat the Windmill as a Demon to give the Cyclops false information — the Cyclops is a Minion, not a Townsfolk.
Unlike the Recluse, Don Quixote has no "might." When a Townsfolk player's ability checks the player affected by Don Quixote, you must register them as some Demon character or the Demon type.

Any player can become Don Quixote's Windmill: alive or dead; Don Quixote himself; a Townsfolk, Outsider, Minion, or even a Demon. But once the Windmill is set, the affected player cannot change until Don Quixote visits you.

Once Don Quixote visits you, you must mark a new player as the "Windmill." He now knows who was previously affected; whether to make an important player the new "Windmill" to keep influencing the game, or an unimportant one to limit further damage, is your judgment call.
When the Windmill must move, any player except the currently marked one can be the new Windmill.

Don Quixote's visits are unlimited in number and timing — he may visit you at any time (compare the Puzzle Master). It's better to have players visit during the day to avoid disrupting night actions; if you're busy when Don Quixote visits, you may have him come back when you're free.

Though Don Quixote can visit any number of times in a day, remind players that frequent visits are pointless: he can never know who will be affected next, and visiting repeatedly in one day yields no useful information and changes nothing.

If Don Quixote visits you while poisoned or drunk, you may tell him a player who isn't actually affected. But you must still immediately move the "Windmill" reminder to a new player's character token.

The first half of Don Quixote's ability works even after his death, so his death can't stop its side effects. The second half stops working once he's dead — Don Quixote can only visit the Storyteller while alive.
Travellers cannot become the Windmill (Traveller Exclusion Principle).
Information format: a player's name or seat number.
False information format: the name or seat number of a player not marked "Windmill."
howToRun: While preparing for the first night, place Don Quixote's "Windmill" reminder by any player's character token.

Whenever a Townsfolk's ability would check the character or character type of the player marked "Windmill," that player registers as a Demon and as a Demon character; you decide which Demon character they register as.

At any time during the game, Don Quixote may visit you privately, and you tell him which player is marked "Windmill." After you tell Don Quixote who is marked "Windmill," immediately move the "Windmill" reminder to another player's character token.
examples: The Truelove is Don Quixote's Windmill (registers as a Demon character to Townsfolk abilities). On the first night, the Fortune Teller chooses themself and the Truelove and gets the false answer "yes."
The Poisoner is Don Quixote's Windmill. On the first night, the Dreamer chooses the Poisoner and gets the false answer "Imp, Seamstress."
The Baron is Don Quixote's Windmill. On the first night, the Perfumer chooses the evil character Vortox; the Baron learns the Perfumer is in play.

The Noble is Don Quixote's Windmill. On the first night, the Seamstress chooses the Noble and the Dreamer and gets the true answer "yes." (Don Quixote's ability only makes the affected player register as the Demon type or a Demon character — not as the evil team.)
The Noble is Don Quixote's Windmill. On the first day, the Bard publicly chooses the Noble; that night the Bard gets the false answer "0."

The Noble is Don Quixote's Windmill. On the first day, Don Quixote asks the Storyteller and learns the Noble player; Don Quixote's Windmill immediately changes from the Noble to the Fortune Teller. On the second day, Don Quixote asks the Storyteller and learns the Fortune Teller player; Don Quixote's Windmill immediately changes from the Fortune Teller to the Poisoner.
tips: You're Don Quixote, and you may lead the good team astray on the road to the Demon. No matter! You can always visit the Storyteller to learn whom you've affected, then eliminate possible errors. But the side effect is obvious too: a new player becomes your interference! Whether to use your ability early to eliminate errors, or avoid using it to prevent greater damage — rely on your wisdom. After all, you are Don Quixote!
The Truelove, Noble, Seamstress, Cat Adventurers, and Cowboy are not affected by your ability! Their abilities check teams, lies, or Minions — none of which relate to your ability!

The player you learn isn't necessarily not the Demon! A cunning Storyteller may deliberately set the Demon as your "Windmill" to disrupt good's judgment of the Demon's species — or to make you think they're just a good player affected by your ability!
If you've locked onto a Demon but doubt whether your ability is affecting them, visit the Storyteller! If the Storyteller's answer isn't that player, execute them immediately!
bluffing: Bluffing as Don Quixote is a great way to get a locked-on Demon off the hook! Whether you're a Minion or the Demon themself, once you claim to be Don Quixote, logically any player in the game could register as a Demon to Townsfolk abilities. Especially after pretending to visit the Storyteller and claiming the player you learned is the locked-on Demon — the danger of the Demon being executed today drops a notch.

Note! Before Don Quixote visits the Storyteller, the affected player doesn't change; after each visit, it changes immediately. Organize what you want to say in advance — don't leave too big a hole in your story.
characters.creator: Taiyi
characters.tags: Consult, Even If Dead, Information, Misregistration, Reverse, You Start Knowing

customBoxes.title: Reminder Tokens
customBoxes.content:
[[Windmill]]
Placed when: While preparing for the first night, or after Don Quixote visits you.
Condition: Place the "Windmill" reminder by any player's character token. If Don Quixote visited you, move the "Windmill" to another player's character token (even if Don Quixote is poisoned or drunk).
Removed when: Don Quixote leaves play, or after Don Quixote visits you.

characters.name: Puck
characters.ability: Once per game, at night*, choose a non-Demon character: they die. If not in play, choose a player: they become that character.
characters.lede: Puck loves to destroy characters she hates or conjure characters she likes.
characters.quote: Come on, come on! Let's turn this serious deduction into a playground! I promise— winks —I'll make everything extra, extra 'fun'! Quick, let me see who'll be lucky enough to become my new toy today?
summaryBullets: If multiple players in play are the character Puck chose, the Storyteller chooses one of them to die.
If Puck publicly claimed to be the Minstrel during the day and chose players, even if he becomes the Minstrel that night, no players are drunk because of him.

Code X's ability is "On your Xth night" — if Puck turns a player into Code X mid-game, that night is his first night as Code X, and so on. For example, if on the 4th night Puck turns herself into Code X, the Storyteller wakes Code X and signals that she may only choose once.
Puck cannot choose Traveller characters — she cannot kill Travellers or turn players into Travellers (the Traveller Exclusion Principle).
Jinx: When the Miser is chosen or created by Puck, the Miser immediately loses his ability.
Jinx: When an evil player becomes the Hanged Man or gains the Hanged Man's ability (e.g., an evil Philosopher), they immediately lose that ability.
howToRun: Each night except the first, wake Puck. She may shake her head to not use her ability, or point to a character icon on the character sheet. If the character she chose is in play, mark that character's player dead. If the character she chose is not in play, have Puck choose another player and mark that player as becoming her chosen character, then put Puck to sleep. Then wake the player whose character changed. Show them, in turn, the "You are" info token and their new character token, then put them back to sleep. Once Puck has used her ability, do not wake Puck on later nights.
examples: On the second night, Puck chooses the Fortune Teller; the Fortune Teller is in play — the Fortune Teller dies.
On the second night, Puck chooses the Fortune Teller; the Fortune Teller is not in play. The Storyteller has Puck choose a player; Puck chooses herself — Puck becomes the Fortune Teller (evil).
On the second night, Puck chooses the Sweetheart; the Sweetheart is not in play. The Storyteller has Puck choose a player; Puck chooses the Baron — the Baron becomes the Sweetheart (evil).
tips: If you're Puck and your team urgently needs to kill an important character, you can choose that character directly.

If you're Puck, you can turn yourself or a teammate into any not-in-play character at any time to gain that character's ability. Turn yourself into the Dreamwalker or the Cyclops to inspect other players! Or become the Minstrel and start drunken-spamming Townsfolk — also a great choice! You can even cosplay your sweetheart the Wish Fairy! So many possibilities! Become the Hellspawn to relocate the Demon! Become the Lady to make someone die in your place! Become the Sweetheart to make others drunk! Become the Perfumer to hand out perfume to good players, then have the Demon claim to be the Perfumer! Become Don Quixote! Become the Cowboy! There are too many ways to play — give your imagination free rein!

If you're Puck and your teammates include the Twin Giants, turning one of the Twin Giants into another character both avoids the Twin Giants' downside and gains another character's ability — killing two birds with one stone.

If you're Puck, although you can't create a Demon directly, if needed you can turn yourself or another Minion into the Hellspawn and use the Hellspawn's ability to relocate the Demon — provided you're sure the Hellspawn isn't in play, or you'll kill him outright.
If you're Puck, turning yourself into the Wish Fairy can also achieve a Demon relocation — or, to be precise, any need at all, as long as you can meet the Storyteller's requirement.

If you're a good player and things like an Outsider claiming to have learned the Cyclops is in play happen without an extra Outsider, or you feel the Twin Giants are in play but can never find which two players they are — consider Puck's presence! Maybe Puck secretly changed some players' characters!
If a critically important Townsfolk dies on day one — especially one who never told anyone their character — consider whether Puck did it!

Because of Puck's existence, you can't fully trust players who have "proven themselves" with their abilities — such as the Perfumer, the Cowboy, the Ranger, the Lady. They might be evil players created by Puck!

Removed when: After announcing the dead player at dawn; the Storyteller may remove it at their convenience.

characters.name: CodeX
characters.ability: Once per game, on your Xth night, choose players X times in total: they are poisoned until dusk. Players chosen multiple times die instead.
characters.lede: CodeX causes mass poisoning — even death — on a single night. The more nights he experiences, the stronger his ability becomes.
characters.quote: Program activated... instructions received. Executing operation on Target #1 once; target is expected to lose consciousness immediately. Executing operation on Target #2 twice; total cellular disintegration of the target is expected.
summaryBullets: A player killed by CodeX is no longer poisoned by CodeX.

"On your Xth night" refers to the number of nights you have been CodeX or possessed CodeX's ability. If a player becomes CodeX or gains CodeX's ability mid-game, that night counts as their first night as CodeX — so if they use CodeX's ability that night, they may only choose once. Subsequent nights follow the same pattern.
CodeX cannot choose Traveller players (the Traveller Exclusion Principle).
howToRun: Each night, wake CodeX. If he shakes his head, put him back to sleep. If he wants to use his ability, let him choose players as many times as the number of nights he has been CodeX tonight. CodeX may distribute his choices freely — he may choose several players once each, choose the same player multiple times, or any other distribution. Mark players chosen once with "Poisoned"; mark players chosen multiple times with "Dead". Then put CodeX back to sleep. Mark a CodeX who has used his ability with the "Ability Used" reminder, and do not wake him on subsequent nights.
examples: On the first night, CodeX chooses the Noble once; the Noble gets false information from being poisoned. CodeX is not woken on subsequent nights.

On the first night, CodeX does not use his ability. On the second night, CodeX chooses the Fortune Teller and the Undertaker once each; both the Fortune Teller and the Undertaker get false information from being poisoned. CodeX is not woken on subsequent nights.

On the first and second nights, CodeX does not use his ability. On the third night, CodeX chooses the Fortune Teller once and the Undertaker twice; the Fortune Teller gets false information from being poisoned, and the Undertaker dies. CodeX is not woken on subsequent nights.

Before the fifth night, CodeX does not use his ability. On the fifth night, CodeX chooses the Fortune Teller once, the Undertaker twice, and the Drunk twice; the Fortune Teller gets false information from being poisoned, and the Undertaker and the Drunk die. CodeX is not woken on subsequent nights.
On the 4th night, Puck turns herself into CodeX, but the Storyteller signals that she may only choose once — because tonight is her first night as CodeX.
tips: The later the game goes, the stronger CodeX's ability becomes. You can use your ability early to intervene in the situation and make an impact, or save it for a decisive blow late in the game.

Early in the game your poisoning ability is critical, but the number of players you can choose is very limited. In the mid-to-late game your poisoning matters less, but you can choose a large number of players. Choosing the best moment to use your ability is the key skill of CodeX.
CodeX needs to spend 2 choices to cause a death. If CodeX kills a player on the second night, no player will be poisoned by CodeX for the entire game.
No matter how CodeX uses his ability, his influence exists on at most one day — find the most likely day and carefully examine that day's information or deaths.

During the first two nights of the game, if CodeX uses his ability to poison players, he cannot cause a death. If you're sure CodeX is in play and no suspicious deaths have occurred, then CodeX must have poisoned players on some night.
A player killed by CodeX definitely wasn't poisoned by CodeX. If you suspect a player was killed by CodeX, they definitely weren't poisoned by CodeX.

Removed when: When the day phase ends, or when CodeX dies or leaves play.

characters.name: Cyclops
characters.ability: Each night, choose a player: you & the Demon learn their character. If an Outsider, they learn the Cyclops is in play. [+1 Outsider]
characters.lede: The Cyclops inspects other players' characters each night.
characters.quote: I've only got one eye, but this eye works real well. Whatever you're doing in your house, I can see it crystal clear from the hilltop. Don't blame me for peeking — my master told me to watch, and I just do as I'm told. That thing you muttered before bed last night? I heard that too — my ears aren't bad either.
summaryBullets: You may deceive a drunk or poisoned Cyclops by giving him wrong character information. But while the Cyclops is drunk or poisoned, he can no longer make the Demon receive the information or make an Outsider learn the Cyclops is in play.

When playing in person, first wake the Cyclops, have him choose and learn the character, and put him back to sleep; then wake the Demon and tell the Demon which player the Cyclops chose and what that player's character is. Do not wake the Cyclops and the Demon at the same time.
If multiple Demons are in play, the Storyteller decides which Demon shares the Cyclops's information.
When the Cyclops chooses an Outsider, immediately after the Cyclops finishes acting, wake that Outsider and tell them the Cyclops is in play.
The Cyclops cannot choose Traveller players (the Traveller Exclusion Principle).
howToRun: During initial setup, before putting character tokens into the bag, replace one Townsfolk character token with one Outsider character token. Each night, wake the Cyclops and have him choose a player; show the Cyclops that player's character token, then put the Cyclops back to sleep. Wake the Demon, show the Demon that player's character token, then point to that player, and put the Demon back to sleep. If the Cyclops chose an Outsider that night, also wake that Outsider, show them the Cyclops character token (or tell them the Cyclops is in play), then put that player back to sleep.
examples: The Cyclops is in play, so there is one more Outsider in play than the default. On the first night, the Cyclops chooses player #1, the Seamstress; the Cyclops and the Demon learn player #1 is the Seamstress. On the first day, the Demon claims to be the Dreamwalker and accurately names player #1 as the Seamstress.
On the first night, the Cyclops chooses player #1, the Recluse; the Cyclops and the Demon learn player #1 is the Recluse. The Recluse learns that the Cyclops is in play.
On the second night, the Cyclops chooses player #1, the Sage; the Cyclops and the Demon learn player #1 is the Sage. That night, the Demon doesn't kill the Sage and chooses another player instead.
tips: Prioritize checking players who seem to be important characters — knowing who the important characters are is key intel.
Prioritize checking the characters of high-skill players; confirming their characters and alignment helps you judge the situation.
Avoid checking suspected Outsiders — that exposes the Cyclops's presence and the Outsider count.

Remember your intel is shared with the Demon — the Demon will use your intel to decide which players to kill. You and the Demon don't even need to communicate much to pull off seamless coordination — that's the strength of your ability.

If the Cyclops isn't in play, you can publicly claim to be an Outsider — even claim to have learned the Cyclops is in play. If the good team really believes the Cyclops is in play, you'll most likely survive to the end. The side effect: if the good players confirm the Cyclops isn't in play, you'll immediately be treated as evil.

If an Outsider claims the Cyclops is in play and the Outsider count exceeds the default, there are only 2 possibilities: either the Cyclops really is in play and the Outsiders are all good (unless the Chimera is in play), or the Outsider claiming the Cyclops is in play is evil and the Cyclops isn't in play.
Watch the Outsider count in play — if it's above default, then even if no Outsider has learned the Cyclops is in play, the Cyclops very likely exists.

characters.name: Ettin
characters.ability: If you die, the other Ettin dies tonight. The Ettins' votes only count if all Ettins vote together. [+1 Ettin (you decide who)]
characters.lede: The Ettin brings an extra Minion to the evil team — they are symbionts who must vote together.
characters.quote: (Solemnly) Giants will never be slaves... (chipping in) Unless food and lodging are included! (Suddenly excited) We're amazing at killing people! (Covering its mouth) Shut up! Say 'carrying out justice'!
summaryBullets: On the first night, the Ettin acts before the Minion and Demon info.
If the Ettin chose a Minion or the Demon, you may shake your head to signal him to choose again.
On the first night, a player chosen by the Ettin's ability becomes an evil Ettin.
If an Ettin is created mid-game, he can no longer turn another player into an Ettin, because the [ ] ability changes the game's initial setup.
As the Storyteller, while multiple Ettins are alive, you should always watch all Ettins' joint voting.

If one Ettin voted and the other didn't, don't deliberately announce that a player's vote wasn't counted or deliberately skip the Ettins when counting. Just count the votes normally and announce the final tally (minus the Ettins' votes). Players must notice on their own whether the announced tally doesn't match the actual number of voters, thereby finding the Ettins' traces. If a player demands to know why the tally doesn't match the number of voters, you only need to answer that you made no mistake.

Players should use existing vote patterns to find out who the Ettins are — they may not force other players to vote to verify who the Ettins are. If players force an Ettin to vote or not vote, or any other behavior forcing the Ettins' votes, you may count the Ettins' votes normally even if only one Ettin votes. (First guide or advise players not to do this, and tell all players they may vote as they wish. If players don't heed the advice, when players force the Ettins' votes you may count the Ettins' votes normally.)
After all Ettins are dead, since the Ettin's ability no longer exists in play, dead Ettins are no longer restricted by the must-vote-together rule.

If, for some reason, one Ettin is alive while the other Ettin is dead: because the Ettin's ability still exists in play, the 2 Ettins (whether alive or dead) still need to vote together for the Storyteller to count their votes. If a dead Ettin votes but isn't counted because the alive Ettin didn't vote, do not take away their vote token.
The Storyteller has no obligation to help players record previous voting rounds. If players want to review votes to find the Ettins, they need to keep their own records.

If 2 Ettins are in play and one Ettin dies, the surviving Ettin also dies at the Ettin's action point that night. But if the already-dead Ettin is drunk or poisoned at that moment, the surviving Ettin doesn't die and won't die from the Ettin's ability on later nights either (the dead Ettin missed the ability trigger point due to being drunk or poisoned). However, the pair of one dead and one alive Ettin are both still restricted by the must-vote-together rule (the surviving Ettin's ability still exists).

If an Ettin leaves play mid-game (turned into another character), the remaining single Ettin's ability no longer does anything (the Ettin's ability is designed around more than one Ettin being in play; with only one Ettin, the ability loses its precondition).

Jinx (Hellspawn & Ettin): If the total number of evil players in play already exceeds the initial setup by one (not counting evil Travellers), the Hellspawn's ability "you immediately turn evil and swap characters with the Demon" is changed to "you immediately swap characters and teams with the Demon".
howToRun: On the first night, wake the Ettin (this happens before the Minion info) and have him point to a player; replace that player's original character token with the Ettin token, then wake that player, show them the "You are" info token and this Ettin token, then show a thumbs-down (they turned evil), then have the 2 Ettins make eye contact. If the Ettin chose a Minion or the Demon, you may have him choose again. Then put them back to sleep.
If an Ettin dies, all other Ettins die that night.
During a vote, if some Ettins voted but not all Ettins voted, subtract the Ettins' votes after counting all votes, then announce the final tally.
examples: On the first night, the Ettin chooses the Seamstress; the Seamstress becomes another evil Ettin, and the two Ettins make eye contact. They are then woken together during the Minion info and learn who the other Minions and the Demon are.
On the first night, the Ettin chooses the Demon or a Minion; to avoid ending the game immediately, the Storyteller shakes their head to prompt the Ettin to choose again.

During a vote, one Ettin raises their hand to vote while the other doesn't. When the Storyteller counts to the last voting player the tally is 8 votes, but they publicly announce that player got 7 votes.
Momo and Yaoyao are both Ettins. Yaoyao is killed by the Demon at night — Momo also dies that night.
One Ettin dies by execution; the other Ettin dies that night.
One Ettin is killed by the Demon at night; the other Ettin also dies that night.

Players force one Ettin to vote while the other Ettin doesn't, to verify whether they are Ettins. The Storyteller's dissuasion fails — one Ettin votes and the other doesn't, but the Storyteller counts the Ettins' votes normally. (See Rule Details for this entry.)
tips: The Ettin in play means the evil team has one extra Minion! That's a huge boost for evil — coordinate well with your "brother"! You bring the evil team extra nomination power and vote advantage; acting as one, you'll seem incredibly strong!

Always watch whether your "brother" voted — keep pace with him. If you split your votes, you expose the Ettins in play, and the good team will very likely find which two players are the Ettins by analyzing the votes.
If you're the Ettin, choose players you think are strong! Making them your "brother" brings enormous help to the evil team!
Although you and your "brother" are of one mind and one heart, most of the time you'd best not act too familiar — that makes it easier to expose you as the Ettins.

If you're the Ettin, living and dying together isn't always bad — a well-timed death can help the evil team achieve special goals! For example, with 5 players left alive, if 2 of them are Ettins, that day will be the final day! Whether one Ettin dies by execution or the Demon kills one Ettin at night, only 2 alive players will remain when the next day comes — meaning the game is over. Besides that, you can also die at the right time to bluff as the Gambler, or help a teammate bluff as the Lady/Ranger — characters that can cause extra deaths.
If, in a vote, the tally the Storyteller announces doesn't match the actual number of voters, then one of the voting players must be an Ettin! And among the non-voting players is the other Ettin!
If you suspect the Ettins are in play, they must be among two players who always vote together or always abstain together!
Don't force other players to vote or not vote to verify whether they're the Ettins! In that situation, the Storyteller counts the Ettins' votes normally!

When one Ettin dies, the other dies that night! If you suspect a player is an Ettin, the best move is to try to execute him! If an execution triggers an abnormal night death, another Ettin is very likely among that night's dead players.
In most cases, the Ettin turns a Townsfolk or Outsider into another Ettin at game start. If the Outsider count in play doesn't match the default, consider this possibility!
