characters.tags: Drunkenness, Poison, Setup, Social, You Start Knowing

customBoxes.title: Reminder Tokens
customBoxes.content:
[[Hammered!]]
Placed when: While preparing for the first night.
Condition: By any player's character token.
Removed when: The Cat Chorus dies or leaves play.

[[Hyped Up!]]
Placed when: At dusk.
Condition: When the song you named is sung successfully.
Removed when: At dusk.

customBoxes.title: Design Notes
customBoxes.content:
The Cat Chorus is part of the Cat series — a bold, innovative character set themed around social interaction.

The Cat series encourages social behavior, with emphasis on caring for dead players and players of weaker, marginal characters.

The Cat Chorus suits high-interaction scripts emphasizing party and entertainment, getting every player involved and quickly heating up the atmosphere.

As an Outsider, the Cat Chorus's negative effect is one player drunk; its positive effect is guaranteeing one night free of poison/drunkenness for all Townsfolk. So is the Cat Chorus Outsider-strength? The key is who holds the trigger. The Storyteller controls the trigger, ensuring the Cat Chorus can't bring huge positive swings on evil's critical nights and decide the game.

characters.callout: The Cat Chorus's ability only suspends poison and drunkenness — it does not cure them, and it does not affect other forms of interference like the Vortox's false information.

characters.name: Beekeeper
characters.ability: A player is poisoned, even after you die. Each night*, choose a player: if they are poisoned by you, they become healthy.
characters.lede: The Beekeeper poisons a player, but can also cure them.
characters.quote: I'm terribly sorry — these naughty little ones have hurt you. This is honey from my own hives; a dab of it will bring the swelling and pain right down. Please, do accept it.
summaryBullets: Note: the Beekeeper's night-order slot is before the vast majority of characters. Check the script's night-order sheet for details.
Any player can be poisoned by the Beekeeper, including Outsiders, Minions, and even the Demon. But most of the time, you should poison a Townsfolk.

If the Beekeeper dies without ever choosing the player poisoned by him, that player does not recover. A dead Beekeeper loses the ability to choose players. If the Beekeeper dies having already chosen the poisoned player, that player is not re-poisoned.
If the Beekeeper is poisoned or drunk when choosing the player poisoned by him, then even if the Beekeeper later recovers, that player is not poisoned by him again.
The Beekeeper cannot learn whether he chose the poisoned player. Even after choosing them, the Beekeeper must keep choosing on later nights.
If several Beekeepers are in play (simultaneously or successively), each Beekeeper's ability is independent and they don't interfere with each other.
If every player has been chosen by the Beekeeper, the Beekeeper no longer needs waking.
The Beekeeper does not poison Traveller players (Traveller Exclusion Principle).
howToRun: While preparing for the first night, choose any player and place the Beekeeper's "Poisoned" reminder by their character token — that player is poisoned.

Each night except the first, wake the Beekeeper. Let the Beekeeper point at any player. If that player is poisoned by the Beekeeper, they become healthy — remove their "Poisoned" reminder. Put the Beekeeper back to sleep.
examples: The Noble is poisoned by the Beekeeper. On the first night, the Noble gets false information. On the second night, the Beekeeper chooses the Noble; the Noble becomes healthy.

The Fortune Teller is poisoned by the Beekeeper. On the first and second nights, the Fortune Teller gets false information. On the third night, the Beekeeper chooses the Fortune Teller; the Fortune Teller becomes healthy and gets correct information.
tips: If you're the Beekeeper and you think some important Townsfolk is poisoned by you, choose them. Whether or not they were poisoned by you before, after you choose them they definitely won't be poisoned by you anymore.
If you're the Beekeeper, don't choose Townsfolk who've already used their ability — choose the ones still actively functioning.
bluffing: The Beekeeper poisons a player, usually a Townsfolk. If you can't explain some Townsfolk's information, you can claim to be the Beekeeper and say they were poisoned by your ability.
characters.creator: Taiyi
characters.otherNightReminder: Wake him and let him choose a player.

customBoxes.title: Reminder Tokens
customBoxes.content:
[[Poisoned]]
Placed when: While preparing for the first night.
Condition: Place it by a player's character token.
Removed when: The Beekeeper leaves play, or the poisoned player is chosen by the Beekeeper.

customBoxes.title: Design Notes
customBoxes.content:
Compared to the Truelove's after-the-fact drunkenness, the Beekeeper is a drunkenness-first design.

The Beekeeper's design encourages surviving as long as possible, guessing and undoing the harm he caused.

The Beekeeper guarantees at least one first-night poison.

characters.name: Hekatonkheires
characters.ability: If you die by execution, you may publicly declare you are the Hekatonkheires: your next vote counts as today's votes on you.
characters.quote: The blood of the Hundred-Handed never yields! Every shard that executes me becomes another arm lifting my boulder. I will smash through your hypocrisy, though it be hard as the walls of Troy.
summaryBullets: If the Hekatonkheires doesn't publicly declare he is the Hekatonkheires immediately after dying by execution, his ability cannot trigger normally. Generally, any public declaration within two minutes of the Hekatonkheires dying by execution counts as a valid declaration.

If a player who is not the Hekatonkheires publicly declares they are the Hekatonkheires after dying by execution, you must also play along and respond to them as you would a real Hekatonkheires — even though they don't have the Hekatonkheires's ability.
A Hekatonkheires who dies from causes other than execution cannot trigger his ability.

If the Hekatonkheires dies from an abnormal execution (e.g., the Cerenovus), the Hekatonkheires can still publicly declare. His vote count equals the votes he received when nominated that day. If the Hekatonkheires wasn't nominated that day or received no votes, his next vote counts as 0 votes.

When the Hekatonkheires votes after gaining his ability, the Storyteller must directly state the current cumulative total when counting to the Hekatonkheires's vote. For example: "1 vote" (pointing to a voting player), "2 votes" (pointing to the previous voting player), "13 votes" (pointing to the Hekatonkheires), "14 votes" (pointing to the next voting player).
howToRun: If the Hekatonkheires dies by execution and immediately publicly declares he is the Hekatonkheires, place the "Revenge" reminder by the Hekatonkheires's character token and note down the number of votes he received that day.
The next time the Hekatonkheires votes (usually using his vote token), his vote counts as the number of votes noted down on the day he died by execution.
examples: The Hekatonkheires gets 12 votes on day one and dies by execution, and immediately upon learning he died, publicly declares he is the Hekatonkheires. On the final day, the Hekatonkheires uses his vote token to vote; when the Storyteller counts to the Hekatonkheires, his vote counts as 12 votes. That day a good player gets 14 votes in total and dies by execution — the evil team wins.

The Hekatonkheires gets 12 votes on day one and dies by execution, but he doesn't publicly declare he is the Hekatonkheires. On the final day, the Hekatonkheires uses his vote token to vote; when the Storyteller counts to the Hekatonkheires, his vote counts as 1 vote normally.

The Hekatonkheires gets 4 votes on day four and dies by execution, and immediately upon learning he died, publicly declares he is the Hekatonkheires. The next day, the Hekatonkheires uses his vote token to vote; when the Storyteller counts to the Hekatonkheires, his vote counts as 4 votes.
tips: If you're the Hekatonkheires, rack your brains to die by execution early.
If you're the Hekatonkheires, bluff as absurdly as you can. If the good players see through your bluff and execute you — wonderful. If they don't see through it — the bluff succeeded too.

If you're the Hekatonkheires, think carefully about whether to publicly declare you are the Hekatonkheires. Generally, early in the game, if you've received enough votes to dominate an execution, you can declare without hesitation. In the mid-to-late game, if declaring would only bank you 3 or 4 votes, you need to carefully consider whether it's worth it — because publicly declaring definitely exposes you as an evil player, which is usually harmful to the evil team.

If you're another Minion, sometimes declaring you're the Hekatonkheires when you die by execution is also a viable tactic. Although you can't actually gain the Hekatonkheires's ability, it makes the good team deeply wary of you — especially if you received a large number of votes.
If you're a good player, if nobody declares they're the Hekatonkheires after dying by execution, the Hekatonkheires's ability definitely won't trigger.

If you're a good player and someone declares they're the Hekatonkheires after dying by execution, remember the votes they received that day. If they're really the Hekatonkheires, that means the evil team can add those votes to any execution on any day at any time — actively prepare and respond.
characters.creator: Taiyi

customBoxes.title: Reminder Tokens
customBoxes.content:
[[Revenge]]
Placed when: When the Hekatonkheires publicly declares he is the Hekatonkheires.
Condition: If the Hekatonkheires declares he is the Hekatonkheires immediately after dying by execution, place it by the Hekatonkheires's character token.
Removed when: After the Hekatonkheires votes, or when he leaves play.

customBoxes.title: Design Notes
customBoxes.content:
An extremely powerful execution-punishment Minion (a "landmine" Minion).

The "public declaration" element was added, first to give the good team time and room to counter, and second to give other evil players who aren't the Hekatonkheires room to exploit.

characters.name: Skeleton King
characters.ability: Each night*, choose a player: they die. If your team wins, Townsfolk who gave up their vote tokens also win. [+1 Outsider]
characters.lede: The Skeleton King leads the surrendered Townsfolk to victory alongside him.
characters.quote: My patience is shorter than your life. Last chance — bow your head, offer your loyalty, and I shall grant you the right to press your knees to the ground. My throne never lacks kneeling men; it lacks men clever enough. Your bones look hard enough, but I've seen harder — ground to dust, all of them. One last time: yield, or shatter?
summaryBullets: Vote token: the voting indicator a player gets upon death. A player receives one vote token after dying. A dead player may only vote using their vote token. Whether each player has vote tokens, and how many, is public information anyone can check.

Giving up vote tokens: during the day, to trigger a certain character's ability, a dead player publicly chooses that character and gives the vote tokens they hold to the Storyteller — that player loses all vote tokens they hold. A player without vote tokens cannot give up vote tokens. Giving up vote tokens is public, visible to all players, and can only be done during the day. As long as a character with a give-up-vote-tokens ability exists in the script, players may publicly choose that character and give up vote tokens — even if that character isn't in play.

Winning by the normal condition: winning through non-special-victory means by meeting the normal win condition. In the context of the Skeleton King's ability, this means winning by having only two players left alive — including early-victory methods such as all alive players being evil, since those methods essentially fast-forward the game to the "only two alive players" win condition.
The Skeleton King's second ability only takes effect when the Skeleton King wins. So if the Skeleton King loses, Townsfolk who gave up vote tokens don't lose alongside him because of his ability.

"When you win" refers to the moment the Skeleton King is confirmed to have won. If abilities such as win/loss-result swaps haven't resolved yet, resolve those first; after confirming the Skeleton King has won, then resolve the Skeleton King's ability effect.
The Skeleton King's ability cannot choose Traveller players (the Traveller Exclusion Principle).
howToRun: During initial setup, before putting character tokens into the bag, replace one Townsfolk character token with one Outsider character token.
Each night except the first, wake the Skeleton King. Have him point to any player. That player dies — mark them with the "Dead" reminder. Put the Skeleton King back to sleep.

If a player holding vote tokens publicly surrenders to the Skeleton King, take away all their vote tokens. (This is a universal game action — even if the Skeleton King isn't in play, you handle it the same way.)
When the Skeleton King wins, announce that all Townsfolk who gave up their vote tokens also win.
examples: Because the Demon is the Skeleton King, there are 3 Outsiders in play — one more than the default 2.

On the fifth day, the dead Dreamwalker and Washerwoman — who still hold vote tokens — publicly surrender to the Skeleton King and give up their vote tokens. That day the Fortune Teller is executed, leaving only the Skeleton King and the Tailor alive. The evil team wins — the Dreamwalker and the Washerwoman also win.

On the final day, all dead Townsfolk publicly surrender to the Skeleton King and give up their vote tokens. The evil team wins, and thanks to the Skeleton King's ability, the dead Townsfolk who gave up their vote tokens win alongside them.
tips: If the Skeleton King is in play, a Townsfolk is guaranteed victory simply by giving up their vote tokens — an enormous temptation for Townsfolk players. So whether or not the in-play Demon is the Skeleton King, convincing dead Townsfolk that the Demon is the Skeleton King so they raise their hands in surrender gives evil a huge advantage — Townsfolk who gave up vote tokens definitely won't join the final day's vote.
The Skeleton King increases the Outsider count — you or a teammate bluffing as an Outsider is a fine way to fake the Skeleton King's presence.
If you're the Skeleton King, you can send Minions to loudly proclaim the in-play Demon is the Skeleton King — this splits the good team with ease.

If you're the Skeleton King, keeping most Outsiders alive into the late game is an extremely favorable situation. Dead Townsfolk are always wavering; if only Outsiders survive, they're the only ones who'll unite against you.
If you're a Townsfolk who believes the in-play Demon is the Skeleton King and you've survived to the final day, persuading the other dead players to vote is your most important job.
Outsiders aren't affected by the Skeleton King's ability — Outsiders are the key force resisting the Skeleton King. Winning their support gives you a major advantage against him.
Dead Townsfolk can't be trusted — even if the Demon isn't the Skeleton King, they might be deceived into sitting out the final day's vote.

In a 12-player game with the Skeleton King in play, there's generally 1 Demon, 2 Minions, and 3 Outsiders. Even if every Townsfolk dies, good only needs to win one dead Townsfolk's vote to execute the Skeleton King on the final day. So don't over-fear the Skeleton King — persuading the wavering dead Townsfolk is the key.
characters.creator: Taiyi
characters.otherNightReminder: Have him choose a player.

customBoxes.title: Reminder Tokens
customBoxes.content:
[[Dead]]
Placed when: After the Skeleton King acts at night and chooses a player.
Condition: The player the Skeleton King chose is currently alive, can be killed by the Skeleton King, and the Skeleton King is not drunk or poisoned — place it by that player's character token to remind the Storyteller to announce that night's dead player at dawn.
Removed when: After announcing the dead player at dawn; the Storyteller may remove it at their convenience.

[[Surrender" ×4]]
Placed when: After a player holding vote tokens gives up their vote tokens.
Condition: During the day, after a Townsfolk holding vote tokens publicly hands them in, take away all their vote tokens and place the "Surrender" reminder by that Townsfolk's character token.
Removed when: The Skeleton King dies or leaves play.

characters.name: Skipper
characters.ability: Each night*, learn if the Demon is clockwise or anti-clockwise of the executee. If an evil player was executed, you are drunk until dawn.
characters.lede: The Skipper closes in on the Demon through executions.
characters.quote: An offering to Poseidon will turn my compass toward the Demon's hiding place — clockwise or anti-clockwise, clearer than any chart. The price of sacrificing a traitor is a cup of bitter divine wine. Lads, remember to wake me before dawn!
summaryBullets: "Left" and "right" in the Skipper's information refer to the executed player facing the center of the circle of players — their left-hand side or right-hand side.

If the number of players seated between the player executed today and the Demon is smaller on the left than on the right, the Skipper learns "left." If smaller on the right, the Skipper learns "right." If both sides are equal, the Storyteller decides whether to give "left" or "right."
The Skipper's ability counts all players (except Travellers) seated between the executed player and the Demon, including dead players.
If nobody was executed that day, the Skipper is not woken. If several players were executed the same day, the Skipper's ability uses the last executed player.
If several Demons are in play, the Storyteller decides which Demon the Skipper's ability locates.
The Skipper's ability ignores Traveller players (Traveller Exclusion Principle).
Information format: "left" or "right." In in-person games, the Storyteller may raise their clockwise or anti-clockwise hand to indicate "left" or "right."

False information format: when "left" is the correct information, "right" is false; when "right" is correct, "left" is false. If both sides are equal, both "left" and "right" count as false information.
howToRun: Each night except the first, wake the Skipper. If the number of players seated between the player executed today (the offering) and the Demon is smaller on the left than on the right, tell the Skipper "left" (or raise your left hand). If smaller on the right than on the left, tell the Skipper "right" (or raise your right hand). If both sides are equal, the Storyteller decides whether to give "left" or "right."

When a player is executed, place the "Offering" reminder by the executed player's character token. When an evil player is executed, place the "Drunk" reminder by the Skipper's character token. At dawn, remove all "Drunk" and "Offering" reminders first.
examples: On the first day, a good player is executed. The number of players seated between this player and the Demon is smaller on the left than on the right. That night, the Skipper learns "left."

On the first day, an evil player is executed and the Skipper is drunk. The number of players seated between this player and the Demon is smaller on the left than on the right. That night, the Skipper learns "right."
On the first day, a good player is executed. The number of players seated between this player and the Demon is equal on both sides. That night, the Skipper learns "left."

On the third day, a good player is executed. There is one dead Demon and one living Demon in play. The dead Demon is nearer the executed player's left; the living Demon is nearer the executed player's right. That night, the Skipper learns "right," because the Storyteller chose the living Demon as the Demon the Skipper's ability locates.
On the third day, nobody was executed. That night, the Skipper is not woken.
tips: If you're the Skipper, each piece of information lets you eliminate roughly half the players from being the Demon. Compare your information across nights and hunt the Demon among the players hit multiple times.

If you're the Skipper, you must "sacrifice" good players for Poseidon to guide you — otherwise, drunk, your information is meaningless. So if you think the executed player was evil, that night's information is worthless. Conversely, if your information one night is clearly wrong, the player executed that day was very likely evil.
If you're the Skipper and you execute neighboring players in a row, your information narrows very slowly. Executing players far from the previously executed player locates the Demon much faster.
If you're the Demon, the Skipper's information is very powerful — deal with him quickly. If you can't kill the Skipper yet, send evil players to be executed; that disrupts his ability well.

If you're the Demon, push everyone to execute players neighboring the last executed player, so the Skipper's information becomes low-value. Keep track of your own position relative to each day's executed player to avoid being found too quickly.
bluffing: To bluff as the Skipper, keep your information internally consistent. If your first report says "the Demon is among the left half" and your second says "the Demon is among the right half," your credibility as the Skipper collapses.
Claim to be the Skipper and offer opinions about whom to execute, claiming that following your advice finds the Demon faster.
characters.creator: Taiyi
characters.otherNightReminder: Tell him clockwise or anti-clockwise.

customBoxes.title: Reminder Tokens
customBoxes.content:
[[Offering]]
Placed when: When a player is executed.
Condition: Place it by the executed player's character token.
Removed when: At dawn, or when the Skipper dies or leaves play.

[[Drunk]]
Placed when: When an evil player is executed.
Condition: Place it by the Skipper's character token.
Removed when: At dawn, or when the Skipper dies or leaves play.

characters.name: Medium
characters.ability: If a Townsfolk you nominated dies by execution, they learn that night that the Medium is in play.
characters.lede: Townsfolk learn that they died at the Medium's hands.
characters.quote: I don't like talking, but the dead do.
summaryBullets: If a Townsfolk is changed into another character after dying by an execution nominated by the Medium, they still learn the Medium is in play that night. (Whether to tell them is judged by whether the token was placed.)
If the Medium is poisoned or drunk at night, the Townsfolk who was nominated by them and died by execution does not learn the Medium is in play.
If the Medium was poisoned or drunk during the day but is sober and healthy by night, the Townsfolk who was nominated by them and died by execution still learns the Medium is in play.
Information format: "The Medium is in play," or show the woken player the Medium character token.
False information format: this character has no false information format (per the official "general simplification principle"). The Vortox and similar characters do not affect the Medium's ability.
howToRun: When a Townsfolk dies by execution, if the player who nominated that Townsfolk today is the Medium, place the "Learn" reminder by that Townsfolk's character token.
That night, wake that Townsfolk and tell them the Medium is in play. Then remove the "Learn" reminder.
examples: On the first day, the Medium nominates the Noble, who dies by execution that day. That night, the Noble is woken and learns the Medium is in play.
On the second day, the Medium nominates the Butler, who dies by execution that day. That night, the Butler is not woken.
On the third day, the Medium nominates the Baron, who dies by execution that day. That night, the Baron is not woken.
On the fourth day, the Medium nominates the Fortune Teller, who dies by execution that day. That night, the Medium is dead, and the Fortune Teller is not woken.
tips: If you're the Medium, fight to nominate and execute other players — but preferably without revealing that you're the Medium. If the player you executed says they learned the Medium is in play, they're very likely a Townsfolk. If they deny learning it, they're very likely not a Townsfolk.

If you're the Medium, you can ask everyone to let you nominate to prove you're really the Medium. But make sure the player you execute is a Townsfolk — otherwise they won't learn the Medium is in play.

If you learned the Medium is in play at night, you can be sure the player who nominated and executed you is the Medium. Don't announce it; confer secretly with the Medium player. The next time a Townsfolk the Medium nominates and executes doesn't know — or denies — that the Medium is in play, you two can join forces to confirm they're very likely an evil player!
bluffing: Bluff as the Medium and nominate executions: the other side will inevitably deny learning the Medium is in play, and you attack them as an evil player.
Bluff as the Medium, nominate and execute your teammate, and cover for each other, faking a Medium-and-Townsfolk pair.
characters.creator: Taiyi
characters.otherNightReminder: If the 'Learn' reminder was placed, wake the player marked 'Learn' and tell them the Medium is in play.

customBoxes.title: Reminder Tokens
customBoxes.content:
[[Learn]]
Placed when: When a Townsfolk dies by an execution nominated by the Medium.
Condition: A Townsfolk died by execution and the nominator was the Medium; place it by that Townsfolk's character token.
Removed when: After a player learns the Medium is in play, or at dawn.

customBoxes.title: Design Notes
customBoxes.content:
A character themed around the nomination protagonist.

A Perfumer variant.

A strong functional character for mutual confirmation and creating opposition.

The evil team has ample counterplay and room for maneuver.

characters.name: Miko
characters.ability: Each night, choose 2 players that neighbor each other (not yourself): you learn if either of them is a Minion.
characters.lede: The Miko can check whether players are Minions.
characters.quote: The ancient tree before the shrine told me something filthy has mixed into the town. I'll do for the tree what it cannot — sink my roots into the soil, pull the evil out, and return it to the clear breeze. Don't worry, it won't hurt. A purified soul will smell plum blossom on the wind.
summaryBullets: The Miko cannot choose herself, and can only choose two players sitting next to each other.
The Miko may choose dead players, and the "neighboring" requirement does not skip dead players.
If at least one of the Miko's chosen players is a Minion, she learns "yes." If neither is a Minion, she learns "no."
If the Miko chooses herself or two players not sitting next to each other, have her choose again.
The Miko's ability cannot choose Travellers, and the "neighboring" requirement of her ability skips Travellers (Traveller Exclusion Principle).
Information format: "yes" or "no."
False information format: "yes" or "no" (opposite to the truth).
howToRun: Each night, wake the Miko. Let the Miko point at two players sitting next to each other, not including herself. If either of the two players is a Minion, nod to the Miko for "yes." Otherwise, shake your head for "no." Put the Miko back to sleep.
examples: On the first night, the Miko chooses the Fortune Teller and the Baron, who sit next to each other, and learns "yes."
On the second night, the Miko chooses the Saint and the Imp, who sit next to each other, and learns "no."
tips: If you're the Miko, your ability can quickly locate Minions or rule players out. If you learn "no," both chosen players are definitely not Minions. If you learn "yes," at least one of them is a Minion.
If you're the Miko and you learned "yes," you can pin down exactly which player is the Minion by repeatedly choosing overlapping pairs.
If you're the Miko, your ability cannot verify the Demon or other kinds of evil players — a player you verified as not a Minion isn't necessarily good.

If you're a Minion and the Miko attacks you as possibly the Minion she checked, note that she can't pinpoint which of the pair it was in short order. Use this to attack the other player sitting next to you as the Minion instead.

If you're a Minion whose character isn't that important, deliberately jumping out to be checked at the right moment — drawing everyone's attention — is a vital technique, especially when the good team's eyes are fixed near the Demon.
bluffing: Report that two players hostile to each other include a Minion, let them attack each other, and reap the profits!
In the mid-to-late game, report that a pair including the Demon contains a Minion — this may make the good team think the Demon is a Minion and choose not to execute them. This is risky, though.
Reporting that players are not Minions brings you closer to them. But if you never find a Minion, players will question whether you're real.
characters.creator: Taiyi
characters.firstNightReminder: Let her choose two neighboring players other than herself.
characters.otherNightReminder: Let her choose two neighboring players other than herself.

customBoxes.title: Design Notes
customBoxes.content: A benchmark-template character.

characters.name: Sensate
characters.ability: Each night, the Demon chooses an alive player (not you): you & the Demon learn their character.
characters.lede: The Sensate "shares vision" with the Demon, seeing what the Demon sees.
characters.quote: The vision of darkness — I've accepted it on behalf of the light. I am no prophet; I make no prophecies. I merely borrow the Demon's eyes to expose his tricks and send him on his way.
summaryBullets: The Sensate's ability makes the Demon and the Sensate learn "who" is what "character," so you cannot simply give the Sensate a character alone. See the information format below.

If the Demon chose an ineligible player (a dead player, the Sensate, a Traveller), have the Demon choose again. The Sensate only learns the player the Demon finally chose and their character — not how many choices the Demon made.
If for some reason the Demon cannot choose, or no Demon is in play, the Storyteller chooses on their behalf.
If several Demons are in play, the Storyteller chooses one of them to perform the Sensate's ability — generally a living evil Demon takes priority.
If the Sensate is poisoned or drunk, the Demon is not woken. The Storyteller decides which player and character to tell the Sensate; it may be true or false.

The Sensate and the Demon always learn the same information, even false information. For example, if the Vortox chooses #1 the Fortune Teller and learns #1 is the Scarlet Woman, the Sensate also learns #1 is the Scarlet Woman.
The Demon cannot choose Travellers (Traveller Exclusion Principle).
Information format: player + character (e.g., "#1 Fortune Teller" or "May Scarlet Woman").
False information format: player + character (a character that is not that player's character; e.g., #1 is the Fortune Teller, but the Demon and the Sensate learn "#1 Scarlet Woman").
howToRun: Each night, wake the Demon and show them, in turn, the "This character's ability affected you" info token and the Sensate's character token, and let them choose a player. If the Demon chose a dead player or the Sensate, shake your head and have them choose again. Once the Demon has chosen a player, show them that player's character token. Put the Demon to sleep. Wake the Sensate, point at the player the Demon chose, and show that player's character token. Put the Sensate to sleep.
examples: On the first night, the Demon uses the Sensate's ability to choose player #1 (the Sensate); the Storyteller shakes their head and has the Demon choose again, because the Sensate's ability cannot choose the Sensate. The Demon chooses player #2 (the Chambermaid); the Demon learns #2 is the Chambermaid; the Storyteller puts the Demon to sleep and wakes the Sensate, who learns #2 is the Chambermaid.

On the first night, the Demon uses the Sensate's ability to choose player #2 (the Chambermaid); the Demon learns #2 is the Chambermaid, and the Sensate learns #2 is the Chambermaid. On the second night, #2 is still alive; the Demon chooses #2 again; both learn #2 is the Chambermaid. On the third night, player #2 is dead; the Demon chooses #2, and the Storyteller shakes their head because the Sensate's ability cannot choose dead players. The Demon chooses player #3 (the Fortune Teller); the Demon learns #3 is the Fortune Teller, and the Sensate learns #3 is the Fortune Teller.
tips: If you're the Sensate, remember: the information you get is also what the Demon gets! The player you see is the player the Demon chose to show you! So hiding your information is mostly pointless — but hiding that you're the Sensate, so the Demon doesn't find and kill you too early, is worth something.

If you're the Sensate and a player claims to be the Sensate and correctly reports other players' characters — especially matching what you learned — they're an evil player: possibly the Demon, possibly a Minion the Demon sent. Since they've claimed to be the Sensate, a jump-for-jump brawl between you is unavoidable.
If you're the Sensate, you can execute the players you learn to force the Demon to choose new living players, gaining you new information.

If you're the Sensate, the Demon will generally choose to show you a player as some good character. If you learn a player is an evil character, think hard. Why would the Demon deliberately expose an evil player to you? Are you poisoned? Is the Demon in play the Vortox? Or is this a Demon plot to induce you to execute someone?
If you're the Demon, choosing the same living player night after night maximally restricts the Sensate's information, keeping them from gaining too much too fast.
If you're the Demon and you chose a living player but the Storyteller shook their head and made you re-choose, that player is the Sensate. If needed, you can kill them the next night.
If you're the Demon, choosing a Minion — or even a Demon — at the right moment throws the Sensate into doubt and disrupts the good team's execution decisions, provided you have a complete evil plan.
If you're the Demon and the player you previously chose has died, preferably choose players everyone already accepts as good — this keeps as many players as possible under suspicion of being evil.

If you're the Demon, you can send a Minion to claim the Sensate and privately verify characters with the players you've learned. This wins their trust in the short term. But the real Sensate will jump out eventually, and two Sensates can't avoid a true-or-fake battle.
bluffing: If the Demon was never woken because of the Sensate's ability, no Sensate is in play, and you can safely use the Sensate as an extra bluff.
The key prerequisite for bluffing as the Sensate is correctly reporting players' characters — especially players who haven't revealed. Get it wrong and you may be suspected immediately.

To keep the Sensate from gaining too much information, the Demon mostly chooses the same player for the first few days unless that player has died. Note this: as the Sensate, what you learn should always be living players' characters.
characters.creator: Taiyi, 黑猫 (Black Cat)
characters.firstNightReminder: Wake the Demon to choose a player and tell the Demon what character they are. Put the Demon to sleep, then wake the Sensate and tell them what character that player is.
characters.otherNightReminder: Wake the Demon to choose a player and tell the Demon what character they are. Put the Demon to sleep, then wake the Sensate and tell them what character that player is.

customBoxes.title: Design Notes
customBoxes.content:
The Sensate is an excellent exemplar of interactive design, achieving multiple design goals in a single short sentence. First, learning one player's character each night is an overpowered effect even as a one-shot check (compare the Ravenkeeper). But the Sensate hands the choice to the Demon, who can keep choosing the same living player to limit what the Sensate learns. Meanwhile the Sensate can execute learned players to force the Demon to choose new ones — highly interactive and strategic, while capping the ability's strength. Second, sharing vision with the Demon (both learn the information) avoids the fixed "Dreamer checks someone day one; matched Dreamer is confirmed good" routine, further lowering the ability's ceiling while giving the evil team more information and room to maneuver. It also fits the "Sensate" (super-sense, shared senses) concept perfectly.

The official character most similar to the Sensate is the King. The Sensate shares many traits with the King: both are exposed to the Demon, both involve strategy against the Demon, both learn living characters. But the King plus Choirboy is two characters, and the pair's biggest impression is that they're blank slates in practice. The Sensate achieves most of the King's design goals with a single character and a very lean ability text. The Sensate's floor is at least a "Washerwoman," and the shared-information form breaks the monotonous "you learn X is X" exposure pattern of the King — many functions in one sentence.

characters.name: Blood Thief
characters.ability: Before the final day, when the only alive evil player dies, you become their character & alignment.
characters.lede: The Blood Thief takes over the game when all of evil falls.
characters.quote: The muddled Demon, the witless Minions — the farce that fumbled the victory is over. Now, watch closely: the one-of-a-kind reversal!
summaryBullets: "The final day": the first day on which fewer than 5 players are alive (Travellers not counted). On the final day, the Storyteller publicly announces at the first opportunity that today is the final day. A game has at most one "final day"; if the game doesn't end on the final day, later days with fewer than 5 alive players are not treated as the "final day". If the game ends early (e.g., a special victory or the Demon's death), the game may have no "final day" at all. Before the final day arrives: the period before the final day. When the final day arrives: the moment the final day begins (usually the first dawn with fewer than 5 non-Traveller alive players). After the final day arrives: the final day and everything after.
The Blood Thief's ability can only trigger when the last living evil player dies. If more than one evil player is alive, the Blood Thief's ability doesn't trigger.

If five or more players were alive before the last evil player's death — that is, if four or more players remain alive after it — the Blood Thief immediately becomes that evil player's character and team; if the Blood Thief becomes a Demon, the game continues as if the Demon hadn't died.
The Blood Thief's ability ignores Travellers (Traveller Exclusion Principle).
howToRun: When the only living evil player dies, if the final day has not yet arrived, replace the Blood Thief's character token and team with that evil player's character token and team. That night, wake the former Blood Thief and show them, in turn, the "You are" info token, a thumbs-down, and their new character token.
examples: On the first day, the Imp dies by execution, but the Imp is not the only living evil player. The game ends; good wins.
It is the final day, and the Imp is the only living evil player. That day the Imp dies by execution; the game ends; good wins.
Only 5 players remain alive, and the Imp is the only living evil player among them. That day the Imp dies by execution; the Blood Thief becomes the evil Imp.
On the third night, 7 players remain alive, and the Vortox is the only living evil player among them. That night the Vortox kills themself; the Blood Thief becomes the evil Vortox.
tips: If you're the Blood Thief, you can generally only become an evil player (usually the Demon) in the mid-to-late game. If you don't want to become the Demon, get yourself killed — then you definitely never will.

If you're the Blood Thief, reveal your character cautiously. If you fail to die in the early-to-mid game, you might become the new Demon at any time later. If you've already told other players you're the Blood Thief by then, you're easily executed — even if you never actually became the Demon.

If you're the Blood Thief and it's already the final day without you changing character, the Demon is still alive in play and you've missed the last train to evil. If you did anything that hurt the town's reasoning, reveal your character and explain your behavior.
If you're the Blood Thief and you've become an evil player (usually the Demon), all evil players are dead and you're the only living evil player left — fight for yourself.
If you're an evil player, working out whether a Blood Thief is in play matters a lot. The Blood Thief gives the evil team a powerful safety net.

If you're a Minion and you've figured out who the Blood Thief is, do everything to keep them from revealing their character. You can even "swap characters" — each claiming the other's. Then at a convenient moment you can claim the Blood Thief identity and court death, laying groundwork for the Blood Thief becoming the Demon.

If you're the Demon and you want the Blood Thief to become the new Demon, remember: you must be the last evil player to die. If other evil players haven't died in time, you can help them when necessary — kill them yourself at night.

If you're the Demon, executing yourself to make the Blood Thief the new Demon may be a bit obvious. When needed, you can also kill yourself so the Blood Thief succeeds you — provided, of course, you're already the last living evil player.
bluffing: Blood Thieves rarely reveal themselves. Revealing yourself as the Blood Thief early gets you executed very easily — though if you're a Minion eager to die, that's a fine approach.

Revealing yourself as the Blood Thief in the mid-to-late game — especially on the final day — confuses the good team enormously. They can't tell whether you're a Blood Thief who became the Demon, a Blood Thief who didn't, or even a Minion posing as the Blood Thief.
characters.creator: Taiyi

customBoxes.title: Reminder Tokens
customBoxes.content:
[[Is the Demon]]
Placed when: When the Blood Thief becomes a Demon through their own ability.
Condition: When the Blood Thief becomes a Demon, place it by the Blood Thief's character token.
Removed when: The Demon character the Blood Thief became leaves play.

customBoxes.title: Design Notes
customBoxes.content:
As a turn-evil + Demon-relocating Outsider, the Blood Thief's side effect is enormous; correspondingly, the conditions are strict. The Blood Thief becoming the Demon means he's the only evil player left. In scripts where evil lacks survival tools, he gives the evil team an excellent safety net.

As a "hidden" Outsider, the Blood Thief either reveals early and courts death, or reveals on the final day to clear his name. Likewise, a Minion may claim to be the Blood Thief and court death to trigger the ability. So the Blood Thief is a "hidden" Outsider with no fixed script — and not all that hidden, either.

characters.name: Two-Face
characters.ability: Each night*, you change to the alignment opposing the last player who died by execution.
characters.lede: Two-Face keeps shifting allegiance between the poles of good and evil.
characters.quote: One thought of good, and the heart knows no bounds. One thought of evil, and the square inch imprisons itself. One thought arising, good and evil beget each other. One thought fallen, mortal and saint are both forgot.
summaryBullets: If Two-Face dies, they lose their ability. A dead Two-Face no longer changes team from their own ability.
You may wake Two-Face every night and tell them their current team, or only wake and tell them on nights when their team changes.

If Two-Face is poisoned or drunk, Two-Face does not change team, but the Storyteller may wake them at night and deceive them that their team changed. If you deceived them while they were poisoned or drunk, you must tell them their actual team on a night after they are sober and healthy again.
howToRun: On nights except the first, if Two-Face is on the same team as the last player who died by execution, wake Two-Face: if Two-Face is currently good, tell them they have turned evil; if currently evil, tell them they have turned good. If Two-Face is on a different team to the last player who died by execution, do not wake Two-Face.
examples: On the first day, the Fortune Teller dies by execution. That night, Two-Face turns evil. On the second day, the Poisoner dies by execution. That night, Two-Face turns good. On the third day, the Seamstress dies by execution. That night, Two-Face turns evil.

On the first day, the Fortune Teller dies by execution. That night, Two-Face turns evil. On the second day, the Empath dies by execution. That night, Two-Face's team does not change. On the third day, the Seamstress dies by execution. That night, Two-Face's team does not change.
tips: If you're Two-Face, you'll probably be evil for most of the game — since good players generally die by execution more than evil players.
If you're Two-Face and tired of swinging between good and evil, the only foolproof way to fix your team is — death.

If you're Two-Face, you're one of the few Outsiders who can gain lots of "information" through your ability! Turning evil at night means the player who died by execution that day was good; otherwise they were evil. But your "information" is hard for everyone to accept! Two-Face can barely earn anyone's trust. And since you might turn evil at any time, think carefully about whether to report what you "know" to help the good team.

If you're Two-Face and you're evil on the final day, throw your votes for evil without hesitation! If you're good on the final day, you'd best be open about it — turning good means an evil player died by execution the day before, and now you must reason out who the Demon is with everyone and execute them to win with the good team.
If you're a good player, remember: Two-Face's words can't be trusted — they may betray you at any moment.
If you're an evil player, remember: Two-Face's words can't be trusted — they may betray you at any moment.

If you're an evil player, one reliable way to keep Two-Face on your side is executing a good player on the day before the final day — this almost guarantees Two-Face is evil on the final day, voting for evil.
bluffing: Two-Face can hardly earn anyone's trust, and some players always want to execute Two-Face to fix their team — so bluffing as Two-Face is fairly dangerous.
If you claim to be Two-Face and currently good, you're accusing the last player who died by execution of being evil — tread carefully if you're not prepared for that.
characters.creator: Taiyi
characters.otherNightReminder: If the player who died by execution today is on the opposite team to them, wake them and tell them their new team.

customBoxes.title: Design Notes
customBoxes.content:
As a "hidden" Outsider, Two-Face stays evil for the vast majority of the game, and because of the ability's nature, almost nobody trusts a player who openly claims Two-Face. Two-Face fulfills the "hidden" Outsider role well, providing soft Outsider-count variation logic for scripts.

Two-Face's niche resembles the Politician's — an Outsider serving evil most of the time. But the design gives Two-Face more reasoning logic and behavioral motive rather than pure chaos. Evil bluffing as Two-Face is high-value, facilitating evil's operations.

When a script's evil team is weak, Two-Face — an Outsider with a large negative effect — supplements evil's strength nicely.

characters.name: Mob lawyer
characters.ability: Each night, you learn a player: tomorrow, if either you or they would be executed, the other might be executed instead.
characters.lede: The Mob lawyer takes the fall to protect a client — or frames the client to protect himself.
characters.quote: Good day, my client. Have you seen the recent news? Allow me to read it to you: 'Your daughter works as a serving-girl at the inn and often pilfers the establishment's goods; your wife sneaks into the noble hunting grounds every week to pick fruit and vegetables against the law; and the tithes you've reported these past years show signs of considerable under-declaration and tampering.' I mean nothing by it, client. As long as tomorrow in court you testify word for word as written on this paper, I shall pretend I never heard any of it.
summaryBullets: In principle the Mob lawyer can learn any player. But try not to let them learn themself or dead players.
The Mob lawyer does not learn Traveller players.

If the Mob lawyer is poisoned or drunk at night, you must still tell them a player, but do not mark any player as "Client." The next day, even if the Mob lawyer regains their ability, it definitely cannot trigger.
If the Mob lawyer is poisoned or drunk when the execution happens, their ability cannot trigger — even if a player is marked "Client."

The Mob lawyer may learn good or evil players. When players assume you'll always give them evil players, give them more good players — and vice versa. Don't let players read your mind. For example, on the final day, when everyone assumes the Storyteller will surely have the Mob lawyer learn the Demon, you can give a non-Demon player to mislead them.
Whether the Mob lawyer's ability triggers is decided by the Storyteller. The Storyteller may never trigger it, or trigger it several times in a row.

Do not use the Mob lawyer's ability to force good into a guaranteed loss. For example: 3–4 players alive, the Mob lawyer learned the Demon, the Demon is executed, the Mob lawyer's ability triggers and the Mob lawyer dies instead. On the final day you may have the Mob lawyer learn the Demon, but don't trigger the ability in a way that directly decides the game.

When the Mob lawyer tries to get themself executed on the first day, consider having the "Client" executed instead. This self-proves the Mob lawyer but keeps them in play; if they try to execute themself again on later days, you can keep triggering the substitution — punishing utilitarian self-execution play.
Don't state outright that a substitute execution is due to the Mob lawyer's ability, even though in most scripts it can only be that. Simply announce "Player X was executed instead of player Y."
The Mob lawyer does not learn Traveller players (Traveller Exclusion Principle).
Information format: one player (e.g., "player #1" or "May").
False information format: none.
howToRun: Each night, wake the Mob lawyer and point at a player. Place the "Client" reminder by that player's character token, and put the Mob lawyer back to sleep. The next day, if a player is marked "Client" and either the Mob lawyer or the "Client" is about to be executed, you may have the other one executed instead. Whether or not you triggered the Mob lawyer's ability, remove the "Client" reminder at dusk.
examples: On the first night, the Mob lawyer learns player #1 (the Fortune Teller). The next day, player #1 is about to be executed; the Mob lawyer is executed instead of player #1.
On the first night, the Mob lawyer learns player #1 (the Fortune Teller). The next day, the Mob lawyer is about to be executed; player #1 is executed instead of the Mob lawyer.
On the first night, the Mob lawyer learns player #1 (the Fortune Teller). The next day, player #1 dies by execution; the Mob lawyer is not executed instead.
On the first night, the Mob lawyer learns player #1 (the Fortune Teller). The next day, the Mob lawyer dies by execution; player #1 is not executed instead.
tips: If you're the Mob lawyer, think first each day whether your "client" is more likely good or evil. If you think your client is evil, don't fear executing them. Even if the Storyteller makes you die instead, you can execute them again the next day — after you die by execution, the Storyteller can no longer use your ability to protect them! And your death proves you really are the Mob lawyer.

If you're the Mob lawyer, be cautious about executing yourself. The Storyteller may well "punish" your self-sacrifice by having your client die instead — keeping the Mob lawyer's ability in play for the Storyteller to keep sowing chaos. But there's an upside: you prove you're the Mob lawyer. If you need to prove yourself, you can try executing yourself — though Storytellers are always scheming, and at such times they may just not trigger your ability.

If you're the Mob lawyer, announce your character and the players you learn early, and discuss with everyone — preventing your ability from disrupting executions. People might also glean something from the players you learn, though more often nothing comes of it.

If you're an evil player and the Mob lawyer learned a good player, you can push everyone to execute that good player with the excuse that "the Storyteller always gives the Mob lawyer evil players." If the Storyteller happens to substitute the Mob lawyer, you can demand that player's execution again the next day for the same reason — winning the evil team an enormous round advantage.

If you're an evil player and you notice the Mob lawyer learned an evil player, the Storyteller will very likely trigger the Mob lawyer's ability to protect them — so that player needn't fear execution so much.
If you're the Demon, avoid attacking the Mob lawyer at night. Keeping them in play creates more chaos — the Storyteller can use their ability to protect evil or disrupt good's execution tempo.
bluffing: Bluff as the Mob lawyer: name your "client" and analyze them, verbally attacking your "client" as the evil player the Storyteller wants to protect, and demand their execution.

To bluff as the Mob lawyer, announce yourself early and reveal your "client" daily — it wins trust more easily. But you don't actually have the ability, so your "clients" should be marginal players — to avoid executing them without a substitution, which would make others suspect you.
characters.creator: Taiyi
characters.firstNightReminder: Wake the Mob lawyer and point at the player marked 'Client.'
characters.otherNightReminder: Wake the Mob lawyer and point at the player marked 'Client.'

customBoxes.title: Reminder Tokens
customBoxes.content:
[[Client]]
Placed when: Each night, when the Mob lawyer acts.
Condition: The Mob lawyer is alive and has their ability; place it by any player's character token.
Removed when: At dusk, or when the Mob lawyer dies or leaves play.

customBoxes.title: Design Notes
customBoxes.content:
The Mob lawyer's main function is disrupting execution tempo — a niche with almost no other Outsiders. Scrambling the good team's execution rhythm or misleading them into wrong execution judgments serves as an excellent negative effect, helping the Demon survive to the late game.

The Mob lawyer has an anti-suicide design: when the Mob lawyer courts death, you can substitute their learned player, keeping the Mob lawyer alive — punishing utilitarian death-seeking play.

The Mob lawyer gets information. They can read the Storyteller's mind from the players they learn, playing a simple psychological game — is my learned player good or evil? Is the Storyteller protecting evil, or misleading me? This raises the Mob lawyer's engagement and reduces the "sitting in jail" feeling of being an Outsider.

characters.name: Pirate Cat King
characters.ability: Dead players may give up vote tokens. On the final day, if you are dead, players who have split 12 vote tokens.
characters.lede: The Pirate Cat King owns all the world's treasure! You want it?! Hand over your vote token!
characters.quote: Wealth, fame, power — the cat-man who owned everything in this world, Pirate Cat King Gol D. Meowger. His single sentence before execution sent the whole world to the seas! 'You want my treasure, meow? If you want it, you can have it all — go find it, meow! I left every treasure in that place, meow!' And so, all cat-folk set sail for the Grand Line in pursuit of their dreams, and the world entered the Great Age of Pirate Cats!
summaryBullets: Vote token: the voting indicator a player gains upon death. A dead player gains one vote token and may only vote by using it. Whether each player has vote tokens, and how many, is public knowledge.

Unlike the official definition, in Odyssey a player holding multiple vote tokens may use them all in a single nomination to cast multiple votes, or use any number of tokens to cast the corresponding number of votes. When using multiple vote tokens at once, the player should hold up the corresponding number of fingers while voting so the Storyteller can tally. After the tally, the Storyteller collects the corresponding tokens.

Giving up vote tokens: a dead player, during the day, publicly choosing a character and giving their held vote tokens to the Storyteller to trigger a character's ability; that player loses all their held vote tokens. A player without vote tokens cannot give any up. Giving up tokens is public, visible to all players, and can only happen during the day. As long as a character with a give-up-tokens ability is on the script, players may publicly choose that character and give up tokens even if the character isn't in play.

Even if the Pirate Cat King isn't in play, is dead, or is poisoned or drunk, when a player says they're giving up vote tokens, respond publicly and collect the tokens just as if the Pirate Cat King had their ability — but don't mark that player as a "Treasure Hunter."

"The final day": the first day on which fewer than 5 players are alive (Travellers not counted). On the final day, the Storyteller publicly announces at the first opportunity that today is the final day. A game has at most one "final day"; if the game doesn't end on the final day, later days with fewer than 5 alive players are not treated as the "final day". If the game ends early (e.g., a special victory or the Demon's death), the game may have no "final day" at all. Before the final day arrives: the period before the final day. When the final day arrives: the moment the final day begins (usually the first dawn with fewer than 5 non-Traveller alive players). After the final day arrives: the final day and everything after.
When the final day begins, if the Pirate Cat King's ability can trigger, distribute the 12 vote tokens immediately.

When the final day begins, if the Pirate Cat King is alive, or dead but poisoned or drunk, no vote tokens are distributed. For the rest of that day, no tokens are distributed even if the Pirate Cat King becomes sober and healthy or dies.
The 12 vote tokens must be split evenly among all "Treasure Hunters." If they can't be split evenly, give each as many equal tokens as possible; the Storyteller takes back the leftover.

The Pirate Cat King themself can never share in the "treasure," because only death grants a vote token, and only token-holders can give them up. And once the Pirate Cat King is dead, the channel for becoming a "Treasure Hunter" is gone.
Traveller players cannot give up vote tokens (Traveller Exclusion Principle).
howToRun: Each day, a dead player holding vote tokens may publicly choose the Pirate Cat King and give up their vote tokens. You publicly respond to that player with "This game's Xth treasure hunter has appeared!" or similar, then collect all their vote tokens — even if the Pirate Cat King isn't in play or is poisoned or drunk. If the Pirate Cat King is currently alive and has their ability, place the "Treasure Hunter" reminder by the character token of the player who gave up tokens.

Immediately after announcing that the final day has arrived, if the Pirate Cat King is dead, take out 12 vote tokens and distribute them equally among the players marked "Treasure Hunter." Give each as many equal tokens as possible; the Storyteller takes back any leftover tokens that can't be split evenly.
examples: On the second day, the dead Poisoner publicly chooses the Pirate Cat King and gives up a vote token; the Storyteller publicly responds, "You have become this game's first treasure hunter." That night, the Pirate Cat King dies. On the third day, the dead Fortune Teller publicly chooses the Pirate Cat King and gives up a vote token; the Storyteller publicly responds, "You have become this game's second treasure hunter," but since the Pirate Cat King is dead, the Storyteller does not mark the Fortune Teller as a "Treasure Hunter." When the final day arrives, the Poisoner gets 12 vote tokens and uses them all in one vote that day.

On the second day, the dead Poisoner publicly chooses the Pirate Cat King and gives up a vote token. On the third day, the dead Fortune Teller does the same. On the fourth day, the dead Saint and Empath do the same. The Storyteller publicly responds to each player who gives up a token. On a later night, the Pirate Cat King dies. When the final day arrives, the dead Poisoner, Fortune Teller, Saint, and Empath each get 3 vote tokens.

On the second day, the dead Poisoner publicly chooses the Pirate Cat King and gives up a vote token. On the third day, the dead Fortune Teller does the same. On the fourth day, the dead Saint and Empath do the same. The Storyteller publicly responds to each. When the final day arrives, the Pirate Cat King is still alive — nobody gets vote tokens.

On the second day, the dead Poisoner gives up a vote token. On the third day, the dead Fortune Teller gives up one. On the fourth day, the dead Saint and Empath give up theirs. The Storyteller publicly responds to each player — but the Pirate Cat King isn't actually in play. When the final day arrives, nobody gets vote tokens.
tips: If you're the Pirate Cat King, as a good player you certainly don't want your "treasure" flowing into evil pockets! So hide yourself well until you die — or fight to survive to the final day, so nobody can take your "treasure"! Or you can privately tell one or two players you believe are good, letting them hunt for treasure to claim your "treasure" on the final day!

If you're the Pirate Cat King and, while alive, you spot a suspected evil player giving up tokens to become a treasure hunter, immediately encourage other good players to do the same! If all 12 vote tokens fall into one evil player's hands, you've already lost half the game!
If you're a good player but not the Pirate Cat King, you can bluff as the Pirate Cat King to trick evil players into giving up their vote tokens! But beware — good players may be fooled by you too!

If you're an evil player, keep a close eye on the Outsiders in play and what characters they are. If you find the Pirate Cat King is in play, sending at least one dead player to become a treasure hunter is usually a good deal — even if you get no "treasure" in the end, you only lost one vote token.

If you're the Demon and lots of dead good players joined the treasure hunt, they've wasted piles of vote tokens! Remember, the Pirate Cat King must be dead on the final day for the ability to trigger! You need only deliberately avoid the Pirate Cat King and let them survive to the final day — those foolish good players lose their investment forever. Of course, they can also execute the Pirate Cat King before the final day, but that undoubtedly buys you more survival chances. If necessary, you can also have a Minion become a treasure hunter that day for a share.

If you're an evil player, if you can get the Pirate Cat King poisoned, removed, or stripped of ability on the final day — anything, as long as their ability can't trigger normally — every treasure hunter loses everything! They lose their voting rights on the final day.
bluffing: Bluff as the Pirate Cat King and lure masses of good players into giving up their vote tokens — a huge boon for evil! Those fools lose their voting rights on the final day!

If you're bluffing as the Pirate Cat King, remember: everyone wants the Pirate Cat King dead before the final day! That both lets treasure hunters get tokens and self-proves you. So if you're the Demon, your risk of execution is enormous.

If you're bluffing as the Pirate Cat King, remember: you have no real "treasure" to share. So even if you die on the final day, you can't prove yourself on the final day. If you don't plan to come out as evil on the final day, prepare in advance an explanation for why your ability didn't work properly.
characters.creator: Taiyi

customBoxes.title: Reminder Tokens
customBoxes.content:
[[Treasure Hunter" ×5]]
Placed when: When a dead player publicly gives up vote tokens.
Condition: While the Pirate Cat King is alive and has their ability.
Removed when: The Pirate Cat King leaves play.

customBoxes.title: Design Notes
customBoxes.content:
The Pirate Cat King is the apex design of the Cat series — a bold, innovative character set themed around social interaction.

The Cat series encourages social behavior, with emphasis on caring for dead players and players of weaker, marginal characters.

Following the Skeleton King and the Hanged Man, the Pirate Cat King pushes vote-token design one step further.

The Pirate Cat King is an Outsider with a major impact on the game, requiring both teams to strategize around it. Is the Pirate Cat King actually in play? How many treasure hunters should our side send? How do we kill the Pirate Cat King before the final day? If good lets evil sneak away with all 12 vote tokens, the Demon need only survive to the final day to effectively declare victory.

characters.name: Clone
characters.ability: Once per game, at night*, you may choose a player: they die, and you become their character.
characters.lede: The Clone kills players and becomes their copy.
characters.quote: Invade, absorb, reshape. The key to it all lies in that code called DNA. Or in the ignorant parlance of this era, should I call it — the soul?
summaryBullets: If the Clone attacked a player but didn't cause that player's death (including attacking a dead player), the Clone's character doesn't change.
After the Clone becomes a new character, from that night onward, the Clone uses the new character's ability normally, just like that character.
If the Clone kills the Demon, the game doesn't end from the Demon's death — because the Clone becomes the new Demon.
If the Clone kills and becomes the Demon, he is not woken by the Demon's ability that night — because the Clone acts after the Demon, who has already acted.
The Clone cannot choose Traveller players (the Traveller Exclusion Principle).
howToRun: Each night except the first, wake the Clone. He may shake his head to not use his ability, or point to any player. If that player can be killed, mark that player dead, turn the Clone into that player's character, show the Clone in turn the "You are" info token and his new character token, then put him back to sleep. If that player can't be killed by the Clone, put the Clone back to sleep. Once the Clone has used his ability, do not wake the Clone on later nights.
examples: On the second night, the Clone chooses the Fortune Teller player; the Fortune Teller dies, and the Clone becomes the Fortune Teller.
On the second night, the Clone chooses the Golem player; the Golem dies, and the Clone becomes the Golem. The next day, the new Golem nominates the Fortune Teller — the Fortune Teller dies.
On the fourth night, the Clone chooses the Vortox player; the Vortox dies, and the Clone becomes the Vortox. The Vortox already acted that night, so the new Vortox is not woken.
On the fourth night, the Clone chooses the Saint player protected by the Innkeeper. The Saint doesn't die, and the Clone doesn't become the Saint.
On the fourth night, the Clone chooses the dead Fang Gu. The Fang Gu can't die again, and the Clone doesn't become the Fang Gu.
tips: If you're the Clone, you can use your ability to kill important players. Or fake other characters' ability effects, such as the Gossip or the Gambler.
If you're the Clone, you can judge what character the player you killed was by the new character you become.
If you're the Clone, killing the Demon lets you become the new Demon. Relocating the Demon is an important use of your ability.

If you're the Clone and you know the other player's character, you can seize their ability by killing them. Kill a Poisoner, then poison every night. Or kill a Snake Charmer to swap with the Demon at any time. Or kill a Virgin to deliberately waste the good team's execution chance.

If you're a good player, note that the Clone may change the Demon's position by killing and becoming the new Demon. If an abnormal extra death occurs at night and the victim is your prime suspect, they might be the Demon killed by the Clone.

If you're a good player and the abnormal extra night deaths include characters whose abilities greatly affect the situation — such as the Virgin or the Gossip — the Clone may have killed them and gained their abilities. Guard against the Clone using new abilities to cause greater destruction.
characters.creator: Taiyi
characters.tags: Character Change, Death, Once Per Game
characters.otherNightReminder: Have him choose a player.

customBoxes.title: Reminder Tokens
customBoxes.content:
[[No Ability]]
Placed when: When the Clone chooses to use his ability during his night action and chooses a player.
Condition: As long as the Clone chose a player, place this reminder by the Clone's character token regardless of whether the Clone is drunk or poisoned.
Removed when: The Clone dies or leaves play.

[[Dead]]
Placed when: When the Clone chooses to use his ability during his night action and chooses a player.
Condition: The player the Clone chose is currently alive, the Clone can kill that player, and the Clone is not drunk or poisoned — place it by that player's character token to remind the Storyteller to announce that night's dead player at dawn.
Removed when: After announcing the dead player at dawn; the Storyteller may remove it at their convenience.

characters.name: Witch Doctor
characters.ability: Each night, choose a player: they are poisoned. Your last choice dies & becomes healthy.
characters.lede: Deaths suffered by players poisoned by the Witch Doctor are delayed until they are no longer under the Witch Doctor's protection.
characters.quote: When the serpent staff strikes the earth and jungle smoke rises, breathe deep this bewitching incense of mandrake and wolfsbane. Do not resist this divine gift — this is the indestructible body, this is the rapture of the heart, this is the ultimate bliss of the mortal world.
summaryBullets: Death delayed: when a player is about to die, they temporarily don't die — the death is postponed until the delayed-death effect ends or disappears. Delayed death postpones deaths from execution and from character abilities alike.

A player whose death is postponed by the delayed-death effect dies from the same cause as the first death they suffered during the delay. For example, if a death-delayed player is first attacked by the Demon and then executed again, and the delayed-death effect ends that night, that player is treated as dying from the Demon's attack — because the Demon attack was the first cause of death.

A player whose death was delayed by the Witch Doctor's ability is no longer poisoned when they die. E.g., the Ravenkeeper is chosen by the Witch Doctor and then executed; that night the Witch Doctor chooses a new target, and the Ravenkeeper's delayed-death effect ends and he dies. At that point the Ravenkeeper dies and is not poisoned, so his ability works correctly.

A player whose death was delayed by the Witch Doctor's ability dies immediately when the Witch Doctor's ability disappears. E.g., with 3 players left alive, the Witch Doctor dies by execution — the Demon whose death he delayed dies immediately. Good wins.

If the Witch Doctor chooses himself, he loses all abilities from being poisoned, so he can't delay his own death. A Witch Doctor who poisoned himself recovers immediately after choosing another player, and poisons the player he chose.

As long as the Witch Doctor keeps choosing the same player, every death that player suffers keeps being delayed — even if they suffer death multiple times, they don't die, until they are no longer affected by the Witch Doctor's ability, at which point they die immediately.
The Witch Doctor cannot choose Traveller players (the Traveller Exclusion Principle).
howToRun: Each night, wake the Witch Doctor. Have the Witch Doctor point to any player. The chosen player is poisoned and they die — place the "Voodoo" reminder by the chosen player's character token. Put the Witch Doctor back to sleep. When the Witch Doctor chooses a new player, remove the "Voodoo" reminder.

If a player with the "Voodoo" reminder is about to die, they die — place the "Delayed Death" reminder by that player's character token. When a player with the "Delayed Death" reminder is no longer affected by the Witch Doctor's ability (including the Witch Doctor choosing a new player, or the Witch Doctor dying, leaving play, being drunk or poisoned, or losing his ability), they die immediately. Remove the "Delayed Death" reminder.
examples: On the first night, the Witch Doctor chooses the Noble; the Noble is poisoned and gets false information that night. The next day, the Noble is executed but doesn't die (death delayed). On the second night, the Witch Doctor chooses the Fortune Teller; the Noble's delayed-death effect ends and the Noble dies.

On the second night, the Witch Doctor chooses the Fortune Teller; the Demon attacks the Fortune Teller, but the Fortune Teller doesn't die thanks to the Witch Doctor's ability (death delayed), and the poisoned Fortune Teller gets false information. The next day, the Fortune Teller is executed but doesn't die thanks to the Witch Doctor's ability (death delayed). On the third night, the Witch Doctor still chooses the Fortune Teller; the poisoned Fortune Teller gets false information. On the night with 4 players left, the Witch Doctor chooses himself; the Fortune Teller's delayed-death effect ends and the Fortune Teller dies. The Demon kills another player. Only two players remain alive — evil wins.

On the fourth night, the Witch Doctor chooses the Imp; the Imp is poisoned and attacks the Fortune Teller that night, but because the Imp is poisoned, the Fortune Teller doesn't die. The next day, the Imp is executed but doesn't die (death delayed). On the fifth night, the Witch Doctor still chooses the Imp; the Imp's death continues to be delayed. The next day, the Witch Doctor is executed; the Imp's delayed-death effect ends, and the Witch Doctor and the Imp die together. The good team wins.

On the first night, the Witch Doctor chooses the Monk; the Monk is poisoned. On the first day, the Monk is executed but doesn't die (death delayed). On the second day, the Witch Doctor is executed; the Monk's delayed-death effect ends, and the Witch Doctor and the Monk die together.

On the second night, the Witch Doctor chooses the Banshee; the Imp attacks the Banshee, but the Banshee doesn't die (death delayed). On the second day, the Banshee is executed but doesn't die (death delayed). On the third night, the Witch Doctor chooses another player; the Banshee dies, her ability triggers, and all players know the Banshee has awakened (the Demon attack was the first cause of death, so the Banshee is treated as killed by the Demon).
On the first night, the Witch Doctor chooses himself; because he is poisoned, the Witch Doctor loses all abilities, so he is not protected from dying.
tips: Remember, your ability has at least three uses. First: disrupting other players' abilities through poisoning. Second: making a player not die when executed (temporarily), to protect a specific player or fake another character's ability. Third: coordinating with the Demon to shift that night's death to a later night, to fake a safe night or other goals. Use your imagination and make brilliant plays with the Witch Doctor's ability!

If you want to choose the Demon, remember two things. First, the Demon is poisoned by your ability and can't kill his target. Second, if the Demon is executed while under your protection, he doesn't die immediately — but he dies immediately once he loses your ability's protection.
You can choose the same target as the Demon at night to create a safe night. Then choose a new target on another night to create the illusion of multiple players dying on the same night.
If you're a good player and think you're poisoned by the Witch Doctor, you can try executing yourself — if you die, you definitely weren't poisoned by the Witch Doctor the previous night.

If you're a good player who was executed but didn't die, then died that night — and you weren't the only one who died that night — you were most likely chosen by the Witch Doctor the previous night, and he chose a new target that night.

If you're a good player and you've executed a suspected Demon multiple times without him dying, and the nights have all been safe — there's a very high probability a Witch Doctor is secretly keeping the Demon alive. Stop executing him and go find and execute the Witch Doctor hiding in the shadows.
The Witch Doctor can't protect himself. If you've found the Witch Doctor, execute him as soon as possible.

characters.otherNightReminder: Have him choose a player.

customBoxes.title: Reminder Tokens
customBoxes.content:
[[Voodoo]]
Placed when: After the Witch Doctor acts at night and chooses a player.
Condition: Place it by the character token of the player the Witch Doctor chose. If the Witch Doctor is drunk or poisoned at this time, do not place this reminder.
Removed when: The Witch Doctor chooses a new player, or the Witch Doctor dies or leaves play.

[[Delayed Death]]
Placed when: When a player with the "Voodoo" reminder is about to die.
Condition: Place it by the character token of a player with the "Voodoo" reminder. If the Witch Doctor is drunk or poisoned at this time, do not place this reminder.
Removed when: The Witch Doctor chooses a new player, or the Witch Doctor dies, leaves play, is drunk or poisoned, or loses his ability. If it's night at that time, wait until dawn to remove it, to remind the Storyteller to announce that night's dead players at dawn.

characters.name: The Sea-born
characters.ability: Each night*, choose a player: they die. The Storyteller has Minion abilities of their choosing & helps you win. [No Minions, any Outsiders]
characters.lede: The Sea-born has no Minions — the Storyteller aids him with Minion abilities.
characters.quote: My dear child, noble blood of Poseidon runs in your veins — how could I allow those filthy, lowly Minions to serve you? While you slept upon the waves, your father's trident churned the entire Aegean. Every ship that dared set sail before dawn was torn apart by the storm. When the last sailor sinks to the seabed, is that stillness not your father's gentlest lullaby?
summaryBullets: The Sea-born's design concept is "the Storyteller takes the field, matching wits with the players." In a Sea-born game, you play Poseidon, the doting father. As a true god, you are indestructible — and your dear boy the Sea-born is your only weakness. So look after your dear boy as much as possible within the rules!

Once the game enters its first night, because of the Sea-born's ability, you must drop your "neutral" stance for this game and instead help the Sea-born win as much as possible.
