characters.quote: I know. I know it all. Just wait until that day — I will know it all!
summaryBullets: "The final day": the first day of the game with fewer than 5 alive players (not counting Travellers). When the final day arrives, the Storyteller immediately announces "the final day has come." A game has at most one "final day" — if the game doesn't end on the final day, later days with fewer than 5 alive players are not treated as the "final day". If the game ends early (e.g. special victory or the Demon's death), that game has no "final day".

During setup, regardless of whether the Kappa was added by another character's setup-modifying ability, as long as the Kappa exists, the Outsider count can be changed freely. Once the Kappa is added to the setup, his ability overrides other setup-adjusting abilities, such as the Baron's.
The Kappa's ability cannot subtract the Kappa himself.
The Storyteller decides how many Outsiders the Kappa adds or removes.
A Kappa created mid-game has no ability.
The Kappa only learns the number of Outsider players on the final day.
On the final day, if the Kappa is already dead, he cannot learn the number of Outsider players.
The Kappa learns the current number of Outsider players — including alive Outsider players and dead Outsider players.
If the Kappa is poisoned or drunk, he might learn a wrong number of Outsider players.
Information format: a number, such as "1" or "2" or "3".
howToRun: During game setup, add or remove any number of Outsider character tokens (you cannot remove the Kappa itself) — or make no change. Confirm the total number of character tokens matches the number of players.

On the final day, if the Kappa asks to speak privately with you, leave the circle of players together with him and make sure your private chat can't be overheard. Then whisper to the Kappa the current number of Outsider players.
examples: A 12-player game. The Kappa is in play and the Kappa removes one Outsider — the Kappa is the only Outsider in play. On the final day, the Kappa visits the Storyteller and learns "1".

A 12-player game. The Kappa is in play and the Kappa adds three Outsiders — there are four Outsiders in play. On the final day, the Kappa is already dead, so he cannot learn how many Outsider players there are.
A 12-player game. The Kappa is in play and the Kappa doesn't change the Outsider count — there are two Outsiders in play. On the final day, the Kappa visits the Storyteller and learns "2".
tips: If you're the Kappa, you'd best announce you're a Kappa as soon as possible, so everyone knows the Outsider count may have changed.
If you're the Kappa, you can hide your character until you learn the Outsider count — this prevents the Demon from knowing you're the Kappa and killing you.
If you're an evil player and you know the Kappa is in play, try bluffing as an Outsider.
If you're an evil player and you know the Kappa isn't in play, you can bluff as the Kappa and have your teammates bluff as Outsiders.
If you're the Demon, best kill the Kappa before the final day arrives, preventing him from learning the Outsider count — especially when your teammates are bluffing as Outsiders.
bluffing: Bluffing as the Kappa while your teammates bluff as other Outsiders is an excellent tactic.
Bluffing as the Kappa makes every Outsider untrustworthy — logically, any of them could be an evil bluff.
Before bluffing as the Kappa, first judge whether the Kappa is in play to avoid a clash.
characters.creator: Taiyi

customBoxes.title: Design Notes
customBoxes.content:
A simple, fundamental Outsider character.

Giving the Kappa the ability to learn information on the final day gives the Kappa a reason to hide his character. For both a real Kappa and an evil player bluffing as the Kappa, this expands the play possibilities and avoids formulaic play.

characters.name: Nurgle
characters.ability: Each night*, choose a player: they die, and the players neighboring them are poisoned until your next attack.
characters.lede: Nurgle's attack kills while poisoning the players within range.
characters.quote: Oh, my poor child, you're not looking well — your face is too clean, your skin too smooth. That won't do. Come, let Grandfather hold you; it's been days since I embraced a new face. Your body lacks something warm, something... that grows slowly. Once my little 'gift' stirs in your belly, you'll discover what a reassuring feeling rot can be. Don't be afraid — there'll be a little swelling, a little itching, but that's just my children saying hello. When you bloom all over, you'll thank me.
summaryBullets: The players neighboring them: the two players nearest to "them", regardless of life or death, skipping Travellers (the Traveller Exclusion Principle).
Nurgle's attack can poison not only Townsfolk, but also Outsiders, Minions — even Nurgle himself.
Nurgle's poisoning ends at the moment Nurgle is about to act next. So if Nurgle poisons himself, that poisoning doesn't affect his next attack.
Even if Nurgle's attack doesn't cause a death, it still causes poisoning. If Nurgle attacks a protected player or a dead player, the players neighboring the attacked player are still poisoned.
howToRun: Each night except the first, remove all of Nurgle's "Poisoned" reminders, then wake Nurgle. Have Nurgle point to any player. Put Nurgle back to sleep. The chosen player dies — place Nurgle's "Dead" reminder by that player's character token. The two players neighboring the chosen player are poisoned — place Nurgle's "Poisoned" reminders by those two players' character tokens.
examples: On the second night, Nurgle attacks the Saint; the Saint dies. The Fortune Teller sits to the Saint's left, and the Baron to his right — the Fortune Teller and the Baron are poisoned.

On the second night, Nurgle attacks the Fortune Teller; Nurgle sits to the Fortune Teller's left, and the Fool to his right — Nurgle and the Fool are poisoned. On the fourth night, Nurgle attacks the Noble; by now Nurgle and the Fool have recovered, and the Noble dies. The players on both sides of the Noble are poisoned, even though they're both already dead.
On the third night, Nurgle attacks the already-dead Fortune Teller; the Empath sits to the Fortune Teller's left, and the Fool to his right — the Empath and the Fool are poisoned.

On the third night, Nurgle attacks the Fool protected by the Monk; the Fool doesn't die. The Empath sits to the Fool's left, and the Fortune Teller to his right — the Empath and the Fortune Teller are poisoned.
tips: If you're Nurgle, plan your attacks carefully so your death and poison effects work efficiently.
If you're Nurgle, your attack may poison players other than Townsfolk — that might not be good for you. Try to avoid disrupting abilities that matter to you.
If you're Nurgle, attacking dead players or protected players at the right moments to poison and disrupt the game is a fine option too.
If you're a good player, Nurgle's poison always lingers around the players who die at night. So if the players neighboring you are all alive, you don't need to worry about being poisoned by Nurgle.

If you're a good player, Nurgle usually avoids attacking players neighboring important Minions, so as not to disrupt their abilities. If you can confirm the in-play Demon is Nurgle, a player claiming an important Townsfolk who stays alive — with both neighbors also alive — is highly suspicious.
characters.creator: Taiyi
characters.otherNightReminder: Have him choose a player.

customBoxes.title: Reminder Tokens
customBoxes.content:
[[Dead]]
Placed when: After Nurgle chooses a player.
Condition: If the player Nurgle chose is currently alive and Nurgle is not drunk or poisoned, place it by that player's character token.
Removed when: After announcing the dead player at dawn; the Storyteller may remove it at their convenience.

[[Poisoned" ×2]]
Placed when: After Nurgle chooses a player.
Condition: If Nurgle is sober and healthy when choosing, place them by the character tokens of the two players neighboring the player he chose.
Removed when: Nurgle acts, dies, or leaves play.

customBoxes.title: Design Notes
customBoxes.content:
A simple, brutal poisoning Demon.

Poison bound to kills, with a controllable poison range.

Has good not-in-play deterrence.

Has certain side effects; strength heavily depends on kill planning — a test of player skill.

characters.name: Somnmaid
characters.ability: The 1st time the Demon attacks you, you do not die & learn their character.
characters.lede: The Somnmaid can survive the Demon's attack and learn their character.
characters.quote: Every night I pray, begging God to let me meet someone 'who shouldn't be saved.' At last, you've come. Your curiosity about me and mine about you are the two ends of the same rope. You're wondering: 'Will this woman tremble before me?' I'm wondering: 'Will this man kneel before me?' We each harbor our own thoughts — but as long as we draw close enough, those thoughts become the same warmth. Stay, even if only for one night, and let me light you a candle that never needs to go out.
summaryBullets: Attack: when a player with a Demon ability, or the Storyteller, selects a player with the Demon's killing ability. Attacks usually kill an alive player; sometimes they don't, such as attacking a player who cannot die or a dead player.
The first time the Somnmaid is attacked by the Demon, she is woken immediately after the Demon finishes acting and learns the character.
If the Somnmaid is attacked by the Demon during the day, she is woken at the first opportunity after nightfall and learns the character — even if she died by execution that day.
The Somnmaid's ability only works the first time the Demon attacks her, and she does not die from that attack.
A poisoned or drunk Demon attacking the Somnmaid still triggers her ability.
Whatever reason the Somnmaid didn't die when attacked by the Demon, she learns the Demon's character and loses her ability.
When the Somnmaid dies from anything other than the Demon's ability, she neither survives nor learns a character.

"The Demon" in the Somnmaid's ability includes both players whose character is a Demon and non-Demon players who have a Demon ability. So what the Somnmaid learns isn't necessarily a Demon character: if a player who has a Demon ability but isn't a Demon character attacks her, she learns their true character.
If the Somnmaid is poisoned or drunk, you may wake her on a night the Demon didn't attack her and tell her a character, deceiving her into thinking she was attacked that night.
Information format: a character, e.g., the Imp or the Fang Gu.
False information format: a character, but not the character of the player who attacked the Somnmaid.
howToRun: At night, if the Demon attacks the Somnmaid, the Somnmaid does not die from it. Then wake the Somnmaid and tell her the character of the Demon who attacked her.
examples: On the second night, the Imp attacks the Somnmaid; the Somnmaid does not die, and is woken and learns the Imp.
On the second night, the Fang Gu attacks the Somnmaid; the Somnmaid does not die, and is woken and learns the Fang Gu. On the third night, the Fang Gu attacks the Somnmaid; the Somnmaid dies.
tips: If you're the Somnmaid, bluff as an important Townsfolk as much as possible to bait the Demon into attacking you.
If you're the Somnmaid and you died at night, you definitely didn't die from the Demon's attack — or you were poisoned or drunk.
If you're the Somnmaid and you were woken and learned a character, you were definitely attacked by the Demon last night (or poisoned/drunk) — share what you learned with everyone as soon as possible.
If you're the Demon, beware the Somnmaid and avoid her as much as possible. If you attack her, first you can't kill her, and second you expose the Demon's species — an enormous disadvantage for evil.

If you're the Demon and you've already attacked the Somnmaid once by mistake, absent a better target you might as well attack her again to kill her for good — especially while everyone trusts she's the Somnmaid.
bluffing: The Somnmaid works as a backup bluff: admit you're actually the Somnmaid after your other bluff fails.
You can go public as the Somnmaid and name the Demon character you learned. If no player died last night, this move is very effective for selling your Somnmaid bluff.
characters.creator: Taiyi, Imp

customBoxes.title: Reminder Tokens
customBoxes.content:
[[No Ability]]
Placed when: After the Demon attacks the Somnmaid.
Condition: After the Demon attacks the Somnmaid, if the Somnmaid did not die, place it by the Somnmaid's character token.
Removed when: The Somnmaid dies or leaves play.

customBoxes.title: Design Notes
customBoxes.content:
A safe-night-logic landmine Townsfolk.

Landmine payoff: half a round plus exposing the Demon's character — a middling, reasonable landmine reward.

Compared to the Soldier: only one free hit, but it trades for crucial information about the Demon's character. Most importantly, it fixes the fatal flaw of abilities firing with no feedback.

characters.name: Khorne
characters.ability: Each night*, choose 2 players: they die. If a good player died today, 1 of the players you choose tonight does not die.
characters.lede: Khorne both kills players and protects them.
characters.quote: You're too timid — even your blade trembles. You don't deserve to stand here; you defile your banner and your glory. Only the warriors who dared look me in the eye, who charged at me, who tried to strike back even as they fell, deserve my mourning — however brief. And you? You deserve to be casually chopped down, unknown to all, with not even a fly bothering to land on your corpse.
summaryBullets: Khorne can attack two players each night. Those two players die in the order Khorne chose them.
If a good player died during the day, which of the two players Khorne chooses that night dies and which is protected is decided by the Storyteller.

As long as a good player died during the day — whether by execution or another cause — one of the players Khorne chooses that night can't die that night, including from Khorne's ability or any other cause.

Certain characters who can cause deaths at night before Khorne acts (such as the Gambler): if they caused a death that night before Khorne acted, and are then chosen as the player Khorne protects, revoke the death they caused that night. If those deaths would cause death-triggered effects, wait until after Khorne acts — if Khorne didn't protect them, then resolve those effects.
If Khorne is drunk or poisoned when a good player dies during the day, and Khorne later recovers, one of the players Khorne chooses that night still can't die.
If Khorne isn't in play when a good player dies during the day, and Khorne is later created, Khorne kills two players that night.
If Khorne protects a good player chosen by the Half-Orc, so that the Half-Orc causes no death, the other player Khorne chose that night dies normally without the Half-Orc's protection.
A good Traveller player dying during the day doesn't affect Khorne's ability. Khorne cannot choose Travellers. (The Traveller Exclusion Principle)
howToRun: Each night except the first, wake Khorne. Have Khorne point to any two players. Put Khorne back to sleep. The chosen players die — place Khorne's "Dead" reminders by those two players' character tokens.

If a good player died today, place the "Doesn't Die" reminder by Khorne's character token. That night, after Khorne chooses two players, place the "Dead" reminder by one of them — they die. Move the "Doesn't Die" reminder to the other player's character token — they can't die tonight, including from Khorne's ability or any other cause.
At dawn, remove all "Doesn't Die" reminders.
examples: On the first day, a good player dies by execution. That night, Khorne chooses the Fortune Teller and the Noble — the Noble dies; the Fortune Teller doesn't.

On the first day, a good player dies by execution. That night, the Gambler guesses a character wrong; Khorne chooses the Fortune Teller and the Gambler — the Fortune Teller dies; the Gambler doesn't (affected by Khorne's ability — see Rule Details).
On the first day, an Outsider dies by execution. That night, Khorne chooses the Fortune Teller and the Noble — the Fortune Teller dies. Then the Godfather chooses the Noble — the Noble doesn't die.
On the first day, the Golem nominates and kills a good player. That night, Khorne chooses the Fortune Teller and the Noble — the Fortune Teller dies; the Noble doesn't.
On the second day, only one good player is executed but doesn't die. That night, Khorne attacks two players — both die.
On the third day, only one evil player dies by execution. That night, Khorne attacks two players — both die.
On the fourth day, nobody is executed. That night, Khorne attacks two players — both die.
tips: If you're Khorne, kill as fast as possible — prioritize players who seem important.

If you're Khorne, your protection ability can keep players who should have died at night alive, causing chaos — e.g., protecting a Gambler who guessed wrong, or a Minion targeted by Demon-hunting Townsfolk.
If you're Khorne and a good player died today, you can't land precise kills that night — so choose two equally important players to guarantee your kill value.

If you're Khorne, you can also hide your edge — deliberately choose dead players or protected players so only one player dies. This fakes another Demon in play, or leads everyone to believe the player executed that day was good.

If you're Khorne, don't fear the good team not executing players during the day, or executing players without deaths — you can immediately make the death count "catch up" that night. But this may also expose the Demon as Khorne.
If you're a good player and unexplained multi-death nights keep happening, consider the possibility that the Demon is Khorne.

If you're a good player and you believe the Demon is Khorne but only one player died at night, the player executed that day may have been good. If 2 or more players died at night, the player executed that day was very likely evil.
If you're a good player and you believe the Demon is Khorne, try to execute players every day. Even if you don't choose someone to execute, Khorne will "choose for you" at night.
characters.creator: Taiyi
characters.otherNightReminder: Have him choose two players.

customBoxes.title: Reminder Tokens
customBoxes.content:
[[Dead" ×2]]
Placed when: After Khorne chooses players.
Condition: If the players Khorne chose are currently alive and Khorne is not drunk or poisoned, place them by those players' character tokens.
Removed when: After announcing the dead players at dawn; the Storyteller may remove them at their convenience.

[[Doesn't Die]]
Placed when: When a good player dies during the day, or when Khorne acts.
Condition: When a good player dies during the day, place it by Khorne's character token — even if Khorne is drunk or poisoned. When Khorne acts, if this reminder is in the Grimoire, move it to the character token of one of the players Khorne chose.
Removed when: At dawn.

customBoxes.title: Design Notes
customBoxes.content:
A multi-kill Demon — but outside multi-kill scenarios, he can't control his kills.

Each Minion executed adds 1 kill; each evil-converted player executed adds 1 kill; execution-survival and no-execution scenarios each add 1 kill. By the 5-kill model, he's slightly overpowered — but the inability to control kills in single-kill scenarios offsets his strength to a degree.

Granting the Demon a protection ability is a very novel idea — it muddies some logic in scripts where Townsfolk can cause deaths.

Though he's a multi-kill Demon specialized for execution-survival logic, he performs at normal strength in ordinary scripts too — and he can pressure the good team into executing players from day one, avoiding stalls.

characters.name: Toxblast
characters.ability: When a player dies by execution, the 2 nearest Townsfolk are poisoned until dusk. If no-one is executed, all Townsfolk are poisoned.
characters.lede: The Townsfolk neighboring an executed player are poisoned.
characters.quote: My masterpiece flows beneath his skin! Those exquisite compounds! The moment the noose tightens, they'll burst from every orifice and wound of his like a rain of brilliant fireworks — landing on your faces, seeping into your lungs. Beautiful, isn't it?
summaryBullets: If a player was executed but nobody died, no player is poisoned by Toxblast that day.
If multiple players die by execution on the same day, 2 Townsfolk are poisoned each time.
If a Townsfolk poisoned by Toxblast becomes another character, they immediately recover, and no other Townsfolk "takes over" their poisoning.
When a player dies by execution, the poisoned Townsfolk are the two Townsfolk nearest to that player clockwise and counterclockwise (skipping all players who aren't Townsfolk), whether alive or dead.
howToRun: When a player dies by execution, immediately find the two Townsfolk nearest to that player in the clockwise and counterclockwise directions, and place "Poisoned" reminders by their character tokens — they are poisoned from now on. Then remove all "Poisoned" reminders placed yesterday.

Each dusk, if no player was executed today, place the "Poisoned" reminder by Toxblast's character token — this represents all Townsfolk being poisoned. Then remove all "Poisoned" reminders placed yesterday.
examples: On the first day, no player is executed — all Townsfolk are poisoned.
On the first day, the Noble dies by execution. The Townsfolk nearest to the Noble are the Fortune Teller and the Empath sitting beside him — the Fortune Teller and the Empath are poisoned.
On the third day, the Baron dies by execution. The Townsfolk nearest to him are the dead Noble and the dead King — the dead Noble and the dead King are poisoned.
tips: If you're Toxblast, watch each day's execution and figure out which Townsfolk are poisoned by you — they'll lose their abilities or get false information. You can anticipate this and craft lies that fit their information, making their abilities look normal.

If you're another evil player, Toxblast has very strong not-in-play deterrence — whether or not Toxblast is in play, you can use "Toxblast might be in play, poisoning the Townsfolk beside the executed player" to reasonably explain all kinds of things.

If you're a good player, arrange each day's executions sensibly, and watch which players Toxblast's poison might land on. If the players neighboring the executed player aren't Townsfolk, Toxblast's poison skips over them to poison players further away — don't overlook this.
characters.creator: Taiyi

customBoxes.title: Reminder Tokens
customBoxes.content:
[[Poisoned" ×2]]
Placed when: When a player dies by execution, or when the day ends with no player executed.
Condition: When a player dies by execution, place them by the character tokens of the two Townsfolk neighboring that player. When the day ends with no player executed, place it by Toxblast's character token.
Removed when: Toxblast dies or leaves play; at every dusk.

customBoxes.title: Design Notes
customBoxes.content:
Passive poison, no first-night poison — compensated by a large dosage.

The ability comes with built-in forced-execution guidance, speeding up the script's pace and avoiding stalling play where nobody gets executed.

A new option among interference Minions.

characters.name: Twinflower
characters.ability: You think you are a Townsfolk character, but you are not. [+1 Twinflower, the two Twinflowers sit next to each other]
characters.lede: The two neighboring Twinflowers both think they're Townsfolk.
characters.quote: Twin shadows bloom as one; good and evil leave their traces. Two flowers on a single stem, bound together by fate.
summaryBullets: A Twinflower always thinks she's a Townsfolk character — she cannot think she's anything else.
The Twinflowers always sit next to each other, with no other player between them.

Twinflowers don't learn the Minion info, but appear normally in the Demon's Demon info and the other Minions' Minion info (unlike the Marionette). This means the Demon and the other Minions know the Twinflower players are Minions, but not what Minion they are. However, two neighboring extra Minions almost certainly means they are the Twinflowers.

When playing in person, don't wake the two Twinflowers during the Minion info — wake the other Minion players, then point to the two Twinflowers: this tells the other Minions those two are also Minions. When showing the Demon the Demon info, point to the Twinflowers and the other Minion players as normal — the Demon only learns which players are Minions (including the Twinflowers), not who the Twinflowers are.
The Townsfolk character a player who thinks she's a Twinflower drew has its ability produce no effect at all, but the Storyteller pretends the effects work. This works similarly to the Drunk.
In interactions, Twinflowers are still treated as the evil team and Minion characters.

If a player is turned into a Twinflower mid-game, they think they've become a Townsfolk character (if they were already a Townsfolk, they may keep thinking they're their original Townsfolk character, so they don't learn their character changed). A Twinflower created mid-game doesn't add +1 other Twinflower and doesn't need to meet the neighboring-other-Twinflower condition.
howToRun: During game setup, before putting character tokens into the bag, remove the Twinflower character token and add one Townsfolk character token.
While preparing for the first night, choose two Townsfolk sitting next to each other and place the Twinflower's "Twinflower" reminders by their character tokens.

Run the Townsfolk a Twinflower thinks she is as if they were drunk. A Twinflower is woken at the times of the Townsfolk character she thinks she is, may get false information, but is not woken during the first-night Minion info, and so on.

Twinflowers don't learn the Minion info, but appear normally in the Demon info and the Minion info. This means the Demon and the other Minions know the Twinflower players are Minions, but not what Minion they are. However, two neighboring extra Minions almost certainly means they are the Twinflowers.
examples: 12-player game. There are 3 Minions in play; the 2 Twinflowers sit next to each other and think they're the Fortune Teller and the Empath respectively.
tips: If you're a Twinflower, you won't learn you're a Twinflower — you'll think you're a Townsfolk. If a player finds you and tells you you're actually a Twinflower, they might be lying — or you might really be a Twinflower. If you really are a Twinflower, that means you're an evil Minion.

If you're a Twinflower, another Twinflower definitely sits next to you. If you suspect you're a Twinflower, find that Twinflower — if both your abilities seem to be failing, the probability you're both Twinflowers is high.
If you're a Twinflower and suspect you're a Twinflower, best find your "twin" sister and talk it over together!

If you're a good player, the Twinflowers definitely sit next to each other and both think they're Townsfolk! If two neighboring Townsfolk both have malfunctioning abilities, and their behavior differs across the early, middle, and late game, they're very likely the Twinflowers!

If you're another evil player, should you tell the Twinflowers they're Twinflowers? It depends on the situation. If things are going well for evil, you can leave them "unawakened" for now. If things look bad, find them, tell them the truth, and let them fight hard for the evil team!
characters.creator: Taiyi

customBoxes.title: Reminder Tokens
customBoxes.content:
[[Twinflower" ×2]]
Placed when: While preparing for the first night.
Condition: After collecting all players' character tokens into the Grimoire, place them by the character tokens of two Townsfolk sitting next to each other.
Removed when: The Twinflowers leave play.

customBoxes.title: Design Notes
customBoxes.content:
Similar to the Doll — a subspecies of the Marionette evolving in another direction.

The +1 Minion design effectively compensates for strength. The must-be-Townsfolk and mutually-neighboring design frames the scope, avoiding a situation where anyone could be a Twinflower.

Must be Townsfolk and must neighbor each other — could it happen at certain player counts that random dealing leaves no two Townsfolk eligible to be Twinflowers? No — unless there are +3 or +4 Outsiders. Don't believe it? Take the Grimoire and enumerate it yourself.

characters.name: Daruma
characters.ability: Players who answer your question might die. If you answer another's question, you might die. You cannot die for other reasons.
characters.lede: Those who engage with Daruma meet misfortune.
characters.quote: Is everyone here? What are you all doing? What day is it today? What secrets hide in this room? Won't anyone talk with me? Would one more word hurt? Would speaking it aloud bring calamity? Can't I just ask casually?
summaryBullets: Only when the Storyteller hears a player answer Daruma's question, or hears Daruma answer another player's question, can Daruma's ability cause a death.
Whether Daruma's ability causes a death is up to the Storyteller. Answering one question might cause a death; answering many questions might kill nobody.
Daruma cannot die from execution or other players' abilities.
Daruma asking and answering his own questions doesn't trigger his ability.
If multiple players answer Daruma's question, the Storyteller decides which of them die — or that nobody dies.
Generally, causing one death per day is reasonable. In rare cases, two deaths in a day is acceptable.
Daruma's killing ability works both day and night.
If you're going to cause a death with Daruma's ability, do it immediately after the player answers the question.
howToRun: At any time, when you hear a player answer Daruma's question, you may kill that player immediately.
At any time, when you hear Daruma answer another player's question, you may kill Daruma immediately.

Daruma cannot die from any cause other than his own ability. If a sober Daruma is about to die due to an ability other than his own, he stays alive. If a sober Daruma is executed, announce that he is executed but remains alive.
examples: On the first day, Daruma asks the Noble: "What is your character?" The Noble answers the question — the Noble dies.
On the first day, Daruma is executed — but Daruma doesn't die.
On the second night, Daruma asks publicly: "What day is it now?" The Fortune Teller answers the question — the Fortune Teller dies.
On the third day, the Saint asks Daruma: "Was that takeout at the door ordered by you?" Daruma answers the question — Daruma dies.
tips: If you're Daruma, you can start asking questions from day one — ask like crazy! As long as people keep engaging with you, you can keep causing deaths. Do everything you can to make other players respond to you.
If you're Daruma, you can keep your character hidden and suddenly strike in the mid-to-late game, causing multiple players' deaths.

If you're Daruma, once you're exposed as Daruma, other players will avoid talking with you as much as possible. At that point you need to act more natural — casually, offhandedly asking everyday, simple questions often lands the kill more easily.
If you're Daruma, don't answer other players' questions! That's the only way to kill you.
If you're Daruma, deliberately answering other players' questions to seek death in the mid-to-late game may help you win faster.
If you're a good player, don't answer Daruma's questions — don't engage with him! At least once you know he's Daruma.
If you're a good player and clever enough, you can bait Daruma into answering your question — it may be tricky, but it's the only way to get rid of this nuisance for good!
characters.creator: Taiyi

customBoxes.title: Reminder Tokens
customBoxes.content:
[[Dead]]
Placed when: When Daruma causes a death.
Condition: When Daruma kills a player, place it by the killed player's character token.
Removed when: Daruma dies or leaves play.

customBoxes.title: Design Notes
customBoxes.content:
An entertainment Minion.

A "creative" design some players love.

Why design it as immediate death instead of death that night? Night death would fit more scripts, but an entertainment Minion pursues instant-feedback fun. Immediate death delivers a strong dramatic effect that night death can't match.

characters.name: Slaanesh
characters.ability: Each night*, choose a player: they die. You may let them learn you are Slaanesh. The last to learn shares your win condition, even if dead.
characters.lede: Slaanesh can charm the players he kills.
characters.quote: Kneel — not to beg for mercy, but to receive. I am the part of your dreams you dare not wake into. With every step I take toward you, a gorgeous flower blooms from the ground — watered with pleasure, rooted in desire, their fragrance making you forget everything. You call this 'depravity'? How laughable. Come, give me your hand. Let me tell you — restraint is a lie, discipline a shackle; only indulgence is the perfect home for this flesh of yours.
summaryBullets: Slaanesh can only charm when he killed a player. If Slaanesh attacked a player but caused no death, the charm ability can't trigger.
Slaanesh attacking an already-dead player cannot trigger the charm ability.
Every charmed player immediately learns who Slaanesh is.
Only the most recently charmed player's win condition matches Slaanesh's.
A charmed player cannot learn whether their win condition has changed — they must judge for themselves.
Slaanesh's ability cannot choose Traveller players (the Traveller Exclusion Principle).
howToRun: Each night except the first, wake Slaanesh. Have Slaanesh point to any player. The chosen player dies. If that player can be killed by Slaanesh, ask Slaanesh whether to charm. If Slaanesh nods to charm, place the "Dead" reminder by that player's character token, and move the "Charm" reminder to that player's character token. Wake that player, show them Slaanesh's character token, then point to the Slaanesh player, then put that player back to sleep. If Slaanesh shakes his head to decline charming, only place the "Dead" reminder by that player's character token.

The win condition of the most recent player to learn who Slaanesh is (the player marked with "Charm") always matches Slaanesh's. If Slaanesh wins, announce that player also wins. If Slaanesh loses, announce that player also loses — even if Slaanesh is already dead.
examples: On the second night, Slaanesh kills and charms the Fortune Teller; the Fortune Teller learns who Slaanesh is. Slaanesh charms no other player afterward. The game ends — the evil team wins, and the Fortune Teller also wins.

On the second night, Slaanesh kills and charms the Fortune Teller; the Fortune Teller learns who Slaanesh is. Slaanesh charms no other player afterward. The game ends — the good team wins, and the Fortune Teller loses.

On the second night, Slaanesh kills and charms the Fortune Teller; the Fortune Teller learns who Slaanesh is. On the third night, Slaanesh kills and charms the Saint; the Saint learns who Slaanesh is. On the fourth night, Slaanesh kills and charms the Exorcist; the Exorcist learns who Slaanesh is. Slaanesh charms no other player afterward. The game ends — the evil team wins, and the Exorcist also wins.
tips: If you're Slaanesh, you can charm the players you kill early in the game — this quickly wins you more "help". But as the game progresses, previously charmed players may sense something's off from the one-sided situation — they'll easily realize you've betrayed them. If they become sure you've charmed another player, they may step forward and identify you as Slaanesh — extremely bad for you.
If you're Slaanesh, you can charm the players you kill in the mid-to-late game — they'll serve you more loyally, because you're less likely to charm other players afterward.
If you're Slaanesh, you can charm just one player, or charm multiple players. More charms mean more payoff — and more risk!
If you're a good player, remember: good players who didn't die at night definitely can't be charmed by Slaanesh — they're trustworthy.

If you're a good player, judge whether players who died at night have been charmed by observing their behavior! If multiple dead players act strangely, hesitating or flip-flopping their stances, they've very likely been charmed by Slaanesh!

If you're a good player and you learn who Slaanesh is — that means you've been charmed by Slaanesh! Don't immediately reveal who Slaanesh is, because until Slaanesh charms a new player, your fates are bound together. If you discover a new player has been charmed, don't hesitate — immediately reveal who Slaanesh is and try to execute him.

customBoxes.title: Reminder Tokens
customBoxes.content:
[[Dead]]
Placed when: After Slaanesh chooses a player.
Condition: If the player Slaanesh chose is currently alive and can be killed by Slaanesh, place it by that player's character token.
Removed when: After announcing the dead player at dawn; the Storyteller may remove it at their convenience.

[[Charm]]
Placed when: After Slaanesh chooses to charm.
Condition: If Slaanesh killed a player and chooses to charm, place it by that dead player's character token.
Removed when: Slaanesh charms a new player, or Slaanesh leaves play.

customBoxes.title: Design Notes
customBoxes.content:
A special evil-converting Demon.

Only one player is actually "turned", yet multiple good players may serve evil.

Risk matches payoff. If Slaanesh charms only one player, it's nearly the standard conversion model. If Slaanesh charms multiple players, the payoff grows greatly — but once one player wakes up to it, there's the huge risk of directly exposing the Demon.

Good players who didn't die at night definitely can't be charmed — limiting the ability's scope and avoiding an overly broad "anyone could be" logic.

Exposure works both ways — as a punishment exposing the Demon, and as a tool for the evil team: Minions can fake being charmed to frame and attack other good players.
